documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.bots.<name>.passwordFile
documents.content: Path to a file containing the password. The file must be readable by the archisteamfarm user/group. Omit or set to null to provide the password a different way, such as through the web-ui.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.bots.<name>.settings
documents.content: Additional settings that are documented here.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.bots.<name>.username
documents.content: Name of the user to log in. Default is attribute name.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.dataDir
documents.content: The ASF home directory used to store all data. If left as the default value this directory will automatically be created before the ASF server starts, otherwise the sysadmin is responsible for ensuring the directory exists with appropriate ownership and permissions.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.enable
documents.content: If enabled, starts the ArchisSteamFarm service. For configuring the SteamGuard token you will need to use the web-ui, which is enabled by default over on 127.0.0.1:1242. You cannot configure ASF in any way outside of nix, since all the config files get wiped on restart and replaced with the programnatically set ones by nix.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.ipcPasswordFile
documents.content: Path to a file containing the password. The file must be readable by the archisteamfarm user/group.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.ipcSettings
documents.content: Settings to write to IPC.config. All options can be found here.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.package
documents.content: The archisteamfarm package to use. ::: {.warning} Should always be the latest version, for security reasons, since this module uses very new features and to not get out of sync with the Steam API. :::

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.settings
documents.content: The ASF.json file, all the options are documented here. Do note that AutoRestart and UpdateChannel is always to false respectively 0 because NixOS takes care of updating everything. Headless is also always set to true because there is no way to provide inputs via a systemd service. You should try to keep ASF up to date since upstream does not provide support for anything but the latest version and you're exposing yourself to all kinds of issues - as is outlined here.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.web-ui
documents.content: The Web-UI hosted on 127.0.0.1:1242.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.web-ui.enable
documents.content: Whether to start the web-ui. This is the preferred way of configuring things such as the steam guard token.

documents.title: Option: services.archisteamfarm.web-ui.package
documents.content: The ui package to use. ::: {.note} Contents must be in lib/dist :::

documents.title: Option: services.aria2.downloadDirPermission
documents.content:
The permission for settings.dir.
The default is 0770, which denies access for users not in the aria2 group.
You may want to adjust serviceUMask as well, which further restricts the file permission for newly created files (i.e. the downloads).

documents.title: Option: services.aria2.enable
documents.content:
Whether or not to enable the headless Aria2 daemon service.
Aria2 daemon can be controlled via the RPC interface using one of many WebUIs (http://localhost:6800/ by default).
Targets are downloaded to /var/lib/aria2/Downloads by default and are accessible to users in the aria2 group.

documents.title: Option: services.aria2.openPorts
documents.content: Open listen and RPC ports found in settings.listen-port and settings.rpc-listen-port options in the firewall.

documents.title: Option: services.aria2.rpcSecretFile
documents.content: A file containing the RPC secret authorization token. Read https://aria2.github.io/manual/en/html/aria2c.html#rpc-auth to know how this option value is used.

documents.title: Option: services.aria2.serviceUMask
documents.content:
The file mode creation mask for Aria2 service.
The default is 0022 for compatibility reason, as this is the default used by systemd. However, this results in file permission 0644 for new files, and denies aria2 group member from modifying the file.
You may want to set this value to 0002 so you can manage the file more easily.

documents.title: Option: services.aria2.settings

documents.title: Option: services.athens.downloadMode
documents.content:
Defines how Athens behaves when a module@version is not found in storage. There are 7 options:
"sync": download the module synchronously and return the results to the client.
"async": return 404, but asynchronously store the module in the storage backend.
"redirect": return a 301 redirect status to the client with the base URL as the DownloadRedirectURL from below.
"async_redirect": same as option number 3 but it will asynchronously store the module to the backend.
"none": return 404 if a module is not found and do nothing.
"file:": will point to an HCL file that specifies any of the 5 options above based on different import paths.
"custom:" is the same as option 6 but the file is fully encoded in the option. This is useful for using an environment variable in serverless deployments.

documents.title: Option: services.athens.networkMode
documents.content:
Configures how Athens will return the results of the /list endpoint as it can be assembled from both its own storage and the upstream VCS.
Note, that for better error messaging, this would also affect how other endpoints behave.
Modes:
strict: merge VCS versions with storage versions, but fail if either of them fails.
offline: only get storage versions, never reach out to VCS.
fallback: only return storage versions, if VCS fails. Note this means that you may see inconsistent results since fallback mode does a best effort of giving you what's available at the time of requesting versions.

documents.content:
Mode in which to run the server.
'monolithic' runs all components, and is suitable for single-node deployments.
'api-server' runs only the API server, and is suitable for clustering.
'garbage-collector' only runs the garbage collector periodically.
A simple NixOS-based Attic deployment will typically have one 'monolithic' and any number of 'api-server' nodes.
There are several other supported modes that perform one-off operations, but these are the only ones that make sense to run via the NixOS module.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-dir.tls.require
documents.content:

If TLS is not required while TLS or TLS-PSK are enabled, then the Bacula component will connect with other components either with or without TLS or TLS-PSK
If services.bacula-dir.tls.enable or TLS-PSK is enabled and TLS is required, then the Bacula component will refuse any connection request that does not use TLS.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-dir.tls.verifyPeer
documents.content:

Additionally, the client's X509 certificate Common Name must meet the value of the Address directive. If services.bacula-dir.tls.allowedCN is used, the client's x509 certificate Common Name must also correspond to one of the CN specified in the services.bacula-dir.tls.allowedCN directive. This directive is valid only for a server and not in client context.

If you have either /dev/random or bc on your machine, Bacula will generate a random password during the configuration process, otherwise it will be left blank and you must manually supply it.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.autochanger
documents.content: This option defines Autochanger resources in Bacula Storage Daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.autochanger.<name>.changerCommand
documents.content:
The name-string specifies an external program to be called that will automatically change volumes as required by Bacula. Normally, this directive will be specified only in the AutoChanger resource, which is then used for all devices. However, you may also specify the different Changer Command in each Device resource. Most frequently, you will specify the Bacula supplied mtx-changer script as follows:
"/path/mtx-changer %c %o %S %a %d"
and you will install the mtx on your system (found in the depkgs release). An example of this command is in the default bacula-sd.conf file. For more details on the substitution characters that may be specified to configure your autochanger please see the AutochangersAutochangersChapter chapter of this manual. For FreeBSD users, you might want to see one of the several chio scripts in examples/autochangers.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.autochanger.<name>.changerDevice
documents.content: The specified name-string must be the generic SCSI device name of the autochanger that corresponds to the normal read/write Archive Device specified in the Device resource. This generic SCSI device name should be specified if you have an autochanger or if you have a standard tape drive and want to use the Alert Command (see below). For example, on Linux systems, for an Archive Device name of /dev/nst0, you would specify /dev/sg0 for the Changer Device name. Depending on your exact configuration, and the number of autochangers or the type of autochanger, what you specify here can vary. This directive is optional. See the Using AutochangersAutochangersChapter chapter of this manual for more details of using this and the following autochanger directives.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.device
documents.content: This option defines Device resources in Bacula Storage Daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.device.<name>.archiveDevice
documents.content: The specified name-string gives the system file name of the storage device managed by this storage daemon. This will usually be the device file name of a removable storage device (tape drive), for example /dev/nst0 or /dev/rmt/0mbn. For a DVD-writer, it will be for example /dev/hdc. It may also be a directory name if you are archiving to disk storage. In this case, you must supply the full absolute path to the directory. When specifying a tape device, it is preferable that the "non-rewind" variant of the device file name be given.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.device.<name>.extraDeviceConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration to be passed in Device directive.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.device.<name>.mediaType
documents.content:
The specified name-string names the type of media supported by this device, for example, DLT7000. Media type names are arbitrary in that you set them to anything you want, but they must be known to the volume database to keep track of which storage daemons can read which volumes. In general, each different storage type should have a unique Media Type associated with it. The same name-string must appear in the appropriate Storage resource definition in the Director's configuration file.
Even though the names you assign are arbitrary (i.e. you choose the name you want), you should take care in specifying them because the Media Type is used to determine which storage device Bacula will select during restore. Thus you should probably use the same Media Type specification for all drives where the Media can be freely interchanged. This is not generally an issue if you have a single Storage daemon, but it is with multiple Storage daemons, especially if they have incompatible media.
For example, if you specify a Media Type of DDS-4 then during the restore, Bacula will be able to choose any Storage Daemon that handles DDS-4. If you have an autochanger, you might want to name the Media Type in a way that is unique to the autochanger, unless you wish to possibly use the Volumes in other drives. You should also ensure to have unique Media Type names if the Media is not compatible between drives. This specification is required for all devices.
In addition, if you are using disk storage, each Device resource will generally have a different mount point or directory. In order for Bacula to select the correct Device resource, each one must have a unique Media Type.

documents.content: This option defines Director resources in Bacula Storage Daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.director.<name>.monitor
documents.content:
If Monitor is set to no, this director will have full access to this Storage daemon. If Monitor is set to yes, this director will only be able to fetch the current status of this Storage daemon.
Please note that if this director is being used by a Monitor, we highly recommend to set this directive to yes to avoid serious security problems.

documents.title: Option: services.bacula-sd.director.<name>.password
documents.content:
Specifies the password that must be supplied for the default Bacula Console to be authorized. The same password must appear in the Director resource of the Console configuration file. For added security, the password is never passed across the network but instead a challenge response hash code created with the password. This directive is required. If you have either /dev/random or bc on your machine, Bacula will generate a random password during the configuration process, otherwise it will be left blank and you must manually supply it.
The password is plain text. It is not generated through any special process but as noted above, it is better to use random text for security reasons.

documents.title: Option: services.beesd.filesystems.<name>.hashTableSizeMB
documents.content:
Hash table size in MB; must be a multiple of 16.
A larger ratio of index size to storage size means smaller blocks of duplicate content are recognized.
If you have 1TB of data, a 4GB hash table (which is to say, a value of 4096) will permit 4KB extents (the smallest possible size) to be recognized, whereas a value of 1024 -- creating a 1GB hash table -- will recognize only aligned duplicate blocks of 16KB.

Note that deduplication crosses subvolumes; one must not configure multiple instances for subvolumes of the same filesystem (or block devices which are part of the same filesystem), but only for completely independent btrfs filesystems.
This must be in a format usable by findmnt; that could be a key=value pair, or a bare path to a mount point. Using bare paths will allow systemd to start the beesd service only after mounting the associated path.

documents.title: Option: services.boinc.allowRemoteGuiRpc
documents.content:
If set to true, any remote host can connect to and control this BOINC client (subject to password authentication). If instead set to false, only the hosts listed in {var}dataDir/remote_hosts.cfg will be allowed to connect.
See also: https://boinc.berkeley.edu/wiki/Controlling_BOINC_remotely#Remote_access

documents.title: Option: services.boinc.dataDir
documents.content: The directory in which to store BOINC's configuration and data files.

documents.title: Option: services.boinc.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the BOINC distributed computing client. If this option is set to true, the boinc_client daemon will be run as a background service. The boinccmd command can be used to control the daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.boinc.extraEnvPackages
documents.content:
Additional packages to make available in the environment in which BOINC will run. Common choices are:
{var}pkgs.virtualbox: The VirtualBox virtual machine framework. Required by some BOINC projects, such as ATLAS@home.
{var}pkgs.ocl-icd: OpenCL infrastructure library. Required by BOINC projects that use OpenCL, in addition to a device-specific OpenCL driver.
{var}pkgs.linuxPackages.nvidia_x11: Provides CUDA libraries. Required by BOINC projects that use CUDA. Note that this requires an NVIDIA graphics device to be present on the system.
Also provides OpenCL drivers for NVIDIA GPUs; {var}pkgs.ocl-icd is also needed in this case.

documents.title: Option: services.boinc.package
documents.content: The boinc package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.configFile
documents.content: Path to a .json file specifying the state transitions. You don't need to set this unless you prefer to provide the json file yourself instead of using the settings option.

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable bonsaid.

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.extraFlags
documents.content: Extra flags to pass to bonsaid, such as [ "-v" ] to enable verbose logging.

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.package
documents.content: The bonsai package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.settings
documents.content: State transition definitions. See the upstream README for extended documentation and a more complete example.

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.settings.*.command
documents.content:
Command to run when this transition is taken. This is executed inline by bonsaid and blocks handling of any other events until completion. To perform the command asynchronously, specify it like [ "setsid" "-f" "my-command" ].
Only effects transitions with type = "exec".

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.settings.*.delay_duration
documents.content:
Nanoseconds to wait after the previous state change before performing this transition. This can be placed at the same level as a type = "event" transition to achieve a timeout mechanism.
Only effects transitions with type = "delay".

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.settings.*.event_name
documents.content:
Name of the event which should trigger this transition when received by bonsaid. Events are sent to bonsaid by running bonsaictl -e <event_name>.
Only effects transitions with type = "event".

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.settings.*.transitions
documents.content: List of transitions out of this state. If left empty, then this state is considered a terminal state and entering it will trigger an immediate transition back to the root state (after processing side effects).

documents.title: Option: services.bonsaid.settings.*.type
documents.content: Type of transition. Determines how bonsaid interprets the other options in this transition.

documents.content: The hostname to serve BookStack on.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.maxUploadSize
documents.content: The maximum size for uploads (e.g. images).

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx
documents.content: With this option, you can customize the nginx virtualHost settings.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
documents.content:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.
With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.acmeRoot
documents.content: Directory for the ACME challenge, which is public. Don't put certs or keys in here. Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.addSSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443).

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.default
documents.content: Makes this vhost the default.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.enableACME
documents.content: Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost. Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}useACMEHost.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.forceSSL
documents.content: Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) all plain HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.globalRedirect
documents.content: If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) to the given hostname.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol. Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given IP address / port. If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.http3
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.http3_hq
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that special application protocol support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.kTLS
documents.content: Whether to enable kTLS support. Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel. Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listen
documents.content:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host. IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets. Note: this option overrides addSSL and onlySSL.
If you only want to set the addresses manually and not the ports, take a look at listenAddresses.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listen.*.addr
documents.content: Listen address.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listen.*.extraParameters
documents.content: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listen.*.port
documents.content: Port number to listen on. If unset and the listen address is not a socket then nginx defaults to 80.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listen.*.proxyProtocol
documents.content: Enable PROXY protocol.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listen.*.ssl
documents.content: Enable SSL.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.listenAddresses
documents.content:

Note: This option overrides networking.enableIPv6

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.basicAuthFile

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.index

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.priority
documents.content: Order of this location block in relation to the others in the vhost. The semantics are the same as with lib.mkOrder. Smaller values have a greater priority.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.proxyPass
documents.content: Adds proxy_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedProxySettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.proxyWebsockets
documents.content: Whether to support proxying websocket connections with HTTP/1.1.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.recommendedProxySettings
documents.content: Enable recommended proxy settings.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.recommendedUwsgiSettings
documents.content: Enable recommended uwsgi settings.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.return
documents.content: Adds a return directive, for e.g. redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.root
documents.content: Root directory for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.tryFiles
documents.content: Adds try_files directive.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.locations.<name>.uwsgiPass
documents.content: Adds uwsgi_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedUwsgiSettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.onlySSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS and reject plain HTTP connections. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on port 443.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.quic
documents.content: Whether to enable the QUIC transport protocol. Note that QUIC support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.redirectCode
documents.content: HTTP status used by globalRedirect and forceSSL. Possible usecases include temporary (302, 307) redirects, keeping the request method and body (307, 308), or explicitly resetting the method to GET (303). See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.rejectSSL
documents.content: Whether to listen for and reject all HTTPS connections to this vhost. Useful in default server blocks to avoid serving the certificate for another vhost. Uses the ssl_reject_handshake directive available in nginx versions 1.19.4 and above.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.reuseport
documents.content: Create an individual listening socket . It is required to specify only once on one of the hosts.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.root
documents.content: The path of the web root directory.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.serverAliases
documents.content: Additional names of virtual hosts served by this virtual host configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.serverName
documents.content: Name of this virtual host. Defaults to attribute name in virtualHosts.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.sslCertificate
documents.content: Path to server SSL certificate.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.sslCertificateKey
documents.content: Path to server SSL certificate key.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.sslTrustedCertificate
documents.content: Path to root SSL certificate for stapling and client certificates.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.nginx.useACMEHost
documents.content: A host of an existing Let's Encrypt certificate to use. This is useful if you have many subdomains and want to avoid hitting the rate limit. Alternately, you can generate a certificate through {option}enableACME. Note that this option does not create any certificates, nor it does add subdomains to existing ones – you will need to create them manually using .

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.package
documents.content: The bookstack package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.poolConfig
documents.content: Options for the Bookstack PHP pool. See the documentation on php-fpm.conf for details on configuration directives.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.settings
documents.content: Options for Bookstack configuration. Refer to https://github.com/BookStackApp/BookStack/blob/development/.env.example for details on supported values. For passing secrets, append "_FILE" to the setting name. For example, you may create a file /var/secrets/db_pass.txt and set services.bookstack.settings.DB_PASSWORD_FILE to /var/secrets/db_pass.txt instead of providing a plaintext password using services.bookstack.settings.DB_PASSWORD.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.settings.APP_KEY_FILE
documents.content: The path to your appkey. The file should contain a 32 character random app key. This may be set using echo "base64:$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64)" > /path/to/key-file.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.settings.APP_URL
documents.content: The root URL that you want to host BookStack on. All URLs in BookStack will be generated using this value. It is used to validate specific requests and to generate URLs in emails.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.settings.DB_HOST
documents.content: The IP or hostname which hosts your database.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.settings.DB_PASSWORD_FILE
documents.content: The file containing your mysql/mariadb database password.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.settings.DB_PORT
documents.content: The port your database is listening at.

documents.title: Option: services.bookstack.user
documents.content: User bookstack runs as

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs
documents.content: Deduplicating backups using BorgBackup. Adding a job will cause a borg-job-NAME wrapper to be added to your system path, so that you can perform maintenance easily. See also the chapter about BorgBackup in the NixOS manual.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.appendFailedSuffix
documents.content: Append a .failed suffix to the archive name, which is only removed if {command}borg create has a zero exit status.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.archiveBaseName
documents.content: How to name the created archives. A timestamp, whose format is determined by {option}dateFormat, will be appended. The full name can be modified at runtime ($archiveName). Placeholders like {hostname} must not be used. Use null for no base name.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.compression
documents.content: Compression method to use. Refer to {command}borg help compression for all available options.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.createCommand
documents.content:
Borg command to use for archive creation. The default (create) creates a regular Borg archive.
Use import-tar to instead read a tar archive stream from {option}dumpCommand output and import its contents into the repository.
import-tar can not be used together with {option}exclude or {option}patterns.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.dateFormat
documents.content: Arguments passed to {command}date to create a timestamp suffix for the archive name.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.doInit
documents.content: Run {command}borg init if the specified {option}repo does not exist. You should set this to false if the repository is located on an external drive that might not always be mounted.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.dumpCommand
documents.content: Backup the stdout of this program instead of filesystem paths. Mutually exclusive with {option}paths.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.encryption.mode
documents.content: Encryption mode to use. Setting a mode other than "none" requires you to specify a {option}passCommand or a {option}passphrase.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.encryption.passCommand
documents.content: A command which prints the passphrase to stdout. Mutually exclusive with {option}passphrase.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.encryption.passphrase
documents.content: The passphrase the backups are encrypted with. Mutually exclusive with {option}passCommand. If you do not want the passphrase to be stored in the world-readable Nix store, use {option}passCommand.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.environment
documents.content: Environment variables passed to the backup script. You can for example specify which SSH key to use.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.exclude
documents.content:
Exclude paths matching any of the given patterns. See {command}borg help patterns for pattern syntax.
Can not be set when {option}createCommand is set to import-tar.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.extraArgs
documents.content:
Additional arguments for all {command}borg calls the service has. Handle with care.
These extra arguments also get included in the wrapper script for this job.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.extraCompactArgs
documents.content: Additional arguments for {command}borg compact. Can also be set at runtime using $extraCompactArgs.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.extraCreateArgs
documents.content: Additional arguments for {command}borg create. Can also be set at runtime using $extraCreateArgs.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.extraInitArgs
documents.content: Additional arguments for {command}borg init. Can also be set at runtime using $extraInitArgs.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.extraPruneArgs
documents.content: Additional arguments for {command}borg prune. Can also be set at runtime using $extraPruneArgs.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.failOnWarnings
documents.content: Fail the whole backup job if any borg command returns a warning (exit code 1), for example because a file changed during backup.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.group
documents.content: The group borg is run as. User or group needs read permission for the specified {option}paths.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.inhibitsSleep
documents.content: Prevents the system from sleeping while backing up.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.paths
documents.content: Path(s) to back up. Mutually exclusive with {option}dumpCommand.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.patterns
documents.content:
Include/exclude paths matching the given patterns. The first matching patterns is used, so if an include pattern (prefix +) matches before an exclude pattern (prefix -), the file is backed up. See {command}borg help patterns for pattern syntax.
Can not be set when {option}createCommand is set to import-tar.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.persistentTimer
documents.content: Set the Persistent option for the {manpage}systemd.timer(5) which triggers the backup immediately if the last trigger was missed (e.g. if the system was powered down).

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.postCreate
documents.content: Shell commands to run after {command}borg create. The name of the created archive is stored in $archiveName.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.postHook
documents.content: Shell commands to run just before exit. They are executed even if a previous command exits with a non-zero exit code. The latter is available as $exitStatus.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.postInit
documents.content: Shell commands to run after {command}borg init.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.postPrune
documents.content: Shell commands to run after {command}borg prune.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.preHook
documents.content: Shell commands to run before the backup. This can for example be used to mount file systems.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.privateTmp
documents.content: Set the PrivateTmp option for the systemd-service. Set to false if you need sockets or other files from global /tmp.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.prune.keep
documents.content: Prune a repository by deleting all archives not matching any of the specified retention options. See {command}borg help prune for the available options.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.prune.prefix
documents.content: Only consider archive names starting with this prefix for pruning. By default, only archives created by this job are considered. Use "" or null to consider all archives.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.readWritePaths
documents.content: By default, borg cannot write anywhere on the system but $HOME/.config/borg and $HOME/.cache/borg. If, for example, your preHook script needs to dump files somewhere, put those directories here.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.removableDevice
documents.content: Whether the repo (which must be local) is a removable device.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.repo
documents.content: Remote or local repository to back up to.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.startAt
documents.content: When or how often the backup should run. Must be in the format described in {manpage}systemd.time(7). If you do not want the backup to start automatically, use [ ]. It will generate a systemd service borgbackup-job-NAME. You may trigger it manually via systemctl restart borgbackup-job-NAME.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.user
documents.content: The user {command}borg is run as. User or group need read permission for the specified {option}paths.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.jobs.<name>.wrapper
documents.content: Name of the wrapper that is installed into {env}PATH. Set to null or "" to disable it altogether.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.package
documents.content: The borgbackup package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos
documents.content: Serve BorgBackup repositories to given public SSH keys, restricting their access to the repository only. See also the chapter about BorgBackup in the NixOS manual. Also, clients do not need to specify the absolute path when accessing the repository, i.e. user@machine:. is enough. (Note colon and dot.)

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.allowSubRepos
documents.content: Allow clients to create repositories in subdirectories of the specified {option}path. These can be accessed using user@machine:path/to/subrepo. Note that a {option}quota applies to repositories independently. Therefore, if this is enabled, clients can create multiple repositories and upload an arbitrary amount of data.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.authorizedKeys
documents.content: Public SSH keys that are given full write access to this repository. You should use a different SSH key for each repository you write to, because the specified keys are restricted to running {command}borg serve and can only access this single repository.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.authorizedKeysAppendOnly
documents.content: Public SSH keys that can only be used to append new data (archives) to the repository. Note that archives can still be marked as deleted and are subsequently removed from disk upon accessing the repo with full write access, e.g. when pruning.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.group
documents.content: The group {command}borg serve is run as. User or group needs write permission for the specified {option}path.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.path
documents.content: Where to store the backups. Note that the directory is created automatically, with correct permissions.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.quota
documents.content: Storage quota for the repository. This quota is ensured for all sub-repositories if {option}allowSubRepos is enabled but not for the overall storage space used.

documents.title: Option: services.borgbackup.repos.<name>.user
documents.content: The user {command}borg serve is run as. User or group needs write permission for the specified {option}path.

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.configurations
documents.content: Set of borgmatic configurations, see https://torsion.org/borgmatic/docs/reference/configuration/

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.configurations.<name>.repositories
documents.content: A required list of local or remote repositories with paths and optional labels (which can be used with the --repository flag to select a repository). Tildes are expanded. Multiple repositories are backed up to in sequence. Borg placeholders can be used. See the output of "borg help placeholders" for details. See ssh_command for SSH options like identity file or port. If systemd service is used, then add local repository paths in the systemd service file to the ReadWritePaths list.

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.configurations.<name>.repositories.*.label
documents.content: Label to the repository

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.configurations.<name>.repositories.*.path
documents.content: Path to the repository

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.configurations.<name>.source_directories
documents.content: List of source directories and files to backup. Globs and tildes are expanded. Do not backslash spaces in path names.

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable borgmatic.

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.enableConfigCheck
documents.content: Whether to enable checking all configurations during build time.

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.settings
documents.content: See https://torsion.org/borgmatic/docs/reference/configuration/

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.settings.repositories
documents.content: A required list of local or remote repositories with paths and optional labels (which can be used with the --repository flag to select a repository). Tildes are expanded. Multiple repositories are backed up to in sequence. Borg placeholders can be used. See the output of "borg help placeholders" for details. See ssh_command for SSH options like identity file or port. If systemd service is used, then add local repository paths in the systemd service file to the ReadWritePaths list.

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.settings.repositories.*.label
documents.content: Label to the repository

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.settings.repositories.*.path
documents.content: Path to the repository

documents.title: Option: services.borgmatic.settings.source_directories
documents.content: List of source directories and files to backup. Globs and tildes are expanded. Do not backslash spaces in path names.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.checkFrequency
documents.content: Bosun's check frequency

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable bosun.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.extraConfig
documents.content:
Extra configuration options for Bosun. You should describe your desired templates, alerts, macros, etc through this configuration option.
A detailed description of the supported syntax can be found at-spi2-atk https://bosun.org/configuration.html

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.group
documents.content: Group account under which bosun runs.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.influxHost
documents.content: Host and port of the influxdb database.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.ledisDir
documents.content: Path to bosun's ledis data dir

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.listenAddress
documents.content: The host address and port that bosun's web interface will listen on.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.opentsdbHost
documents.content: Host and port of the OpenTSDB database that stores bosun data. To disable opentsdb you can pass null as parameter.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.package
documents.content: The bosun package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.stateFile
documents.content: Path to bosun's state file.

documents.title: Option: services.bosun.user
documents.content: User account under which bosun runs.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable botamusique, a bot to play audio streams on mumble.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.package
documents.content: The botamusique package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.settings
documents.content: Your {file}configuration.ini as a Nix attribute set. Look up possible options in the configuration.example.ini.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.settings.bot.comment
documents.content: Comment displayed for the bot.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.settings.bot.username
documents.content: Name the bot should appear with.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.settings.server.host
documents.content: Hostname of the mumble server to connect to.

documents.title: Option: services.botamusique.settings.server.port
documents.content: Port of the mumble server to connect to.

documents.title: Option: services.bpftune.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable bpftune BPF driven auto-tuning.

documents.title: Option: services.bpftune.package
documents.content: The bpftune package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.brltty.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the BRLTTY daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Broadcast Box.

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to enable opening WebRTC traffic ports in the firewall. Randomly selected ports will not be opened. .

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.package
documents.content: The broadcast-box package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.settings
documents.content:
Attribute set of environment variables.
https://github.com/Glimesh/broadcast-box#environment-variables
:::{.warning} The status API exposes stream keys so {env}DISABLE_STATUS is enabled by default. :::

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.web.host
documents.content: Host address the HTTP server listens on. By default the server listens on all interfaces.

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.web.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to enable opening the HTTP server port and, if enabled, the HTTPS redirect server port in the firewall. .

documents.title: Option: services.broadcast-box.web.port
documents.content: Port the HTTP server listens on.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.extraPackages
documents.content:
Extra packages for btrbk, like compression utilities for stream_compress.
Note: This option will get deprecated in future releases. Required compression programs will get automatically provided to btrbk depending on configured compression method in services.btrbk.instances.<name>.settings option.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.instances
documents.content: Set of btrbk instances. The instance named btrbk is the default one.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.instances.<name>.onCalendar
documents.content: How often this btrbk instance is started. See {manpage}systemd.time(7) for more information about the format. Setting it to null disables the timer, thus this instance can only be started manually.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.instances.<name>.settings
documents.content: configuration options for btrbk. Nested attrsets translate to subsections.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.instances.<name>.settings.stream_compress
documents.content: Compress the btrfs send stream before transferring it from/to remote locations using a compression command.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.instances.<name>.snapshotOnly
documents.content: Whether to run in snapshot only mode. This skips backup creation and deletion steps. Useful when you want to manually backup to an external drive that might not always be connected. Use btrbk -c /path/to/conf resume to trigger manual backups. More examples here. See also snapshot subcommand in {manpage}btrbk(1).

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.ioSchedulingClass
documents.content: IO scheduling class for btrbk (see {manpage}ionice(1) for a quick description). Applies to local instances, and remote ones connecting by ssh if set to idle.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.niceness
documents.content: Niceness for local instances of btrbk. Also applies to remote ones connecting via ssh when positive.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.sshAccess
documents.content: SSH keys that should be able to make or push snapshots on this system remotely with btrbk

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.sshAccess.*.extraArgs
documents.content: Additional arguments to pass to ssh_filter_btrbk

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.sshAccess.*.key
documents.content: SSH public key allowed to login as user btrbk to run remote backups.

documents.title: Option: services.btrbk.sshAccess.*.roles
documents.content: What actions can be performed with this SSH key. See ssh_filter_btrbk(1) for details

documents.title: Option: services.btrfs.autoScrub.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable regular btrfs scrub.

documents.title: Option: services.btrfs.autoScrub.fileSystems
documents.content: List of paths to btrfs filesystems to regularly call {command}btrfs scrub on. Defaults to all mount points with btrfs filesystems. Note that if you have filesystems that span multiple devices (e.g. RAID), you should take care to use the same device for any given mount point and let btrfs take care of automatically mounting the rest, in order to avoid scrubbing the same data multiple times.

documents.title: Option: services.btrfs.autoScrub.interval
documents.content: Systemd calendar expression for when to scrub btrfs filesystems. The recommended period is a month but could be less ({manpage}btrfs-scrub(8)). See {manpage}systemd.time(7) for more information on the syntax.

documents.title: Option: services.btrfs.autoScrub.limit
documents.content: The scrub throughput limit applied on all scrubbed filesystems. The value is bytes per second, and accepts the usual KMGT prefixes.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.configFile
documents.content:
Path to an INI format configuration file to provide Buffyboard. By default, this is generated from whatever you've set in settings. If specified manually, then settings is ignored.
For an example config file see here

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable buffyboard framebuffer keyboard (on-screen keyboard).

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.extraFlags
documents.content: Extra CLI arguments to pass to buffyboard.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.package
documents.content: The buffybox package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings
documents.content: Settings to include in /etc/buffyboard.conf. Every option here is strictly optional: Buffyboard will use its own baked-in defaults for those options left unset.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.input.pointer
documents.content: Enable or disable the use of a hardware mouse or other pointing device.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.input.touchscreen
documents.content: Enable or disable the use of the touchscreen.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.keyboard.haptic_feedback
documents.content: Enable or disable vibrations when pressing keys.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.keyboard.sticky_shift
documents.content: Changes shift key behavior. When true, the keyboard remains in uppercase mode until the shift key is pressed again (sticky). When false, the keyboard switches back to lowercase mode and the shift key deactivates after a non-modifier key is pressed.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.quirks.fbdev_force_refresh
documents.content: If true and using the framebuffer backend, this triggers a display refresh after every draw operation. This has a negative performance impact.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.quirks.ignore_unused_terminals
documents.content:
If true, buffyboard won't automatically update the layout of a new terminal and draw the keyboard, if the terminal is not opened by any process. In this case SIGUSR1 should be sent to buffyboard to update the layout. This quirk was introduced to resolve a race between buffyboard and systemd-logind according to the following scenario:
A user switches to a new virtual terminal
Buffyboard opens the terminal and changes the number of rows
systemd-logind sees that the terminal is opened by some other process and don't start getty@.service

The race is resolved by enabling this option and installing a drop-in file for getty@.service that sends SIGUSR1 to buffyboard.

documents.title: Option: services.buffyboard.settings.theme.default
documents.content: Selects the default theme on boot. Can be changed at runtime to the alternative theme.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.buildbotDir
documents.content: Specifies the Buildbot directory.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.buildbotUrl

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.builders
documents.content: List of Builders.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.changeSource
documents.content: List of Change Sources.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.configurators
documents.content: Configurator Steps, see https://docs.buildbot.net/latest/manual/configuration/configurators.html

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.dbUrl
documents.content: Specifies the database connection string.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the Buildbot continuous integration server.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.extraConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration to append to master.cfg

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.extraGroups
documents.content: List of extra groups that the buildbot user should be a part of.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.extraImports

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.factorySteps
documents.content: Factory Steps

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.group

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.home
documents.content: Buildbot home directory.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.listenAddress
documents.content: Specifies the bind address on which the buildbot HTTP interface listens.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.masterCfg
documents.content: Optionally pass master.cfg path. Other options in this configuration will be ignored.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.package
documents.content: The buildbot-full package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.packages
documents.content: Packages to add to PATH for the buildbot process.

documents.title: Option: services.buildbot-master.pbPort
documents.content: The buildmaster will listen on a TCP port of your choosing for connections from workers. It can also use this port for connections from remote Change Sources, status clients, and debug tools. This port should be visible to the outside world, and you’ll need to tell your worker admins about your choice. documents.title: Option: services.cassandra.heapNewSize
documents.content:
Must be left blank or set together with {option}heapNewSize. If left blank a sensible value for the available amount of RAM and CPU cores is calculated.
Override to set the amount of memory to allocate to the JVM at start-up. For production use you may wish to adjust this for your environment. HEAP_NEWSIZE refers to the size of the young generation.
The main trade-off for the young generation is that the larger it is, the longer GC pause times will be. The shorter it is, the more expensive GC will be (usually).
The example HEAP_NEWSIZE assumes a modern 8-core+ machine for decent pause times. If in doubt, and if you do not particularly want to tweak, go with 100 MB per physical CPU core.

documents.title: Option: services.cassandra.listenAddress
documents.content:
Address or interface to bind to and tell other Cassandra nodes to connect to. You must change this if you want multiple nodes to be able to communicate!
Set {option}listenAddress OR {option}listenInterface, not both.
Leaving it blank leaves it up to InetAddress.getLocalHost(). This will always do the "Right Thing" if the node is properly configured (hostname, name resolution, etc), and the Right Thing is to use the address associated with the hostname (it might not be).

documents.title: Option: services.cassandra.maxHeapSize
documents.content:
Must be left blank or set together with {option}heapNewSize. If left blank a sensible value for the available amount of RAM and CPU cores is calculated.
Override to set the amount of memory to allocate to the JVM at start-up. For production use you may wish to adjust this for your environment. MAX_HEAP_SIZE is the total amount of memory dedicated to the Java heap. HEAP_NEWSIZE refers to the size of the young generation.
The main trade-off for the young generation is that the larger it is, the longer GC pause times will be. The shorter it is, the more expensive GC will be (usually).

documents.title: Option: services.cloud-init.enable
documents.content:
Enable the cloud-init service. This services reads configuration metadata in a cloud environment and configures the machine according to this metadata.
This configuration is not completely compatible with the NixOS way of doing configuration, as configuration done by cloud-init might be overridden by a subsequent nixos-rebuild call. However, some parts of cloud-init fall outside of NixOS's responsibility, like filesystem resizing and ssh public key provisioning, and cloud-init is useful for that parts. Thus, be wary that using cloud-init in NixOS might come as some cost.

documents.title: Option: services.cloudflared.tunnels.<name>.edgeIPVersion
documents.content:
Specifies the IP address version (IPv4 or IPv6) used to establish a connection between cloudflared and the Cloudflare global network.
The value auto relies on the host operating system to determine which IP version to select. The first IP version returned from the DNS resolution of the region lookup will be used as the primary set. In dual IPv6 and IPv4 network setups, cloudflared will separate the IP versions into two address sets that will be used to fallback in connectivity failure scenarios.
See Tunnel run parameters.

documents.content:
A list of NTLM/NTLMv2 authenticating HTTP proxies.
Parent proxy, which requires authentication. The same as proxy on the command-line, can be used more than once to specify unlimited number of proxies. Should one proxy fail, cntlm automatically moves on to the next one. The connect request fails only if the whole list of proxies is scanned and (for each request) and found to be invalid. Command-line takes precedence over the configuration file.

Relay address (the local IP address that will be used to relay the packets to the peer). Multiple relay addresses may be used. The same IP(s) can be used as both listening IP(s) and relay IP(s).
If no relay IP(s) specified, then the turnserver will apply the default policy: it will decide itself which relay addresses to be used, and it will always be using the client socket IP address as the relay IP address of the TURN session (if the requested relay address family is the same as the family of the client socket).

documents.title: Option: services.coturn.secure-stun
documents.content: Require authentication of the STUN Binding request. By default, the clients are allowed anonymous access to the STUN Binding functionality.

documents.title: Option: services.coturn.static-auth-secret
documents.content: 'Static' authentication secret value (a string) for TURN REST API only. If not set, then the turn server will try to use the 'dynamic' value in turn_secret table in user database (if present). The database-stored value can be changed on-the-fly by a separate program, so this is why that other mode is 'dynamic'.

documents.title: Option: services.coturn.static-auth-secret-file
documents.content: Path to the file containing the static authentication secret.

documents.title: Option: services.coturn.tls-listening-port
documents.content: TURN listener port for TLS. Note: actually, "plain" TCP and UDP sessions can connect to the TLS and DTLS port(s), too - if allowed by configuration. The TURN server "automatically" recognizes the type of traffic. Actually, two listening endpoints (the "plain" one and the "tls" one) are equivalent in terms of functionality; but we keep both endpoints to satisfy the RFC 5766 specs. For secure TCP connections, we currently support SSL version 3 and TLS version 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2. For secure UDP connections, we support DTLS version 1.

documents.title: Option: services.coturn.use-auth-secret
documents.content:
TURN REST API flag. Flag that sets a special authorization option that is based upon authentication secret. This feature can be used with the long-term authentication mechanism, only. This feature purpose is to support "TURN Server REST API", see "TURN REST API" link in the project's page https://github.com/coturn/coturn/
This option is used with timestamp:
usercombo -> "timestamp:userid" turn user -> usercombo turn password -> base64(hmac(secret key, usercombo))
This allows TURN credentials to be accounted for a specific user id. If you don't have a suitable id, the timestamp alone can be used. This option is just turning on secret-based authentication. The actual value of the secret is defined either by option static-auth-secret, or can be found in the turn_secret table in the database.

documents.content:

Note that this builds a static web app as opposed to running a full node server, unlike the default docker image.
Writing config changes to disk through the UI, triggering a rebuild through the UI and application status checks are unavailable without the node server; Everything else will work fine.
See the deployment docs for building from source, hosting with a CDN and CDN cloud deploy for more information. .

Note that the full configuration will be written to the nix store as world readable, which may include secrets such as password hashes.
To add files such as icons or backgrounds, you can reference them in line such as
This will add the file to the nix store upon build, referencing it by file path as expected by Dashy.

documents.title: Option: services.datadog-agent.checks
documents.content:
Configuration for all Datadog checks. Keys of this attribute set will be used as the name of the check to create the appropriate configuration in conf.d/$check.d/conf.yaml.
The configuration is converted into JSON from the plain Nix language configuration, meaning that you should write configuration adhering to Datadog's documentation - but in Nix language.
Refer to the implementation of this module (specifically the definition of defaultChecks) for an example.
Note: The 'disk' and 'network' check are configured in separate options because they exist by default. Attempting to override their configuration here will have no effect.

If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.dependency-track.oidc.teamSynchronization
documents.content: This option will ensure that team memberships for OpenID Connect users are dynamic and synchronized with membership of OpenID Connect groups or assigned roles. When a team is mapped to an OpenID Connect group, all local OpenID Connect users will automatically be assigned to the team if they are a member of the group the team is mapped to. If the user is later removed from the OpenID Connect group, they will also be removed from the team. This option provides the ability to dynamically control user permissions via the identity provider. Note that team synchronization is only performed during user provisioning and after successful authentication.

documents.title: Option: services.dependency-track.oidc.teams.claim
documents.content: Defines the name of the claim that contains group memberships or role assignments in the provider's userinfo endpoint. The claim must be an array of strings. Most public identity providers do not support group or role management. When using a customizable / on-demand hosted identity provider, name, content, and inclusion in the userinfo endpoint will most likely need to be configured.

documents.title: Option: services.dependency-track.oidc.userProvisioning
documents.content: Specifies if mapped OpenID Connect accounts are automatically created upon successful authentication. When a user logs in with a valid access token but an account has not been previously provisioned, an authentication failure will be returned. This allows admins to control specifically which OpenID Connect users can access the system and which users cannot. When this value is set to true, a local OpenID Connect user will be created and mapped to the OpenID Connect account automatically. This automatic provisioning only affects authentication, not authorization.

The exports table can include two types of element: a string element (as above), or an alternate table element form { path="/path", opts="ro" }. In the alternate form, the (optional) opts attribute is a comma-separated list of export options. The two table element forms can be mixed in the exports table. Note that although diod will not traverse file system boundaries for a given mount due to inode uniqueness constraints, subdirectories of a file system can be separately exported.

documents.title: Option: services.discourse.siteSettings

Settings containing secret data should be set to an attribute set containing the attribute _secret - a string pointing to a file containing the value the option should be set to. See the example to get a better picture of this: in the resulting {file}config/nixos_site_settings.json file, the login.github_client_secret key will be set to the contents of the {file}/run/keys/discourse_github_client_secret file.

documents.title: Option: services.dolibarr.h2o.tls.recommendations
documents.content:
By default, H2O, without prejudice, will use as many TLS versions & cipher suites as it & the TLS library (OpenSSL) can support. The user is expected to hone settings for the security of their server. Setting some constraints is recommended, & if unsure about what TLS settings to use, this option gives curated TLS settings recommendations from Mozilla’s ‘SSL Configuration Generator’ project (see https://ssl-config.mozilla.org) or read more at Mozilla’s Wiki (see https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Server_Side_TLS).
modern : Services with clients that support TLS 1.3 & don’t need backward compatibility
intermediate : General-purpose servers with a variety of clients, recommended for almost all systems
The default for all virtual hosts can be set with services.h2o.defaultTLSRecommendations, but this value can be overridden on a per-host basis using services.h2o.hosts..tls.recommmendations. The settings will also be overidden by manual values set with services.settings.h2o.hosts..tls.extraSettings.
NOTE: older/weaker ciphers might require overriding the OpenSSL version of H2O (such as openssl_legacy). This can be done with sevices.settings.h2o.package.

If this is set to null (the default), no nginx virtualHost will be configured.

documents.content:

With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.

documents.title: Option: services.dolibarr.nginx.forceSSL

This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.dolibarr.nginx.globalRedirect

documents.title: Option: services.dolibarr.nginx.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol. Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given IP address / port. If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.title: Option: services.dolibarr.nginx.http3
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.dolibarr.nginx.http3_hq

documents.title: Option: services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox.*.after
documents.content:
When an IMAP event of interest occurs, this sieve script is executed after any user script respectively.
This setting each specify the location of a single sieve script. The semantics of this setting is similar to sieve_after: the specified scripts form a sequence together with the user script in which the next script is only executed when an (implicit) keep action is executed.

documents.title: Option: services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox.*.before
documents.content:
When an IMAP event of interest occurs, this sieve script is executed before any user script respectively.
This setting each specify the location of a single sieve script. The semantics of this setting is similar to sieve_before: the specified scripts form a sequence together with the user script in which the next script is only executed when an (implicit) keep action is executed.

documents.title: Option: services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox.*.causes
documents.content:
Only execute the administrator Sieve scripts for the mailbox configured with services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox..name when one of the listed IMAPSIEVE causes apply.
This has no effect on the user script, which is always executed no matter the cause.

documents.title: Option: services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox.*.from
documents.content:
Only execute the administrator Sieve scripts for the mailbox configured with services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox..name when the message originates from the indicated mailbox.
This setting supports wildcards with a syntax compatible with the IMAP LIST command, meaning that this setting can apply to multiple or even all ("*") mailboxes.

documents.title: Option: services.dovecot2.imapsieve.mailbox.*.name
documents.content:
This setting configures the name of a mailbox for which administrator scripts are configured.
The settings defined hereafter with matching sequence numbers apply to the mailbox named by this setting.
This setting supports wildcards with a syntax compatible with the IMAP LIST command, meaning that this setting can apply to multiple or even all ("*") mailboxes.

documents.title: Option: services.draupnir.settings.managementRoom

::: {.warning} When using a room alias, make sure the alias used is on the local homeserver! This prevents an issue where the control room becomes undefined when the alias can't be resolved. :::

documents.title: Option: services.drupal.sites.<name>.configRoot
documents.content:
An optional path string with a leading slash indicating the location of the config sync directory on the Drupal package. Your package will probably have a config sync directory if it has been significantly customized.
The path must be relative to the project root directory.
This option differs from the configSyncDir option, which tells this service where to create a user-writeable config directory on NixOS.

documents.content:
The location of the user-managed Drupal config sync directory. Drupal will both read from and write to this directory when executing configuration management operations.
This option differs from the configRoot option, which this service uses to discover the location of the config sync directory in the package's source code.

documents.content: The dsnet package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.dsnet.settings
documents.content:
The settings to use for dsnet. This will be converted to a JSON object that will be passed to dsnet as a patch, using the patch command when the service is started. See the dsnet documentation for more information on the additional options.
Note that the resulting /etc/dsnetconfg.json is more of a database than it is a configuration file. It is therefore recommended that system specific values are configured here, rather than the full configuration including peers.
Peers may be managed via the dsnet add/remove commands, negating the need to manage key material and cumbersom configuration with nix. If you want peer configuration in nix, you may as well use the regular wireguard module.

If the available memory falls below this threshold (and the analog is true for {option}freeSwapThreshold) the killing begins. SIGTERM is sent first to the process that uses the most memory; then, if the available memory falls below {option}freeMemKillThreshold (and the analog is true for {option}freeSwapKillThreshold), SIGKILL is sent.
See README for details.

If empty, the whitelist defaults to open, but can be managed with the in-game /whitelist console command (see: /help whitelist), which will cause changes to be saved to the game's state directory (see also: stateDirName).

documents.title: Option: services.factorio.loadLatestSave
documents.content:
Load the latest savegame on startup. This overrides saveName, in that the latest save will always be used even if a saved game of the given name exists. It still controls the 'canonical' name of the savegame.

documents.title: Option: services.factorio.mods

Mods the server should install and activate.
The derivations in this list must "build" the mod by simply copying the .zip, named correctly, into the output directory. Eventually, there will be a way to pull in the most up-to-date list of derivations via nixos-channel. Until then, this is for experts only.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.banaction
documents.content: Default banning action (e.g. iptables, iptables-new, iptables-multiport, iptables-ipset-proto6-allports, shorewall, etc). It is used to define action_* variables. Can be overridden globally or per section within jail.local file

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.banaction-allports
documents.content: Default banning action (e.g. iptables, iptables-new, iptables-multiport, shorewall, etc) for "allports" jails. It is used to define action_* variables. Can be overridden globally or per section within jail.local file

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime
documents.content: Number of seconds that a host is banned.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.enable
documents.content: "bantime.increment" allows to use database for searching of previously banned ip's to increase a default ban time using special formula, default it is banTime * 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 ...

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.factor
documents.content: "bantime.factor" is a coefficient to calculate exponent growing of the formula or common multiplier, default value of factor is 1 and with default value of formula, the ban time grows by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 ...

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.formula
documents.content: "bantime.formula" used by default to calculate next value of ban time, default value below, the same ban time growing will be reached by multipliers 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 ...

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.maxtime
documents.content: "bantime.maxtime" is the max number of seconds using the ban time can reach (don't grows further)

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.multipliers
documents.content: "bantime.multipliers" used to calculate next value of ban time instead of formula, corresponding previously ban count and given "bantime.factor" (for multipliers default is 1); following example grows ban time by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 ... and if last ban count greater as multipliers count, always used last multiplier (64 in example), for factor '1' and original ban time 600 - 10.6 hours

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.overalljails
documents.content: "bantime.overalljails" (if true) specifies the search of IP in the database will be executed cross over all jails, if false (default), only current jail of the ban IP will be searched.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.bantime-increment.rndtime
documents.content: "bantime.rndtime" is the max number of seconds using for mixing with random time to prevent "clever" botnets calculate exact time IP can be unbanned again

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.daemonSettings
documents.content: The contents of Fail2ban's main configuration file. It's generally not necessary to change it.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable the fail2ban service.
See the documentation of for what jails are enabled by default.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.extraPackages
documents.content: Extra packages to be made available to the fail2ban service. The example contains the packages needed by the iptables-ipset-proto6 action.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.ignoreIP
documents.content: "ignoreIP" can be a list of IP addresses, CIDR masks or DNS hosts. Fail2ban will not ban a host which matches an address in this list. Several addresses can be defined using space (and/or comma) separator.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.jails
documents.content:
The configuration of each Fail2ban “jail”. A jail consists of an action (such as blocking a port using {command}iptables) that is triggered when a filter applied to a log file triggers more than a certain number of times in a certain time period. Actions are defined in {file}/etc/fail2ban/action.d, while filters are defined in {file}/etc/fail2ban/filter.d.
NixOS comes with a default sshd jail; for it to work well, should be set to "VERBOSE" or higher so that fail2ban can observe failed login attempts. This module sets it to "VERBOSE" if not set otherwise, so enabling fail2ban can make SSH logs more verbose.

documents.title: Option: services.fail2ban.maxretry
documents.content: Number of failures before a host gets banned.

documents.title: Option: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.acmeFallbackHost
documents.content:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.
With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.
