documents.content: The port the server should listen to.

documents.title: Option: services.honk.servername
documents.content: The server name.

documents.title: Option: services.honk.username
documents.content: The admin account username.

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Haskell documentation server.

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.extraOptions
documents.content: Additional command-line arguments to pass to {command}hoogle server

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.haskellPackages
documents.content: Which haskell package set to use.

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.home
documents.content: Url for hoogle logo

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.host
documents.content: Set the host to bind on.

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.packages
documents.content:
The Haskell packages to generate documentation for.
The option value is a function that takes the package set specified in the {var}haskellPackages option as its sole parameter and returns a list of packages.

documents.title: Option: services.hoogle.port
documents.content: Port number Hoogle will be listening to.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable hostapd, a user space daemon for access point and authentication servers. It implements IEEE 802.11 access point management, IEEE 802.1X/WPA/WPA2/EAP Authenticators, RADIUS client, EAP server, and RADIUS authentication server .

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.package
documents.content: The hostapd package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios
documents.content:
This option allows you to define APs for one or multiple physical radios. At least one radio must be specified.
For each radio, hostapd requires a separate logical interface (like wlp3s0, wlp3s1, ...). A default interface is usually be created automatically by your system, but to use multiple radios of a single device, it may be required to create additional logical interfaces for example by using {option}networking.wlanInterfaces.
Each physical radio can only support a single hardware-mode that is configured via ({option}services.hostapd.radios.<radio>.band). To create a dual-band or tri-band AP, you will have to use a device that has multiple physical radios and supports configuring multiple APs (Refer to valid interface combinations in {command}iw list).

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.band
documents.content: Specifies the frequency band to use, possible values are 2g for 2.4 GHz, 5g for 5 GHz, 6g for 6 GHz and 60g for 60 GHz.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.channel
documents.content: The channel to operate on. Use 0 to enable ACS (Automatic Channel Selection). Beware that not every device supports ACS in which case {command}hostapd will fail to start.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.countryCode
documents.content:
Country code (ISO/IEC 3166-1). Used to set regulatory domain. Set as needed to indicate country in which device is operating. This can limit available channels and transmit power. These two octets are used as the first two octets of the Country String (dot11CountryString).
Setting this will force you to also enable IEEE 802.11d and IEEE 802.11h.
IEEE 802.11d: This advertises the countryCode and the set of allowed channels and transmit power levels based on the regulatory limits.
IEEE802.11h: This enables radar detection and DFS (Dynamic Frequency Selection) support if available. DFS support is required on outdoor 5 GHz channels in most countries of the world.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.driver
documents.content: The driver {command}hostapd will use. {var}nl80211 is used with all Linux mac80211 drivers. {var}none is used if building a standalone RADIUS server that does not control any wireless/wired driver. Most applications will probably use the default.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.dynamicConfigScripts
documents.content:
All of these scripts will be executed in lexicographical order before hostapd is started, right after the global segment was generated and may dynamically append global options the generated configuration file.
The first argument will point to the configuration file that you may append to.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks
documents.content: This defines a BSS, colloquially known as a WiFi network. You have to specify at least one.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.apIsolate
documents.content: Isolate traffic between stations (clients) and prevent them from communicating with each other.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.enableRecommendedPairwiseCiphers
documents.content:
Additionally enable the recommended set of pairwise ciphers. This enables newer secure ciphers, additionally to those defined in {option}pairwiseCiphers. You will have to test whether your hardware supports these by trial-and-error, because even if iw list indicates hardware support, your driver might not expose it.
Beware {command}hostapd will most likely not return a useful error message in case this is enabled despite the driver or hardware not supporting the newer ciphers. Look out for messages like Failed to set beacon parameters.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.mode
documents.content:
Selects the authentication mode for this AP.
{var}"none": Don't configure any authentication. This will disable wpa alltogether and create an open AP. Use {option}settings together with this option if you want to configure the authentication manually. Any password options will still be effective, if set.
{var}"wpa2-sha1": Not recommended. WPA2-Personal using HMAC-SHA1. Passwords are set using {option}wpaPassword or preferably by {option}wpaPasswordFile or {option}wpaPskFile.
{var}"wpa2-sha256": WPA2-Personal using HMAC-SHA256 (IEEE 802.11i/RSN). Passwords are set using {option}wpaPassword or preferably by {option}wpaPasswordFile or {option}wpaPskFile.
{var}"wpa3-sae-transition": Use WPA3-Personal (SAE) if possible, otherwise fallback to WPA2-SHA256. Only use if necessary and switch to the newer WPA3-SAE when possible. You will have to specify both {option}wpaPassword and {option}saePasswords (or one of their alternatives).
{var}"wpa3-sae": Use WPA3-Personal (SAE). This is currently the recommended way to setup a secured WiFi AP (as of March 2023) and therefore the default. Passwords are set using either {option}saePasswords or {option}saePasswordsFile.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.pairwiseCiphers
documents.content:
Set of accepted cipher suites (encryption algorithms) for pairwise keys (unicast packets). By default this allows just CCMP, which is the only commonly supported secure option. Use {option}enableRecommendedPairwiseCiphers to also enable newer recommended ciphers.
Please refer to the hostapd documentation for allowed values. Generally, only CCMP or GCMP modes should be considered safe options. Most devices support CCMP while GCMP and GCMP-256 is often only available with devices supporting WiFi 5 (IEEE 802.11ac) or higher. CCMP-256 support is rare.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saeAddToMacAllow
documents.content: If set, all sae password entries that have a non-wildcard MAC associated to them will additionally be used to populate the MAC allow list. This is additional to any entries set via {option}macAllow or {option}macAllowFile.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords
documents.content:
Sets allowed passwords for WPA3-SAE.
The last matching (based on peer MAC address and identifier) entry is used to select which password to use. An empty string has the special meaning of removing all previously added entries.
Warning: These entries will get put into a world-readable file in the Nix store! Using {option}saePasswordFile instead is recommended.
Not used when {option}mode is {var}"wpa2-sha1" or {var}"wpa2-sha256".

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.id
documents.content: If this attribute is given with non-zero length, it will set the password identifier for this entry. It can then only be used with that identifier.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.mac
documents.content: If this attribute is not included, or if is set to the wildcard address (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff), the entry is available for any station (client) to use. If a specific peer MAC address is included, only a station with that MAC address is allowed to use the entry.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.password
documents.content:
The password for this entry. SAE technically imposes no restrictions on password length or character set. But due to limitations of {command}hostapd's config file format, a true newline character cannot be parsed.
Warning: This password will get put into a world-readable file in the Nix store! Prefer using the sibling option {option}passwordFile or directly set {option}saePasswordsFile.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.passwordFile
documents.content: The password for this entry, read from the given file when starting hostapd. SAE technically imposes no restrictions on password length or character set. But due to limitations of {command}hostapd's config file format, a true newline character cannot be parsed.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.pk
documents.content: If this attribute is given, SAE-PK will be enabled for this connection. This prevents evil-twin attacks, but a public key is required additionally to connect. (Essentially adds pubkey authentication such that the client can verify identity of the AP)

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.vlanid
documents.content: If this attribute is given, all clients using this entry will get tagged with the given VLAN ID.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswordsFile
documents.content:
Sets the password for WPA3-SAE. Follows the same rules as {option}saePasswords, but reads the entries from the given file to prevent them from being put into the Nix store.
One entry per line, empty lines and lines beginning with # will be ignored. Each line must match the following format, although the order of optional parameters doesn't matter: <password>[|mac=<peer mac>][|vlanid=<VLAN ID>][|pk=<m:ECPrivateKey-base64>][|id=<identifier>]
Not used when {option}mode is {var}"wpa2-sha1" or {var}"wpa2-sha256".

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.wpaPassword
documents.content:
Sets the password for WPA-PSK that will be converted to the pre-shared key. The password length must be in the range [8, 63] characters. While some devices may allow arbitrary characters (such as UTF-8) to be used, but the standard specifies that each character in the passphrase must be an ASCII character in the range [0x20, 0x7e] (IEEE Std. 802.11i-2004, Annex H.4.1). Use emojis at your own risk.
Not used when {option}mode is {var}"wpa3-sae".
Warning: This password will get put into a world-readable file in the Nix store! Using {option}wpaPasswordFile or {option}wpaPskFile instead is recommended.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.wpaPasswordFile
documents.content:
Sets the password for WPA-PSK. Follows the same rules as {option}wpaPassword, but reads the password from the given file to prevent the password from being put into the Nix store.
Not used when {option}mode is {var}"wpa3-sae".

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.wpaPskFile
documents.content:
Sets the password(s) for WPA-PSK. Similar to {option}wpaPasswordFile, but additionally allows specifying multiple passwords, and some other options.
Each line, except for empty lines and lines starting with #, must contain a MAC address and either a 64-hex-digit PSK or a password separated with a space. The password must follow the same rules as outlined in {option}wpaPassword. The special MAC address 00:00:00:00:00:00 can be used to configure PSKs that any client can use.
An optional key identifier can be added by prefixing the line with keyid=<keyid_string> An optional VLAN ID can be specified by prefixing the line with vlanid=<VLAN ID>. An optional WPS tag can be added by prefixing the line with wps=<0/1> (default: 0). Any matching entry with that tag will be used when generating a PSK for a WPS Enrollee instead of generating a new random per-Enrollee PSK.
Not used when {option}mode is {var}"wpa3-sae".

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.bssid
documents.content: Specifies the BSSID for this BSS. Usually determined automatically, but for now you have to manually specify them when using multiple BSS. Try assigning related addresses from the locally administered MAC address ranges, by reusing the hardware address but replacing the second nibble with 2, 6, A or E. (e.g. if real address is XX:XX:XX:XX:XX, try X2:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX, X6:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX, ... for the second, third, ... BSS)

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.dynamicConfigScripts
documents.content:
All of these scripts will be executed in lexicographical order before hostapd is started, right after the bss segment was generated and may dynamically append bss options to the generated configuration file.
The first argument will point to the configuration file that you may append to. The second and third argument will point to this BSS's MAC allow and MAC deny file respectively.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.group
documents.content: Members of this group can access the control socket for this interface.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.ignoreBroadcastSsid
documents.content:
Send empty SSID in beacons and ignore probe request frames that do not specify full SSID, i.e., require stations to know SSID. Note that this does not increase security, since your clients will then broadcast the SSID instead, which can increase congestion.
{var}"disabled": Advertise ssid normally.
{var}"empty": send empty (length=0) SSID in beacon and ignore probe request for broadcast SSID
{var}"clear": clear SSID (ASCII 0), but keep the original length (this may be required with some legacy clients that do not support empty SSID) and ignore probe requests for broadcast SSID. Only use this if empty does not work with your clients.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.logLevel
documents.content: Levels (minimum value for logged events): 0 = verbose debugging 1 = debugging 2 = informational messages 3 = notification 4 = warning

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macAcl
documents.content:
Station MAC address -based authentication. The following modes are available:
{var}"deny": Allow unless listed in {option}macDeny (default)
{var}"allow": Deny unless listed in {option}macAllow
{var}"radius": Use external radius server, but check both {option}macAllow and {option}macDeny first

Please note that this kind of access control requires a driver that uses hostapd to take care of management frame processing and as such, this can be used with driver=hostap or driver=nl80211, but not with driver=atheros.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macAllow
documents.content: Specifies the MAC addresses to allow if {option}macAcl is set to {var}"allow" or {var}"radius". These values will be world-readable in the Nix store. Values will automatically be merged with {option}macAllowFile if necessary.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macAllowFile
documents.content: Specifies a file containing the MAC addresses to allow if {option}macAcl is set to {var}"allow" or {var}"radius". The file should contain exactly one MAC address per line. Comments and empty lines are ignored, only lines starting with a valid MAC address will be considered (e.g. 11:22:33:44:55:66) and any content after the MAC address is ignored.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macDeny
documents.content: Specifies the MAC addresses to deny if {option}macAcl is set to {var}"deny" or {var}"radius". These values will be world-readable in the Nix store. Values will automatically be merged with {option}macDenyFile if necessary.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macDenyFile
documents.content: Specifies a file containing the MAC addresses to deny if {option}macAcl is set to {var}"deny" or {var}"radius". The file should contain exactly one MAC address per line. Comments and empty lines are ignored, only lines starting with a valid MAC address will be considered (e.g. 11:22:33:44:55:66) and any content after the MAC address is ignored.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.settings
documents.content:
Extra configuration options to put at the end of this BSS's defintion in the hostapd.conf for the associated interface. To find out which options are global and which are per-bss you have to read hostapd's source code, which is non-trivial and not documented otherwise.
Lists will be converted to multiple definitions of the same key, and booleans to 0/1. Otherwise, the inputs are not modified or checked for correctness.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.ssid
documents.content: SSID to be used in IEEE 802.11 management frames.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.utf8Ssid
documents.content: Whether the SSID is to be interpreted using UTF-8 encoding.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.noScan
documents.content: Disables scan for overlapping BSSs in HT40+/- mode. Caution: turning this on will likely violate regulatory requirements!

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.settings
documents.content:
Extra configuration options to put at the end of global initialization, before defining BSSs. To find out which options are global and which are per-bss you have to read hostapd's source code, which is non-trivial and not documented otherwise.
Lists will be converted to multiple definitions of the same key, and booleans to 0/1. Otherwise, the inputs are not modified or checked for correctness.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi4.capabilities
documents.content:
HT (High Throughput) capabilities given as a list of flags. Please refer to the hostapd documentation for allowed values and only set values supported by your physical adapter.
The default contains common values supported by most adapters.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi4.enable
documents.content: Enables support for IEEE 802.11n (WiFi 4, HT). This is enabled by default, since the vase majority of devices are expected to support this.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi4.require
documents.content: Require stations (clients) to support WiFi 4 (HT) and disassociate them if they don't.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi5.capabilities
documents.content: VHT (Very High Throughput) capabilities given as a list of flags. Please refer to the hostapd documentation for allowed values and only set values supported by your physical adapter.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi5.enable
documents.content: Enables support for IEEE 802.11ac (WiFi 5, VHT)

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi5.operatingChannelWidth
documents.content:
Determines the operating channel width for VHT.
{var}"20or40": 20 or 40 MHz operating channel width
{var}"80": 80 MHz channel width
{var}"160": 160 MHz channel width
{var}"80+80": 80+80 MHz channel width

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi5.require
documents.content: Require stations (clients) to support WiFi 5 (VHT) and disassociate them if they don't.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi6.enable
documents.content: Enables support for IEEE 802.11ax (WiFi 6, HE)

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi6.multiUserBeamformer
documents.content: HE multi user beamformee support

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi6.operatingChannelWidth
documents.content:
Determines the operating channel width for HE.
{var}"20or40": 20 or 40 MHz operating channel width
{var}"80": 80 MHz channel width
{var}"160": 160 MHz channel width
{var}"80+80": 80+80 MHz channel width

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi6.require
documents.content: Require stations (clients) to support WiFi 6 (HE) and disassociate them if they don't.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi6.singleUserBeamformee
documents.content: HE single user beamformee support

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi6.singleUserBeamformer
documents.content: HE single user beamformer support

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi7.enable
documents.content: Enables support for IEEE 802.11be (WiFi 7, EHT). This is currently experimental and requires you to manually enable CONFIG_IEEE80211BE when building hostapd.

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi7.multiUserBeamformer
documents.content: EHT multi user beamformee support

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi7.operatingChannelWidth
documents.content:
Determines the operating channel width for EHT.
{var}"20or40": 20 or 40 MHz operating channel width
{var}"80": 80 MHz channel width
{var}"160": 160 MHz channel width
{var}"80+80": 80+80 MHz channel width

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi7.singleUserBeamformee
documents.content: EHT single user beamformee support

documents.title: Option: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.wifi7.singleUserBeamformer
documents.content: EHT single user beamformer support

documents.title: Option: services.hound.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable hound.

documents.title: Option: services.hound.group
documents.content: Group the hound daemon should execute under.

documents.title: Option: services.hound.home
documents.content: The path to use as hound's $HOME. If the default user "hound" is configured then this is the home of the "hound" user.

documents.title: Option: services.hound.listen
documents.content: Listen on this [IP]:port

documents.title: Option: services.hound.package
documents.content: The hound package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.hound.settings
documents.content:
The full configuration of the Hound daemon. See the upstream documentation https://github.com/hound-search/hound/blob/main/docs/config-options.md for details.
:::{.note} The dbpath should be an absolute path to a writable directory. :::.com/hound-search/hound/blob/main/docs/config-options.md>.

documents.title: Option: services.hound.user
documents.content: User the hound daemon should execute under.

documents.title: Option: services.howdy.control
documents.content:
PAM control flag to use for Howdy.
Sets the {option}security.pam.howdy.control option.
Refer to {manpage}pam.conf(5) for options.

documents.title: Option: services.howdy.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable Howdy and its PAM module for face recognition. See services.linux-enable-ir-emitter for enabling the IR emitter support.
::: {.caution} Howdy is not a safe alternative to unlocking with your password. It can be fooled using a well-printed photo.
Do not use it as the sole authentication method for your system. :::
::: {.note} By default, the {option}config.services.howdy.control option is set to "required", meaning it will act as a second-factor authentication in most services. To change this, set the option to "sufficient". :::

documents.title: Option: services.howdy.package
documents.content: The howdy package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.howdy.settings
documents.content: Howdy configuration file. Refer to https://github.com/boltgolt/howdy/blob/d3ab99382f88f043d15f15c1450ab69433892a1c/howdy/src/config.ini for options.

documents.title: Option: services.hqplayerd.auth.password
documents.content:
Password used for HQPlayer's WebUI.
Without this you will need to manually create the credentials after first start by going to http://your.ip/8088/auth

documents.title: Option: services.hqplayerd.auth.username
documents.content:
Username used for HQPlayer's WebUI.
Without this you will need to manually create the credentials after first start by going to http://your.ip/8088/auth

documents.title: Option: services.hqplayerd.config
documents.content:
HQplayer daemon configuration, written to /etc/hqplayer/hqplayerd.xml.
Refer to share/doc/hqplayerd/readme.txt in the hqplayerd derivation for possible values.

documents.title: Option: services.hqplayerd.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable HQPlayer Embedded.

documents.title: Option: services.hqplayerd.licenseFile
documents.content:
Path to the HQPlayer license key file.
Without this, the service will run in trial mode and restart every 30 minutes.

documents.title: Option: services.hqplayerd.openFirewall
documents.content: Opens ports needed for the WebUI and controller API.

documents.title: Option: services.htpdate.enable
documents.content: Enable htpdate daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.htpdate.extraOptions
documents.content: Additional command line arguments to pass to htpdate.

documents.title: Option: services.htpdate.proxy
documents.content: HTTP proxy used for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.htpdate.servers
documents.content: HTTP servers to use for time synchronization.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.adminAddr
documents.content: E-mail address of the server administrator.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.configFile
documents.content: Override the configuration file used by Apache. By default, NixOS generates one automatically.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.customLogFormat
documents.content:
Defines a custom Apache HTTPD access log format string.
This option is only consulted when logFormat is set to custom. The value must be a valid Apache LogFormat specification and will be registered under the symbolic name custom.
See https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/logs.html#formats for the formal definition of log format directives.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the Apache HTTP Server.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.enableMellon
documents.content: Whether to enable the mod_auth_mellon module.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.enablePHP
documents.content: Whether to enable the PHP module.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.enablePerl
documents.content: Whether to enable the Perl module (mod_perl).

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.extraConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines appended to the generated Apache configuration file. Note that this mechanism will not work when {option}configFile is overridden.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.extraModules
documents.content: Additional Apache modules to be used. These can be specified as a string in the case of modules distributed with Apache, or as an attribute set specifying the {var}name and {var}path of the module.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.group
documents.content: Group under which httpd children processes run.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.logDir
documents.content: Directory for Apache's log files. It is created automatically.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.logFormat
documents.content:
Selects the access log format written to log files.
The values combined, common, referer, and agent correspond to predefined Apache HTTPD log formats. Setting the value to custom enables the use of a user-defined format string specified via customLogFormat. The value none disables access logging entirely.
Further details on Apache log formats are available at https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/logs.html.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.logLevel
documents.content: Controls the verbosity of the ErrorLog. See https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/core.html#loglevel for more details.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.logPerVirtualHost
documents.content: If enabled, each virtual host gets its own {file}access.log and {file}error.log, namely suffixed by the {option}hostName of the virtual host.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.maxClients
documents.content: Maximum number of httpd processes (prefork)

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.maxRequestsPerChild
documents.content: Maximum number of httpd requests answered per httpd child (prefork), 0 means unlimited.

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.mpm
documents.content: Multi-processing module to be used by Apache. Available modules are prefork (handles each request in a separate child process), worker (hybrid approach that starts a number of child processes each running a number of threads) and event (the default; a recent variant of worker that handles persistent connections more efficiently).

documents.title: Option: services.httpd.package

documents.title: Option: services.jellyfin.forceEncodingConfig
documents.content:
Whether to overwrite Jellyfin's encoding.xml configuration file on each service start.
When enabled, the encoding configuration specified in {option}services.jellyfin.transcoding and {option}services.jellyfin.hardwareAcceleration will be applied on every service restart. A backup of the existing encoding.xml will be created at encoding.xml.backup-$timestamp.
::: {.warning} Enabling this option means that any changes made to transcoding settings through Jellyfin's web dashboard will be lost on the next service restart. The NixOS configuration becomes the single source of truth for encoding settings. :::
When disabled (the default), the encoding configuration is only written if no encoding.xml exists yet. This allows settings to be changed through Jellyfin's web dashboard and persist across restarts, but means the NixOS configuration options will be ignored after the initial setup.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.acmeFallbackHost
documents.content:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.
With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.acmeRoot
documents.content: Directory for the ACME challenge, which is public. Don't put certs or keys in here. Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.addSSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443).

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.default
documents.content: Makes this vhost the default.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.enableACME
documents.content: Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost. Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}useACMEHost.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.forceSSL
documents.content: Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) all plain HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.globalRedirect
documents.content: If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) to the given hostname.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol. Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given IP address / port. If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.http3
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.http3_hq
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that special application protocol support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.kTLS
documents.content: Whether to enable kTLS support. Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel. Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.audit
documents.content:
If enabled systemd-journald will turn on auditing on start-up. If disabled it will turn it off. If unset it will neither enable nor disable it, leaving the previous state unchanged.
NixOS defaults to leaving this unset as enabling audit without auditd running leads to spamming /dev/kmesg with random messages and if you enable auditd then auditd is responsible for turning auditing on.
If you want to have audit logs in journald and do not mind audit logs also ending up in /dev/kmesg you can set this option to true.
If you want to for some ununderstandable reason disable auditing if auditd enabled it then you can set this option to false. It is of NixOS' opinion that setting this to false is definitely the wrong thing to do - but it's an option.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.rateLimitBurst
documents.content:
Configures the rate limiting burst limit (number of messages per interval) that is applied to all messages generated on the system. This rate limiting is applied per-service, so that two services which log do not interfere with each other's limit.
Note that the effective rate limit is multiplied by a factor derived from the available free disk space for the journal as described on {manpage}journald.conf(5).
Note that the total amount of logs stored is limited by journald settings such as SystemMaxUse, which defaults to 10% the file system size (capped at max 4GB), and SystemKeepFree, which defaults to 15% of the file system size.
It is thus recommended to compute what period of time that you will be able to store logs for when an application logs at full burst rate. With default settings for log lines that are 100 Bytes long, this can amount to just a few hours.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.rateLimitInterval
documents.content:
Configures the rate limiting interval that is applied to all messages generated on the system. This rate limiting is applied per-service, so that two services which log do not interfere with each other's limit. The value may be specified in the following units: s, min, h, ms, us. To turn off any kind of rate limiting, set either value to 0.
See {option}services.journald.rateLimitBurst for important considerations when setting this value.

documents.content:
The location of the output journal.
In case the output file is not specified, journal files will be created underneath the selected directory. Files will be called {file}remote-hostname.journal, where the hostname part is the escaped hostname of the source endpoint of the connection, or the numerical address if the hostname cannot be determined.

documents.content:

documents.title: Option: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.ServerCertificateFile
documents.content:
A path to a SSL certificate file in PEM format.
This option can be used with listen = "https". If the path refers to an AF_UNIX stream socket in the file system a connection is made to it and the certificate read from it.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.ServerKeyFile
documents.content:
A path to a SSL secret key file in PEM format.
Note that due to security reasons, systemd-journal-remote will refuse files from the world-readable /nix/store. This file should be readable by the "" user.
This option can be used with listen = "https". If the path refers to an AF_UNIX stream socket in the file system a connection is made to it and the key read from it.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.SplitMode
documents.content: With "host", a separate output file is used, based on the hostname of the other endpoint of a connection. With "none", only one output journal file is used.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.TrustedCertificateFile
documents.content:
A path to a SSL CA certificate file in PEM format, or all.
If all is set, then client certificate checking will be disabled.
This option can be used with listen = "https". If the path refers to an AF_UNIX stream socket in the file system a connection is made to it and the certificate read from it.

documents.title: Option: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.NetworkTimeoutSec
documents.content:

If the server is not reachable over the network for the configured time, systemd-journal-upload exits. Takes a value in seconds (or in other time units if suffixed with "ms", "min", "h", etc). For details, see {manpage}systemd.time(5).

documents.title: Option: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.ServerCertificateFile

In contrary to what the name suggests, this option configures the client certificate sent to the remote journal server.

In contrary to what the name suggests, this option configures the client private key sent to the remote journal server.
This key should not be world-readable, and must be readably by the systemd-journal group.

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.extraConfig

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.filterBlocks
documents.content:
filterBlocks can be defined to blacklist journal messages which are not errors. Each block matches on a log entry field, and the filters in that block then are matched against all messages with a matching log entry field.
All messages whose PRIORITY is at least 6 (INFO) are processed by journalwatch. If you don't specify any filterBlocks, PRIORITY is reduced to 5 (NOTICE) by default.
All regular expressions are extended Python regular expressions, for details see: http://doc.pyschools.com/html/regex.html

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.filterBlocks.*.filters
documents.content: The filters to apply on all messages which satisfy {option}match. Any of those messages that match any specified filter will be removed from journalwatch's output. Each filter is an extended Python regular expression. You can specify multiple filters and separate them by newlines. Lines starting with '#' are comments. Inline-comments are not permitted.

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.filterBlocks.*.match
documents.content: Syntax: field = value Specifies the log entry field this block should apply to. If the field of a message matches this value, this patternBlock's {option}filters are applied. If value starts and ends with a slash, it is interpreted as an extended python regular expression, if not, it's an exact match. The journal fields are explained in {manpage}systemd.journal-fields(7).

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.interval

The format is described in {manpage}systemd.time(7).

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.mailBinary

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.mailTo

documents.title: Option: services.journalwatch.priority
documents.content: Lowest priority of message to be considered. A value between 7 ("debug"), and 0 ("emerg"). Defaults to 6 ("info"). If you don't care about anything with "info" priority, you can reduce this to e.g. 5 ("notice") to considerably reduce the amount of messages without needing many {option}filterBlocks.

documents.content:
Jupyterhub spawner to use
There are many spawners available including: local process, systemd, docker, kubernetes, yarn, batch, etc.

documents.title: Option: services.jupyterhub.stateDirectory
documents.content: Directory for jupyterhub state (token + database)

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.agentToken
documents.content:
The k3s token agents can use to connect to the server. This option only makes sense on server nodes (role = server).
WARNING: This option will expose your token unencrypted in the world-readable nix store. If this is undesired use the tokenFile option instead.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.agentTokenFile
documents.content: File path containing the k3s token agents can use to connect to the server. This option only makes sense on server nodes (role = server).

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts
documents.content:
Auto deploying Helm charts that are installed by the k3s Helm controller. Avoid using attribute names that are also used in the and options. Manifests with the same name will override auto deploying charts with the same name. This option only makes sense on server nodes (role = server). See the k3s Helm documentation for further information.
WARNING: If you have multiple server nodes, and set this option on more than one server, it is your responsibility to ensure that files stay in sync across those nodes. AddOn content is not synced between nodes, and k3s cannot guarantee correct behavior if different servers attempt to deploy conflicting manifests.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.createNamespace
documents.content: Whether to create the target namespace if not present.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the installation of this Helm chart. Note that setting this option to false will not uninstall the chart from the cluster, if it was previously installed. Please use the the --disable flag or .skip files to delete/disable Helm charts, as mentioned in the docs.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.extraDeploy
documents.content: List of extra Kubernetes manifests to deploy with this Helm chart.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.extraFieldDefinitions
documents.content: Extra HelmChart field definitions that are merged with the rest of the HelmChart custom resource. This can be used to set advanced fields or to overwrite generated fields. See https://docs.k3s.io/helm#helmchart-field-definitions for possible fields.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.hash
documents.content: The hash of the packaged Helm chart. Only has an effect if package is not set. The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a .tgz archive on the filesystem.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.name
documents.content: The name of the Helm chart. Only has an effect if package is not set. The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a .tgz archive on the filesystem.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.package
documents.content: The packaged Helm chart. Overwrites the options repo, name, version and hash in case of conflicts.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.repo
documents.content: The repo of the Helm chart. Only has an effect if package is not set. The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a .tgz archive on the filesystem.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.targetNamespace
documents.content: The namespace in which the Helm chart gets installed.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.values
documents.content:
Override default chart values via Nix expressions. This is equivalent to setting values in a values.yaml file.
WARNING: The values (including secrets!) specified here are exposed unencrypted in the world-readable nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.version
documents.content: The version of the Helm chart. Only has an effect if package is not set. The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a .tgz archive on the filesystem.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.charts
documents.content: Packaged Helm charts that are linked to {file}/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/static/charts before k3s starts. The attribute name will be used as the link target (relative to {file}/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/static/charts). The specified charts will only be placed on the file system and made available via the Kubernetes APIServer from within the cluster. See the option and the k3s Helm controller docs to deploy Helm charts. This option only makes sense on server nodes (role = server).

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.clusterInit
documents.content:
Initialize HA cluster using an embedded etcd datastore.
If this option is false and role is server
On a server that was using the default embedded sqlite backend, enabling this option will migrate to an embedded etcd DB.
If an HA cluster using the embedded etcd datastore was already initialized, this option has no effect.
This option only makes sense in a server that is not connecting to another server.
If you are configuring an HA cluster with an embedded etcd, the 1st server must have clusterInit = true and other servers must connect to it using serverAddr.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.configPath
documents.content: File path containing the k3s YAML config. This is useful when the config is generated (for example on boot).

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.containerdConfigTemplate
documents.content: Config template for containerd, to be placed at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/containerd/config.toml.tmpl. See the docs on configuring containerd.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.disable
documents.content: Disable default components, see the K3s documentation.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.disableAgent
documents.content: Only run the server. This option only makes sense for a server.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable k3s.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.environmentFile
documents.content: File path containing environment variables for configuring the k3s service in the format of an EnvironmentFile. See {manpage}systemd.exec(5).

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.extraFlags
documents.content: Extra flags to pass to the k3s command.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.extraKubeProxyConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration to add to the kube-proxy's configuration file. The subset of the kube-proxy's configuration that can be configured via a file is defined by the KubeProxyConfiguration struct. Note that the kubeconfig param will be overriden by clientConnection.kubeconfig, so you must set the clientConnection.kubeconfig option if you want to use extraKubeProxyConfig.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.extraKubeletConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration to add to the kubelet's configuration file. The subset of the kubelet's configuration that can be configured via a file is defined by the KubeletConfiguration struct. See the documentation for further information.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.gracefulNodeShutdown.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable graceful node shutdowns where the kubelet attempts to detect node system shutdown and terminates pods running on the node. See the documentation for further information. .

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.gracefulNodeShutdown.shutdownGracePeriod
documents.content: Specifies the total duration that the node should delay the shutdown by. This is the total grace period for pod termination for both regular and critical pods.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.gracefulNodeShutdown.shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods
documents.content: Specifies the duration used to terminate critical pods during a node shutdown. This should be less than shutdownGracePeriod.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.images
documents.content: List of derivations that provide container images. All images are linked to {file}/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images before k3s starts and are consequently imported by the k3s agent. Consider importing the k3s airgap images archive of the k3s package in use, if you want to pre-provision this node with all k3s container images. This option only makes sense on nodes with an enabled agent.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.manifests
documents.content:
Auto-deploying manifests that are linked to {file}/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests before k3s starts. Note that deleting manifest files will not remove or otherwise modify the resources it created. Please use the the --disable flag or .skip files to delete/disable AddOns, as mentioned in the docs. This option only makes sense on server nodes (role = server). Read the auto-deploying manifests docs for further information.
WARNING: If you have multiple server nodes, and set this option on more than one server, it is your responsibility to ensure that files stay in sync across those nodes. AddOn content is not synced between nodes, and k3s cannot guarantee correct behavior if different servers attempt to deploy conflicting manifests.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.content
documents.content: Content of the manifest file. A single attribute set will generate a single document YAML file. A list of attribute sets will generate multiple documents separated by --- in a single YAML file.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.enable
documents.content: Whether this manifest file should be generated.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.source
documents.content: Path of the source .yaml file.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.target
documents.content: Name of the symlink (relative to {file}/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests). Defaults to the attribute name.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.nodeExternalIP
documents.content: IPv4/IPv6 external addresses to advertise for node.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.nodeIP
documents.content: IPv4/IPv6 addresses to advertise for node.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.nodeLabel
documents.content: Registering and starting kubelet with set of labels.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.nodeName
documents.content: Node name.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.nodeTaint
documents.content: Registering kubelet with set of taints.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.package
documents.content: The k3s package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.role
documents.content:
Whether k3s should run as a server or agent.
If it's a server:
By default it also runs workloads as an agent.
Starts by default as a standalone server using an embedded sqlite datastore.
Configure clusterInit = true to switch over to embedded etcd datastore and enable HA mode.
Configure serverAddr to join an already-initialized HA cluster.

If it's an agent:
serverAddr is required.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.selinux
documents.content: Enable SELinux in containerd.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.serverAddr
documents.content:
The k3s server to connect to.
Servers and agents need to communicate each other. Read the networking docs to know how to configure the firewall.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.token
documents.content:
The k3s token to use when connecting to a server.
WARNING: This option will expose your token unencrypted in the world-readable nix store. If this is undesired use the tokenFile option instead.

documents.title: Option: services.k3s.tokenFile
documents.content: File path containing the k3s token to use when connecting to a server.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable kanata, a tool to improve keyboard comfort and usability with advanced customization.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards
documents.content: Keyboard configurations.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.config
documents.content:
Configuration other than defcfg.
See the upstream documentation and example config files for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.configFile
documents.content:
The config file.
By default, it is generated by values from other kanata module options.
You can also set it to your own full config file which overrides all other kanata module options. See the upstream documentation and example config files for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.devices
documents.content:
Paths to keyboard devices.
An empty list, the default value, lets kanata detect which input devices are keyboards and intercept them all.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.extraArgs
documents.content: Extra command line arguments passed to kanata.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.extraDefCfg
documents.content:
Configuration of defcfg other than linux-dev (generated from the devices option) and linux-continue-if-no-devs-found (hardcoded to be yes).
See the upstream documentation and example config files for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.port
documents.content: Port to run the TCP server on. null will not run the server.

documents.title: Option: services.kanata.package
documents.content: The kanata package to use. ::: {.note} If {option}danger-enable-cmd is enabled in any of the keyboards, the kanata-with-cmd package should be used. :::

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.dataDir
documents.content: Default data folder for Kanboard.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.domain
documents.content: FQDN for the Kanboard instance.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Kanboard.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.group
documents.content: Group under which Kanboard runs.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx
documents.content: With this option, you can customize an NGINX virtual host which already has sensible defaults for Kanboard. Set to { } if you do not need any customization for the virtual host. If enabled, then by default, the {option}serverName is ${domain}. If this is set to null (the default), no NGINX virtual host will be configured.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
documents.content:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.
With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.acmeRoot
documents.content: Directory for the ACME challenge, which is public. Don't put certs or keys in here. Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.addSSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443).

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.default
documents.content: Makes this vhost the default.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.enableACME
documents.content: Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost. Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}useACMEHost.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.forceSSL
documents.content: Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) all plain HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.globalRedirect
documents.content: If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) to the given hostname.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol. Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given IP address / port. If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.http3
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.http3_hq
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that special application protocol support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.kTLS
documents.content: Whether to enable kTLS support. Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel. Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listen
documents.content:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host. IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets. Note: this option overrides addSSL and onlySSL.
If you only want to set the addresses manually and not the ports, take a look at listenAddresses.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.addr
documents.content: Listen address.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.extraParameters
documents.content: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.port
documents.content: Port number to listen on. If unset and the listen address is not a socket then nginx defaults to 80.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.proxyProtocol
documents.content: Enable PROXY protocol.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.ssl
documents.content: Enable SSL.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.listenAddresses
documents.content:
Listen addresses for this virtual host. Compared to listen this only sets the addresses and the ports are chosen automatically.
Note: This option overrides networking.enableIPv6

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations
documents.content: Declarative location config

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.alias
documents.content: Alias directory for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the location verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.fastcgiParams
documents.content: FastCGI parameters to override. Unlike in the Nginx configuration file, overriding only some default parameters won't unset the default values for other parameters.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.index
documents.content: Adds index directive.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.priority
documents.content: Order of this location block in relation to the others in the vhost. The semantics are the same as with lib.mkOrder. Smaller values have a greater priority.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.proxyPass
documents.content: Adds proxy_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedProxySettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.proxyWebsockets
documents.content: Whether to support proxying websocket connections with HTTP/1.1.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.recommendedProxySettings
documents.content: Enable recommended proxy settings.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.recommendedUwsgiSettings
documents.content: Enable recommended uwsgi settings.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.return
documents.content: Adds a return directive, for e.g. redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.root
documents.content: Root directory for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.tryFiles
documents.content: Adds try_files directive.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.locations.<name>.uwsgiPass
documents.content: Adds uwsgi_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedUwsgiSettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.onlySSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS and reject plain HTTP connections. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on port 443.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.quic
documents.content: Whether to enable the QUIC transport protocol. Note that QUIC support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.redirectCode
documents.content: HTTP status used by globalRedirect and forceSSL. Possible usecases include temporary (302, 307) redirects, keeping the request method and body (307, 308), or explicitly resetting the method to GET (303). See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.rejectSSL
documents.content: Whether to listen for and reject all HTTPS connections to this vhost. Useful in default server blocks to avoid serving the certificate for another vhost. Uses the ssl_reject_handshake directive available in nginx versions 1.19.4 and above.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.reuseport
documents.content: Create an individual listening socket . It is required to specify only once on one of the hosts.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.root
documents.content: The path of the web root directory.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.serverAliases
documents.content: Additional names of virtual hosts served by this virtual host configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.serverName
documents.content: Name of this virtual host. Defaults to attribute name in virtualHosts.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.sslCertificate
documents.content: Path to server SSL certificate.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.sslCertificateKey
documents.content: Path to server SSL certificate key.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.sslTrustedCertificate
documents.content: Path to root SSL certificate for stapling and client certificates.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.nginx.useACMEHost
documents.content: A host of an existing Let's Encrypt certificate to use. This is useful if you have many subdomains and want to avoid hitting the rate limit. Alternately, you can generate a certificate through {option}enableACME. Note that this option does not create any certificates, nor it does add subdomains to existing ones – you will need to create them manually using .

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.package
documents.content: The kanboard package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.phpfpm.settings
documents.content: Options for kanboard's PHPFPM pool.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.settings
documents.content: Customize the default settings, refer to https://github.com/kanboard/kanboard/blob/main/config.default.php for details on supported values.

documents.title: Option: services.kanboard.user
documents.content: User under which Kanboard runs.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.client.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the Kanidm client.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.client.settings
documents.content: Configure Kanidm clients, needed for the PAM daemon. See the documentation and example configuration for possible values.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.client.settings.uri
documents.content: Address of the Kanidm server.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.package
documents.content: The kanidm package to use. Must be set to an explicit version.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.acceptInvalidCerts
documents.content: Whether to allow invalid certificates when provisioning the target instance. By default this is only allowed when the instanceUrl is localhost. This is dangerous when used with an external URL.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.adminPasswordFile
documents.content: Path to a file containing the admin password for kanidm. Do NOT use a file from the nix store here!

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.autoRemove
documents.content: Determines whether deleting an entity in this provisioning config should automatically cause them to be removed from kanidm, too. This works because the provisioning tool tracks all entities it has ever created. If this is set to false, you need to explicitly specify present = false to delete an entity.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable provisioning of groups, users and oauth2 resource servers.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.extraJsonFile
documents.content: A JSON file for provisioning persons, groups & systems. Options set in this file take precedence over values set using the other options. The files get deeply merged, and deduplicated. The accepted JSON schema can be found at https://github.com/oddlama/kanidm-provision#json-schema.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.groups
documents.content: Provisioning of kanidm groups

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.groups.<name>.members
documents.content: List of kanidm entities (persons, groups, ...) which are part of this group.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.groups.<name>.overwriteMembers
documents.content: Whether the member list should be overwritten each time (true) or appended (false). Append mode allows interactive group management in addition to the declared members. Also, future member removals cannot be reflected automatically in append mode.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.groups.<name>.present
documents.content: Whether to ensure that this group is present or absent.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.idmAdminPasswordFile
documents.content: Path to a file containing the idm admin password for kanidm. Do NOT use a file from the nix store here! If this is not given but provisioning is enabled, the idm_admin password will be reset on each restart.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.instanceUrl
documents.content: The instance url to which the provisioning tool should connect.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.persons
documents.content: Provisioning of kanidm persons

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.persons.<name>.displayName
documents.content: Display name

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.persons.<name>.groups
documents.content: List of groups this person should belong to.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.persons.<name>.legalName
documents.content: Full legal name

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.persons.<name>.mailAddresses
documents.content: Mail addresses. First given address is considered the primary address.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.persons.<name>.present
documents.content: Whether to ensure that this person is present or absent.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2
documents.content: Provisioning of oauth2 resource servers

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.allowInsecureClientDisablePkce
documents.content: Disable PKCE on this oauth2 resource server to work around insecure clients that may not support it. You should request the client to enable PKCE! Only for non-public clients.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.basicSecretFile
documents.content: The basic secret to use for this service. If null, the random secret generated by kanidm will not be touched. Do NOT use a path from the nix store here!

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.claimMaps
documents.content: Adds additional claims (and values) based on which kanidm groups an authenticating party belongs to. See Claim Maps for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.claimMaps.<name>.joinType
documents.content: Determines how multiple values are joined to create the claim value. See Claim Maps for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.claimMaps.<name>.valuesByGroup
documents.content: Maps kanidm groups to values for the claim.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.displayName
documents.content: Display name

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.enableLegacyCrypto
documents.content: Enable legacy crypto on this client. Allows JWT signing algorthms like RS256.

documents.title: Option: services.kanidm.provision.systems.oauth2.<name>.enableLocalhostRedirects
documents.content: Allow localhost redirects. Only for public clients.
