documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.createLocally
documents.content: Whether a database should be automatically created on the local host. Set this to false if you plan on provisioning a local database yourself. This has no effect if services.keycloak.database.host is customized.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.host
documents.content:
Hostname of the database to connect to.
For PostgreSQL, this can also be a path to a Unix socket directory (e.g., /run/postgresql) to use peer authentication. This requires adding junixsocket-common and junixsocket-native-common to .

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.name
documents.content:
Database name to use when connecting to an external or manually provisioned database; has no effect when a local database is automatically provisioned.
To use this with a local database, set to false and create the database and user manually.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.passwordFile
documents.content:
The path to a file containing the database password.
Not required when using Unix socket authentication (peer auth) by setting host to a socket path like /run/postgresql.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.port
documents.content: Port of the database to connect to.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.type
documents.content: The type of database Keycloak should connect to.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.useSSL
documents.content:
Whether the database connection should be secured by SSL / TLS.
Defaults to false for localhost and Unix socket connections.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.database.username
documents.content:
Username to use when connecting to an external or manually provisioned database; has no effect when a local database is automatically provisioned.
To use this with a local database, set to false and create the database and user manually.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the Keycloak identity and access management server.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.initialAdminPassword
documents.content:
Initial password set for the temporary admin user. The password is not stored safely and should be changed immediately in the admin panel.
See Admin bootstrap and recovery for details.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.package
documents.content: The keycloak package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.plugins
documents.content: Keycloak plugin jar, ear files or derivations containing them. Packaged plugins are available through pkgs.keycloak.plugins.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.realmFiles
documents.content: Realm files that the server is going to import during startup. If a realm already exists in the server, the import operation is skipped. Importing the master realm is not supported. All files are expected to be in json format. See the documentation for further information.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings
documents.content:
Configuration options corresponding to parameters set in {file}conf/keycloak.conf.
Most available options are documented at https://www.keycloak.org/server/all-config.
Options containing secret data should be set to an attribute set containing the attribute _secret - a string pointing to a file containing the value the option should be set to. See the example to get a better picture of this: in the resulting {file}conf/keycloak.conf file, the https-key-store-password key will be set to the contents of the {file}/run/keys/store_password file.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings.hostname
documents.content:
The hostname part of the public URL used as base for all frontend requests.
See https://www.keycloak.org/server/hostname for more information about hostname configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings.hostname-backchannel-dynamic
documents.content:
Enables dynamic resolving of backchannel URLs, including hostname, scheme, port and context path.
See https://www.keycloak.org/server/hostname for more information about hostname configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings.http-host
documents.content: On which address Keycloak should accept new connections.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings.http-port
documents.content: On which port Keycloak should listen for new HTTP connections.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings.http-relative-path
documents.content:
The path relative to / for serving resources.
::: {.note} In versions of Keycloak using Wildfly (<17), this defaulted to /auth. If upgrading from the Wildfly version of Keycloak, i.e. a NixOS version before 22.05, you'll likely want to set this to /auth to keep compatibility with your clients.
See https://www.keycloak.org/migration/migrating-to-quarkus for more information on migrating from Wildfly to Quarkus. :::

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.settings.https-port
documents.content: On which port Keycloak should listen for new HTTPS connections.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.sslCertificate
documents.content: The path to a PEM formatted certificate to use for TLS/SSL connections.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.sslCertificateKey
documents.content: The path to a PEM formatted private key to use for TLS/SSL connections.

documents.title: Option: services.keycloak.themes
documents.content:
Additional theme packages for Keycloak. Each theme is linked into subdirectory with a corresponding attribute name.
Theme packages consist of several subdirectories which provide different theme types: for example, account, login etc. After adding a theme to this option you can select it by its name in Keycloak administration console.

documents.title: Option: services.keyd.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable keyd, a key remapping daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.keyd.keyboards
documents.content: Configuration for one or more device IDs. Corresponding files in the /etc/keyd/ directory are created according to the name of the keys (like default or externalKeyboard).

documents.title: Option: services.keyd.keyboards.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration that is appended to the end of the file. Do not write ids section here, use a separate option for it. You can use this option to define compound layers that must always be defined after the layer they are comprised.

documents.title: Option: services.keyd.keyboards.<name>.ids
documents.content: Device identifiers, as shown by {manpage}keyd(1).

documents.title: Option: services.keyd.keyboards.<name>.settings
documents.content: Configuration, except ids section, that is written to {file}/etc/keyd/<keyboard>.conf. Appropriate names can be used to write non-alpha keys, for example "equal" instead of "=" sign (see https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/236622). See https://github.com/rvaiya/keyd how to configure.

documents.title: Option: services.keyd.package
documents.content: The keyd package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites
documents.content: Specification of one or more Kimai sites to serve

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.charset
documents.content: Database charset.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.createLocally
documents.content: Create the database and database user locally.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.host
documents.content: Database host address.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.name
documents.content: Database name.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.passwordFile

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.port
documents.content: Database host port.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.serverVersion
documents.content: MySQL exact version string. Not used if createdLocally is set, but must be set otherwise. See https://www.kimai.org/documentation/installation.html#column-table_name-in-where-clause-is-ambiguous for how to set this value, especially if you're using MariaDB.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.socket

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.database.user

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.environmentFile

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.package
documents.content: The kimai package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.poolConfig
documents.content: Options for the Kimai PHP pool. See the documentation on php-fpm.conf for details on configuration directives.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.sites.<name>.settings
documents.content: Structural Kimai's local.yaml configuration. Refer to https://www.kimai.org/documentation/local-yaml.html#localyaml for details.

documents.title: Option: services.kimai.webserver
documents.content:
The webserver to configure for the PHP frontend.
At the moment, only nginx is supported. PRs are welcome for support for other web servers.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.dataDir
documents.content: The Kismet data directory.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable kismet.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.extraConfig
documents.content: Literal Kismet config lines appended to the site config. Note that services.kismet.settings allows you to define all options here using Nix attribute sets.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.group
documents.content: The group to run Kismet as.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.httpd.address

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.httpd.enable

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.httpd.port

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.logTypes

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.package

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.serverDescription
documents.content: The description of the server.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.serverName
documents.content: The name of the server.

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.settings
documents.content: Options for Kismet. See: https://www.kismetwireless.net/docs/readme/configuring/configfiles/

documents.title: Option: services.kismet.user
documents.content: The user to run Kismet as.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.address
documents.content: Listen only on the specified IP address. Specify "ipv4", "ipv6" or "all" to listen on all IPv4, IPv6, or both types of addresses, respectively.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the kiwix-serve server.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.extraArgs
documents.content: Extra arguments to pass to kiwix-serve.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.library
documents.content:
A set of ZIM files to serve. The key is used as the name for the ZIM files (e.g. in the example, the files will be served as wikipedia.zim and nix.zim).
Exclusive with services.kiwix-serve.libraryPath.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.libraryPath
documents.content:
An XML library file listing ZIM files to serve. For more information, see https://wiki.kiwix.org/wiki/Kiwix-manage.
Exclusive with services.kiwix-serve.library.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to open the firewall for the configured port.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.package
documents.content: The kiwix-tools package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kiwix-serve.port
documents.content: The port on which to run kiwix-serve.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.apiSocket
documents.content: Path of the API socket to create.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.configDir
documents.content: Path to Klipper config file.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.configFile
documents.content: Path to default Klipper config.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Klipper, the 3D printer firmware.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.extraSettings
documents.content: Extra lines to append to the generated Klipper configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares
documents.content: Firmwares Klipper should manage

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares.<name>.configFile
documents.content: Path to firmware config which is generated using klipper-genconf

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares.<name>.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable building of firmware for manual flashing .

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares.<name>.enableKlipperFlash
documents.content: Whether to enable flashings scripts for firmware. This will add klipper-flash-$mcu scripts to your environment which can be called to flash the firmware. Please check the configs at klipper whether your board supports flashing via make flash .

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares.<name>.klipperFlashPackage
documents.content: Path to the built klipper-flash package.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares.<name>.package
documents.content: Path to the built firmware package.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.firmwares.<name>.serial
documents.content: Path to serial port this printer is connected to. Derived from service.klipper.settings by default.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.group
documents.content:
Group account under which Klipper runs.
If null is specified (default), a temporary user will be created by systemd.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.inputTTY
documents.content: Path of the virtual printer symlink to create.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.logFile
documents.content: Path of the file Klipper should log to. If null, it logs to stdout, which is not recommended by upstream.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.mutableConfig
documents.content:
Whether to manage the config outside of NixOS.
It will still be initialized with the defined NixOS config if the file doesn't already exist.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.octoprintIntegration
documents.content: Allows Octoprint to control Klipper.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.package
documents.content: The klipper package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.settings
documents.content: Configuration for Klipper. See the documentation for supported values.

documents.title: Option: services.klipper.user
documents.content:
User account under which Klipper runs.
If null is specified (default), a temporary user will be created by systemd.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable KMonad: an advanced keyboard manager.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.extraArgs
documents.content: Extra arguments to pass to KMonad.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards
documents.content: Keyboard configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.config
documents.content: Keyboard configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.defcfg.allowCommands
documents.content: Whether to enable keys to run shell commands.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.defcfg.compose.delay
documents.content: The delay (in milliseconds) between compose key sequences.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.defcfg.compose.key
documents.content: The (optional) compose key to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.defcfg.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable automatic generation of the defcfg block.
When this option is set to true, the config option for this keyboard should not include a defcfg block .

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.defcfg.fallthrough
documents.content: Whether to enable re-emitting unhandled key events.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.device
documents.content: Path to the keyboard's device file.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.enableHardening
documents.content:
Whether to enable systemd hardening.
::: {.note} If KMonad is used to execute shell commands, hardening may make some of them fail. :::

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.extraGroups
documents.content:
Extra permission groups to attach to the KMonad instance for this keyboard.
Since KMonad runs as an unprivileged user, it may sometimes need extra permissions in order to read the keyboard device file. If your keyboard's device file isn't in the input group, you'll need to list its group in this option.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.keyboards.<name>.name
documents.content: Keyboard name.

documents.title: Option: services.kmonad.package
documents.content: The KMonad package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable Use kmscon instead of autovt.
Kmscon is a simple terminal emulator based on linux kernel mode setting (KMS). It is an attempt to replace the in-kernel VT implementation with a userspace console. .

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.extraConfig
documents.content: Extra contents of the kmscon.conf file.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.extraOptions
documents.content: Extra flags to pass to kmscon.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.fonts
documents.content: Fonts used by kmscon, in order of priority.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.fonts.*.name
documents.content: Font name, as used by fontconfig.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.fonts.*.package
documents.content: Package providing the font.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.hwRender
documents.content: Whether to enable 3D hardware acceleration to render the console.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.package
documents.content: The kmscon package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.term
documents.content: Value for the TERM environment variable.

documents.title: Option: services.kmscon.useXkbConfig
documents.content: Whether to enable configure keymap from xserver keyboard settings..

documents.title: Option: services.knot-resolver.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable knot-resolver (version 6) domain name server. DNSSEC validation is turned on by default. If you want to use knot-resolver 5, please use services.kresd.

documents.title: Option: services.knot-resolver.managerPackage
documents.content: The knot-resolver-manager_6 package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.knot-resolver.settings
documents.content: Nix-based (RFC 42) configuration for Knot Resolver. For configuration reference (described as YAML) see https://www.knot-resolver.cz/documentation/latest/config-overview.html

documents.title: Option: services.knot-resolver.settings.network.listen
documents.content: List of interfaces to listen to and its configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.knot-resolver.settings.workers
documents.content: The number of running kresd (Knot Resolver daemon) workers. If set to 'auto', it is equal to number of CPUs available.

documents.title: Option: services.knot.checkConfig

documents.title: Option: services.knot.enable

documents.title: Option: services.knot.enableXDP
documents.content:
Extends the systemd unit with permissions to allow for the use of the eXpress Data Path (XDP).
::: {.note} Make sure to read up on functional limitations when running in XDP mode. :::

documents.title: Option: services.knot.extraArgs

documents.title: Option: services.knot.keyFiles
documents.content: A list of files containing additional configuration to be included using the include directive. This option allows to include configuration like TSIG keys without exposing them to the nix store readable to any process. Note that using this option will also disable configuration checks at build time.

documents.title: Option: services.knot.package
documents.content: The knot-dns package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.knot.settings
documents.content: Extra configuration as nix values.

documents.title: Option: services.knot.settingsFile
documents.content: As alternative to settings, you can provide whole configuration directly in the almost-YAML format of Knot DNS. You might want to utilize pkgs.writeText "knot.conf" "longConfigString" for this.

documents.title: Option: services.komga.enable

Komga configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.komga.user

documents.content: Whether to enable libinput.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelPointsFallback
documents.content: Sets the points of the fallback acceleration function. The value must be a list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelPointsMotion
documents.content: Sets the points of the (pointer) motion acceleration function. The value must be a list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelPointsScroll
documents.content: Sets the points of the scroll acceleration function. The value must be a list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelProfile
documents.content: Sets the pointer acceleration profile to the given profile. Permitted values are adaptive, flat, custom. Not all devices support this option or all profiles. If a profile is unsupported, the default profile for this is used. flat: Pointer motion is accelerated by a constant (device-specific) factor, depending on the current speed. adaptive: Pointer acceleration depends on the input speed. This is the default profile for most devices. custom: Allows the user to define a custom acceleration function. To define custom functions use the accelPoints<Fallback/Motion/Scroll> and accelStep<Fallback/Motion/Scroll> options.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelSpeed
documents.content: Cursor acceleration (how fast speed increases from minSpeed to maxSpeed). This only applies to the flat or adaptive profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelStepFallback
documents.content: Sets the step between the points of the fallback acceleration function. When a step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelStepMotion
documents.content: Sets the step between the points of the (pointer) motion acceleration function. When a step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.accelStepScroll
documents.content: Sets the step between the points of the scroll acceleration function. When a step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.additionalOptions
documents.content: Additional options for libinput mouse driver. See {manpage}libinput(4) for available options.";

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.buttonMapping
documents.content: Sets the logical button mapping for this device, see {manpage}XSetPointerMapping(3). The string must be a space-separated list of button mappings in the order of the logical buttons on the device, starting with button 1. The default mapping is "1 2 3 ... 32". A mapping of 0 deac‐ tivates the button. Multiple buttons can have the same mapping. Invalid mapping strings are discarded and the default mapping is used for all buttons. Buttons not specified in the user's mapping use the default mapping. See section BUTTON MAPPING for more details.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.calibrationMatrix
documents.content: A string of 9 space-separated floating point numbers. Sets the calibration matrix to the 3x3 matrix where the first row is (abc), the second row is (def) and the third row is (ghi).

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.clickMethod
documents.content: Enables a click method. Permitted values are none, buttonareas, clickfinger. Not all devices support all methods, if an option is unsupported, the default click method for this device is used.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.dev
documents.content: Path for mouse device. Set to null to apply to any auto-detected mouse.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.disableWhileTyping
documents.content: Disable input method while typing.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.horizontalScrolling
documents.content: Enables or disables horizontal scrolling. When disabled, this driver will discard any horizontal scroll events from libinput. This does not disable horizontal scroll events from libinput; it merely discards the horizontal axis from any scroll events.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.leftHanded
documents.content: Enables left-handed button orientation, i.e. swapping left and right buttons.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.middleEmulation
documents.content: Enables middle button emulation. When enabled, pressing the left and right buttons simultaneously produces a middle mouse button click.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.naturalScrolling
documents.content: Enables or disables natural scrolling behavior.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.scrollButton
documents.content: Designates a button as scroll button. If the ScrollMethod is button and the button is logically held down, x/y axis movement is converted into scroll events.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.scrollMethod
documents.content: Specify the scrolling method: twofinger, edge, button, or none

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.sendEventsMode
documents.content: Sets the send events mode to disabled, enabled, or disabled-on-external-mouse

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.tapping
documents.content: Enables or disables tap-to-click behavior.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.tappingButtonMap
documents.content: Set the button mapping for 1/2/3-finger taps to left/right/middle or left/middle/right, respectively.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.tappingDragLock
documents.content: Enables or disables drag lock during tapping behavior. When enabled, a finger up during tap- and-drag will not immediately release the button. If the finger is set down again within the timeout, the dragging process continues.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.mouse.transformationMatrix
documents.content: A string of 9 space-separated floating point numbers. Sets the transformation matrix to the 3x3 matrix where the first row is (abc), the second row is (def) and the third row is (ghi).

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelPointsFallback
documents.content: Sets the points of the fallback acceleration function. The value must be a list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelPointsMotion
documents.content: Sets the points of the (pointer) motion acceleration function. The value must be a list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelPointsScroll
documents.content: Sets the points of the scroll acceleration function. The value must be a list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelProfile
documents.content: Sets the pointer acceleration profile to the given profile. Permitted values are adaptive, flat, custom. Not all devices support this option or all profiles. If a profile is unsupported, the default profile for this is used. flat: Pointer motion is accelerated by a constant (device-specific) factor, depending on the current speed. adaptive: Pointer acceleration depends on the input speed. This is the default profile for most devices. custom: Allows the user to define a custom acceleration function. To define custom functions use the accelPoints<Fallback/Motion/Scroll> and accelStep<Fallback/Motion/Scroll> options.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelSpeed
documents.content: Cursor acceleration (how fast speed increases from minSpeed to maxSpeed). This only applies to the flat or adaptive profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelStepFallback
documents.content: Sets the step between the points of the fallback acceleration function. When a step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelStepMotion
documents.content: Sets the step between the points of the (pointer) motion acceleration function. When a step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.accelStepScroll
documents.content: Sets the step between the points of the scroll acceleration function. When a step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies to the custom profile.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.additionalOptions
documents.content: Additional options for libinput touchpad driver. See {manpage}libinput(4) for available options.";

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.buttonMapping
documents.content: Sets the logical button mapping for this device, see {manpage}XSetPointerMapping(3). The string must be a space-separated list of button mappings in the order of the logical buttons on the device, starting with button 1. The default mapping is "1 2 3 ... 32". A mapping of 0 deac‐ tivates the button. Multiple buttons can have the same mapping. Invalid mapping strings are discarded and the default mapping is used for all buttons. Buttons not specified in the user's mapping use the default mapping. See section BUTTON MAPPING for more details.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.calibrationMatrix
documents.content: A string of 9 space-separated floating point numbers. Sets the calibration matrix to the 3x3 matrix where the first row is (abc), the second row is (def) and the third row is (ghi).

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.clickMethod
documents.content: Enables a click method. Permitted values are none, buttonareas, clickfinger. Not all devices support all methods, if an option is unsupported, the default click method for this device is used.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.dev
documents.content: Path for touchpad device. Set to null to apply to any auto-detected touchpad.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.disableWhileTyping
documents.content: Disable input method while typing.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.horizontalScrolling
documents.content: Enables or disables horizontal scrolling. When disabled, this driver will discard any horizontal scroll events from libinput. This does not disable horizontal scroll events from libinput; it merely discards the horizontal axis from any scroll events.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.leftHanded
documents.content: Enables left-handed button orientation, i.e. swapping left and right buttons.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.middleEmulation
documents.content: Enables middle button emulation. When enabled, pressing the left and right buttons simultaneously produces a middle mouse button click.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.naturalScrolling
documents.content: Enables or disables natural scrolling behavior.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.scrollButton
documents.content: Designates a button as scroll button. If the ScrollMethod is button and the button is logically held down, x/y axis movement is converted into scroll events.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.scrollMethod
documents.content: Specify the scrolling method: twofinger, edge, button, or none

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.sendEventsMode
documents.content: Sets the send events mode to disabled, enabled, or disabled-on-external-mouse

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.tapping
documents.content: Enables or disables tap-to-click behavior.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.tappingButtonMap
documents.content: Set the button mapping for 1/2/3-finger taps to left/right/middle or left/middle/right, respectively.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.tappingDragLock
documents.content: Enables or disables drag lock during tapping behavior. When enabled, a finger up during tap- and-drag will not immediately release the button. If the finger is set down again within the timeout, the dragging process continues.

documents.title: Option: services.libinput.touchpad.transformationMatrix
documents.content: A string of 9 space-separated floating point numbers. Sets the transformation matrix to the 3x3 matrix where the first row is (abc), the second row is (def) and the third row is (ghi).

documents.title: Option: services.librechat.credentials

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.distributedPoller.group

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.distributedPoller.memcachedHost

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.distributedPoller.memcachedPort

documents.content: Hostname or IP of the rrdcached server.

documents.content: Enables the 1-Minute Polling. Changing this option will automatically convert your existing rrd files.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.environmentFile

documents.content: Additional config for LibreNMS that will be appended to the config.php. See https://github.com/librenms/librenms/blob/master/misc/config_definitions.json for possible options. Useful if you want to use PHP-Functions in your config.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.finalPackage

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.group

documents.content: The hostname to serve LibreNMS on.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.logDir
documents.content: Path of the LibreNMS logging directory.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx
documents.content: With this option, you can customize the nginx virtualHost settings.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
documents.content:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.
With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.acmeRoot
documents.content: Directory for the ACME challenge, which is public. Don't put certs or keys in here. Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.addSSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443).

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.default
documents.content: Makes this vhost the default.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.enableACME
documents.content: Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost. Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}useACMEHost.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.forceSSL
documents.content: Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) all plain HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.globalRedirect
documents.content: If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) to the given hostname.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol. Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given IP address / port. If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.http3
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.http3_hq
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that special application protocol support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.kTLS
documents.content: Whether to enable kTLS support. Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel. Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listen
documents.content:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host. IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets. Note: this option overrides addSSL and onlySSL.
If you only want to set the addresses manually and not the ports, take a look at listenAddresses.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.addr
documents.content: Listen address.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.extraParameters
documents.content: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.port
documents.content: Port number to listen on. If unset and the listen address is not a socket then nginx defaults to 80.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.proxyProtocol
documents.content: Enable PROXY protocol.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.ssl
documents.content: Enable SSL.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.listenAddresses
documents.content:
Listen addresses for this virtual host. Compared to listen this only sets the addresses and the ports are chosen automatically.
Note: This option overrides networking.enableIPv6

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations
documents.content: Declarative location config

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.alias

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the location verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.fastcgiParams
documents.content: FastCGI parameters to override. Unlike in the Nginx configuration file, overriding only some default parameters won't unset the default values for other parameters.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.index
documents.content: Adds index directive.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.priority
documents.content: Order of this location block in relation to the others in the vhost. The semantics are the same as with lib.mkOrder. Smaller values have a greater priority.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.proxyPass
documents.content: Adds proxy_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedProxySettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.proxyWebsockets
documents.content: Whether to support proxying websocket connections with HTTP/1.1.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.recommendedProxySettings
documents.content: Enable recommended proxy settings.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.recommendedUwsgiSettings
documents.content: Enable recommended uwsgi settings.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.return
documents.content: Adds a return directive, for e.g. redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.root
documents.content: Root directory for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.tryFiles
documents.content: Adds try_files directive.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.uwsgiPass
documents.content: Adds uwsgi_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedUwsgiSettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.onlySSL

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.quic

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.redirectCode
documents.content: HTTP status used by globalRedirect and forceSSL. Possible usecases include temporary (302, 307) redirects, keeping the request method and body (307, 308), or explicitly resetting the method to GET (303). See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.rejectSSL
documents.content: Whether to listen for and reject all HTTPS connections to this vhost. Useful in default server blocks to avoid serving the certificate for another vhost. Uses the ssl_reject_handshake directive available in nginx versions 1.19.4 and above.

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.reuseport

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.root

documents.title: Option: services.librenms.nginx.serverAliases

documents.title: Option: services.litestream.environmentFile
documents.content:
Environment file as defined in {manpage}systemd.exec(5).
Secrets may be passed to the service without adding them to the world-readable Nix store, by specifying placeholder variables as the option value in Nix and setting these variables accordingly in the environment file.
By default, Litestream will perform environment variable expansion within the config file before reading it. Any references to $VAR or ${VAR} formatted variables will be replaced with their environment variable values. If no value is set then it will be replaced with an empty string.
Note that this file needs to be available on the host on which this exporter is running.

documents.title: Option: services.livebook.environment
documents.content:
Environment variables to set.
Livebook is configured through the use of environment variables. The available configuration options can be found in the Livebook documentation.
Note that all environment variables set through this configuration parameter will be readable by anyone with access to the host machine. Therefore, sensitive information like {env}LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD or {env}LIVEBOOK_COOKIE should never be set using this configuration option, but should instead use . See the documentation for that option for more information.
Any environment variables specified in the will supersede environment variables specified in this option.

documents.title: Option: services.livebook.environmentFile
documents.content:
Additional environment file as defined in {manpage}systemd.exec(5).
Secrets like {env}LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD (which is used to specify the password needed to access the livebook site) or {env}LIVEBOOK_COOKIE (which is used to specify the cookie used to connect to the running Elixir system) may be passed to the service without making them readable to everyone with access to systemctl by using this configuration parameter.
Note that this file needs to be available on the host on which livebook is running.
For security purposes, this file should contain at least {env}LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD or {env}LIVEBOOK_TOKEN_ENABLED=false.
See the Livebook documentation and the configuration parameter for further options.

documents.title: Option: services.lldap.settings.force_ldap_user_pass_reset
documents.content:
Force reset of the admin password.
Set this setting to "always" to update the admin password when ldap_user_pass_file changes. Setting to "always" also means any password update in the UI will be overwritten next time the service restarts.
The difference between true and "always" is the former is intended for a one time fix while the latter is intended for a declarative workflow. In practice, the result is the same: the password gets reset. The only practical difference is the former outputs a warning message while the latter outputs an info message.

documents.title: Option: services.logind.settings.Login.KillUserProcesses
documents.content:
Specifies whether the processes of a user should be killed when the user logs out. If true, the scope unit corresponding to the session and all processes inside that scope will be terminated. If false, the scope is "abandoned" (see {manpage}systemd.scope(5)), and processes are not killed.
See {manpage}logind.conf(5) for more details.
Defaulted to false in nixpkgs because many tools that rely on persistent user processes—like tmux, screen, mosh, VNC, nohup, and more — would break by the systemd-default behavior.

documents.title: Option: services.logrotate.checkConfig
documents.content:
Whether the config should be checked at build time.
Some options are not checkable at build time because of the build sandbox: for example, the test does not know about existing files and system users are not known. These limitations mean we must adjust the file for tests (missingok is forced and users are replaced by dummy users), so tests are complemented by a logrotate-checkconf service that is enabled by default. This extra check can be disabled by disabling it at the systemd level with the {option}systemd.services.logrotate-checkconf.enable option.
Conversely there are still things that might make this check fail incorrectly (e.g. a file path where we don't have access to intermediate directories): in this case you can disable the failing check with this option.

The format for capability clauses is described in the “TEXTUAL REPRESENTATION” section of the {manpage}cap_from_text(3) manual page. ::: {.note} cap_setpcap, which is required for the wrapper program to be able to raise caps into the Ambient set is NOT raised to the Ambient set so that the real program cannot modify its own capabilities!! documents.title: Option: services.mastodon.configureNginx
documents.content:
Configure nginx as a reverse proxy for mastodon. Note that this makes some assumptions on your setup, and sets settings that will affect other virtualHosts running on your nginx instance, if any. Alternatively you can configure a reverse-proxy of your choice to serve these paths:
/ -> ${pkgs.mastodon}/public
/ -> 127.0.0.1:{{ webPort }} (If there was no file in the directory above.)
/system/ -> /var/lib/mastodon/public-system/
/api/v1/streaming/ -> 127.0.0.1:{{ streamingPort }}

documents.title: Option: services.matrix-synapse.extras
documents.content:

documents.title: Option: services.matrix-synapse.log
documents.content:
Default configuration for the loggers used by matrix-synapse and its workers. The defaults are added with the default priority which means that these will be merged with additional declarations. These additional declarations also take precedence over the defaults when declared with at least normal priority. For instance the log-level for synapse and its workers can be changed like this:
And another field can be added like this:
Additionally, the field handlers.journal.SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER will be added to each log config, i.e.
synapse for matrix-synapse.service
synapse-<worker name> for matrix-synapse-worker-<worker name>.service

This is only done if this option has a handlers.journal field declared.
To discard all settings declared by this option for each worker and synapse, lib.mkForce can be used.
To discard all settings declared by this option for a single worker or synapse only, or can be used.

documents.title: Option: services.matrix-synapse.package
documents.content:
Reference to the matrix-synapse wrapper with all extras (e.g. for oidc or saml2) added to the PYTHONPATH of all executables.
This option is useful to reference the "final" matrix-synapse package that's actually used by matrix-synapse.service. For instance, when using workers, it's possible to run ${config.services.matrix-synapse.package}/bin/synapse_worker and no additional PYTHONPATH needs to be specified for extras or plugins configured via services.matrix-synapse.
However, this means that this option is supposed to be only declared by the services.matrix-synapse module itself and is thus read-only. In order to modify matrix-synapse itself, use an overlay to override pkgs.matrix-synapse-unwrapped.

This option is useful as the actual parent unit for all matrix-synapse processes changes when configuring workers.

documents.title: Option: services.matrix-synapse.workers
documents.content:
Options for configuring workers. Worker support will be enabled if at least one worker is configured here.
See the worker documention for possible options for each worker. Worker-specific options overriding the shared homeserver configuration can be specified here for each worker.
::: {.note} Worker support will add a replication listener on port 9093 to the main synapse process using the default value of services.matrix-synapse.settings.listeners and configure that listener as services.matrix-synapse.settings.instance_map.main. If you set either of those options, make sure to configure a replication listener yourself.
A redis server is required for running workers. A local one can be enabled using services.matrix-synapse.configureRedisLocally.
Workers also require a proper reverse proxy setup to direct incoming requests to the appropriate process. See the reverse proxy documentation for a general reverse proxying setup and the worker documentation for the available endpoints per worker application. :::

The environment variable values can be prefixed with json:: to have them be parsed as JSON. For example, login_shared_secret_map can be set as follows: MAUTRIX_TELEGRAM_BRIDGE_LOGIN_SHARED_SECRET_MAP=json::{"example.com":"secret"}.

documents.title: Option: services.movim.h2o.tls.recommendations
documents.content:
By default, H2O, without prejudice, will use as many TLS versions & cipher suites as it & the TLS library (OpenSSL) can support. The user is expected to hone settings for the security of their server. Setting some constraints is recommended, & if unsure about what TLS settings to use, this option gives curated TLS settings recommendations from Mozilla’s ‘SSL Configuration Generator’ project (see https://ssl-config.mozilla.org) or read more at Mozilla’s Wiki (see https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Server_Side_TLS).
modern : Services with clients that support TLS 1.3 & don’t need backward compatibility
intermediate : General-purpose servers with a variety of clients, recommended for almost all systems
The default for all virtual hosts can be set with services.h2o.defaultTLSRecommendations, but this value can be overridden on a per-host basis using services.h2o.hosts..tls.recommmendations. The settings will also be overidden by manual values set with services.settings.h2o.hosts..tls.extraSettings.
NOTE: older/weaker ciphers might require overriding the OpenSSL version of H2O (such as openssl_legacy). This can be done with sevices.settings.h2o.package.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.blacklist
documents.content: This section defines which devices should be excluded from the multipath topology discovery.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.blacklist_exceptions
documents.content: This section defines which devices should be included in the multipath topology discovery, despite being listed in the blacklist section.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.defaults
documents.content: This section defines default values for attributes which are used whenever no values are given in the appropriate device or multipath sections.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices
documents.content: This option allows you to define arrays for use in multipath groups.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.alias_prefix
documents.content: The user_friendly_names prefix to use for this device type, instead of the default mpath

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.all_tg_pt
documents.content: Set the 'all targets ports' flag when registering keys with mpathpersist

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.deferred_remove
documents.content: If set to "yes", multipathd will do a deferred remove instead of a regular remove when the last path device has been deleted. This means that if the multipath device is still in use, it will be freed when the last user closes it. If path is added to the multipath device before the last user closes it, the deferred remove will be canceled.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.delay_wait_checks
documents.content: This option is deprecated, and mapped to san_path_err_recovery_time

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.delay_watch_checks
documents.content: This option is deprecated, and mapped to san_path_err_forget_rate

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.detect_checker
documents.content: If set to "yes", multipath will try to detect if the device supports SCSI-3 ALUA. If so, the device will automatically use the tur checker. If set to "no", the checker will be selected as usual.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.detect_prio
documents.content: If set to "yes", multipath will try to detect if the device supports SCSI-3 ALUA. If so, the device will automatically use the sysfs prioritizer if the required sysf attributes access_state and preferred_path are supported, or the alua prioritizer if not. If set to "no", the prioritizer will be selected as usual.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.dev_loss_tmo
documents.content: Specify the number of seconds the SCSI layer will wait after a problem has been detected on a FC remote port before removing it from the system. This can be set to "infinity" which sets it to the max value of 2147483647 seconds, or 68 years. It will be automatically adjusted to the overall retry interval no_path_retry * polling_interval if a number of retries is given with no_path_retry and the overall retry interval is longer than the specified dev_loss_tmo value. The Linux kernel will cap this value to 600 if fast_io_fail_tmo is not set.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.failback
documents.content: Tell multipathd how to manage path group failback. Quote integers as strings

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.fast_io_fail_tmo
documents.content: Specify the number of seconds the SCSI layer will wait after a problem has been detected on a FC remote port before failing I/O to devices on that remote port. This should be smaller than dev_loss_tmo. Setting this to "off" will disable the timeout. Quote integers as strings.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.features
documents.content: Specify any device-mapper features to be used

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.flush_on_last_del
documents.content: If set to "yes" multipathd will disable queueing when the last path to a device has been deleted.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.getuid_callout
documents.content: (Superseded by uid_attribute) The default program and args to callout to obtain a unique path identifier. Should be specified with an absolute path.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.ghost_delay
documents.content: Sets the number of seconds that multipath will wait after creating a device with only ghost paths before marking it ready for use in systemd

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.hardware_handler
documents.content: The hardware handler to use for this device type

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.marginal_path_double_failed_time
documents.content: One of the four parameters of supporting path check based on accounting IO error such as intermittent error

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.marginal_path_err_rate_threshold

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.marginal_path_err_recheck_gap_time
documents.content: One of the four parameters of supporting path check based on accounting IO error such as intermittent error

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.marginal_path_err_sample_time
documents.content: One of the four parameters of supporting path check based on accounting IO error such as intermittent error

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.max_sectors_kb
documents.content: Sets the max_sectors_kb device parameter on all path devices and the multipath device to the specified value

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.no_path_retry
documents.content: Specify what to do when all paths are down. Quote integers as strings

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.path_checker
documents.content: The default method used to determine the paths state

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.path_grouping_policy
documents.content: The default path grouping policy to apply to unspecified multipaths

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.path_selector
documents.content: The default path selector algorithm to use; they are offered by the kernel multipath target

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.prio
documents.content: The name of the path priority routine

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.prio_args
documents.content: Arguments to pass to to the prio function

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.product
documents.content: Regular expression to match the product name

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.product_blacklist
documents.content: Products with the given vendor matching this string are blacklisted

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.revision
documents.content: Regular expression to match the product revision

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.rr_min_io
documents.content: Number of I/O requests to route to a path before switching to the next in the same path group. This is only for Block I/O (BIO) based multipath and only apply to round-robin path_selector.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.rr_min_io_rq
documents.content: Number of I/O requests to route to a path before switching to the next in the same path group. This is only for Request based multipath and only apply to round-robin path_selector.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.rr_weight
documents.content: If set to priorities the multipath configurator will assign path weights as "path prio * rr_min_io".

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.san_path_err_forget_rate
documents.content: If set to a value greater than 0, multipathd will check whether the path failures has exceeded the san_path_err_threshold within this many checks i.e san_path_err_forget_rate. If so we will not reinstante the path till san_path_err_recovery_time.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.san_path_err_recovery_time
documents.content: If set to a value greater than 0, multipathd will make sure that when path failures has exceeded the san_path_err_threshold within san_path_err_forget_rate then the path will be placed in failed state for san_path_err_recovery_time duration. Once san_path_err_recovery_time has timeout we will reinstante the failed path. san_path_err_recovery_time value should be in secs.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.san_path_err_threshold
documents.content: If set to a value greater than 0, multipathd will watch paths and check how many times a path has been failed due to errors.If the number of failures on a particular path is greater then the san_path_err_threshold, then the path will not reinstate till san_path_err_recovery_time. These path failures should occur within a san_path_err_forget_rate checks, if not we will consider the path is good enough to reinstantate.

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.skip_kpartx
documents.content: If set to yes, kpartx will not automatically create partitions on the device

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.uid_attribute
documents.content: The udev attribute providing a unique path identifier (WWID)

documents.title: Option: services.multipath.devices.*.user_friendly_names
documents.content: If set to "yes", using the bindings file /etc/multipath/bindings to assign a persistent and unique alias to the multipath, in the form of mpath. If set to "no" use the WWID as the alias. In either case this be will be overridden by any specific aliases in the multipaths section.

documents.title: Option: services.munin-cron.enable
documents.content:
Enable munin-cron. Takes care of all heavy lifting to collect data from nodes and draws graphs to html. Runs munin-update, munin-limits, munin-graphs and munin-html in that order.
HTML output is in {file}/var/www/munin/, configure your favourite webserver to serve static files.

documents.title: Option: services.munin-cron.extraCSS
documents.content: Custom styling for the HTML that munin-cron generates. This will be appended to the CSS files used by munin-cron and will thus take precedence over the builtin styles.

documents.title: Option: services.munin-cron.extraGlobalConfig
documents.content: {file}munin.conf extra global configuration. See https://guide.munin-monitoring.org/en/latest/reference/munin.conf.html. Useful to setup notifications, see https://guide.munin-monitoring.org/en/latest/tutorial/alert.html

documents.title: Option: services.munin-cron.hosts
documents.content: Definitions of hosts of nodes to collect data from. Needs at least one host for cron to succeed. See https://guide.munin-monitoring.org/en/latest/reference/munin.conf.html

documents.title: Option: services.munin-node.disabledPlugins
documents.content:
Munin plugins to disable, even if munin-node-configure --suggest tries to enable them. To disable a wildcard plugin, use an actual wildcard, as in the example.
munin_stats is disabled by default as it tries to read /var/log/munin/munin-update.log for timing information, and the NixOS build of Munin does not write this file.

documents.title: Option: services.munin-node.enable
documents.content:
Enable Munin Node agent. Munin node listens on 0.0.0.0 and by default accepts connections only from 127.0.0.1 for security reasons.
See https://guide.munin-monitoring.org/en/latest/architecture/index.html.

documents.title: Option: services.munin-node.extraAutoPlugins
documents.content:
Additional Munin plugins to autoconfigure, using munin-node-configure --suggest. These should be the actual paths to the plugin files (or directories containing them), not just their names.
If you want to manually enable individual plugins instead, use {option}services.munin-node.extraPlugins.
Note that only plugins that have the 'autoconfig' capability will do anything if listed here, since plugins that cannot autoconfigure won't be automatically enabled by munin-node-configure.
Plugins will be copied into the Nix store, and it will attempt to modify them to run properly by fixing hardcoded references to /bin, /usr/bin, /sbin, and /usr/sbin.

documents.title: Option: services.munin-node.extraConfig
documents.content: {file}munin-node.conf extra configuration. See https://guide.munin-monitoring.org/en/latest/reference/munin-node.conf.html

documents.title: Option: services.munin-node.extraPluginConfig
documents.content: {file}plugin-conf.d extra plugin configuration. See https://guide.munin-monitoring.org/en/latest/plugin/use.html

documents.title: Option: services.munin-node.extraPlugins
documents.content:
Additional Munin plugins to activate. Keys are the name of the plugin symlink, values are the path to the underlying plugin script. You can use the same plugin script multiple times (e.g. for wildcard plugins).
Note that these plugins do not participate in autoconfiguration. If you want to autoconfigure additional plugins, use {option}services.munin-node.extraAutoPlugins.
Plugins enabled in this manner take precedence over autoconfigured plugins.
Plugins will be copied into the Nix store, and it will attempt to modify them to run properly by fixing hardcoded references to /bin, /usr/bin, /sbin, and /usr/sbin.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.allowHtml
documents.content: Allow HTML in client messages, comments, and channel descriptions.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.autobanAttempts

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.autobanTime
documents.content: The amount of time an IP ban lasts (in seconds).

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.autobanTimeframe
documents.content: Timeframe in which a client can connect without being banned for repeated attempts (in seconds).

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.bandwidth
documents.content: Maximum bandwidth (in bits per second) that clients may send speech at.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.bonjour
documents.content: Whether to enable Bonjour auto-discovery, which allows clients over your LAN to automatically discover Mumble servers.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.clientCertRequired
documents.content: Whether to enable requiring clients to authenticate via certificates.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.dbus
documents.content: Enable D-Bus remote control. Set to the bus you want Murmur to connect to.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.enable

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.environmentFile
documents.content:
Environment file as defined in {manpage}systemd.exec(5).
Secrets may be passed to the service without adding them to the world-readable Nix store, by specifying placeholder variables as the option value in Nix and setting these variables accordingly in the environment file.
Note that this file needs to be available on the host on which murmur is running.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.extraConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration to put into murmur.ini.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.group
documents.content: The name of an existing group to use to run the service. If not specified, the default group will be created.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.hostName
documents.content: Host to bind to. Defaults binding on all addresses.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.imgMsgLength

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.logDays
documents.content: How long to store RPC logs for in the database. Set 0 to keep logs forever, or -1 to disable DB logging.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.logToFile
documents.content: Whether to enable logging to a file instead of journald, which is stored in /var/log/murmur.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to enable opening ports in the firewall for the Mumble server.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.package

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.password
documents.content: Required password to join server, if specified.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.port
documents.content: Ports to bind to (UDP and TCP).

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.registerHostname
documents.content: DNS hostname where your server can be reached. This is only needed if you want your server to be accessed by its hostname and not IP - but the name must resolve on the internet properly.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.registerName
documents.content: Public server registration name, and also the name of the Root channel. Even if you don't publicly register your server, you probably still want to set this.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.registerPassword
documents.content: Public server registry password, used authenticate your server to the registry to prevent impersonation; required for subsequent registry updates.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.registerUrl
documents.content: URL website for your server.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.sendVersion

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.stateDir
documents.content: Directory to store data for the server.

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.textMsgLength

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.tls.caPath

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.tls.certPath

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.tls.keyPath

documents.title: Option: services.murmur.tls.useACMEHost
documents.content: Host of an existing Let's Encrypt certificate to use for TLS. Make sure that the certificate directory is readable by the murmur user or group. Note that this option does not create any certificates and it doesn't add subdomains to existing ones – you will need to create them manually using {option}security.acme.certs.

documents.title: Option: services.mympd.enable

documents.title: Option: services.mympd.extraGroups

documents.title: Option: services.mympd.settings
documents.content:
Manages the configuration files declaratively. For all the configuration options, see https://jcorporation.github.io/myMPD/020-configuration/configuration-files.
Each key represents the "File" column from the upstream configuration table, and the value is the content of that file.

documents.title: Option: services.mympd.settings.http_port
documents.content:
The HTTP port where mympd's web interface will be available.
The HTTPS/SSL port can be configured via {option}config.

documents.title: Option: services.mympd.settings.ssl
documents.content:
Whether to enable listening on the SSL port.
Refer to https://jcorporation.github.io/myMPD/020-configuration/configuration-files#ssl-options for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.configFile
documents.content: Override the configuration file used by MySQL. By default, NixOS generates one automatically from {option}services.mysql.settings.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.dataDir
documents.content:
The data directory for MySQL.
::: {.note} If left as the default value of /var/lib/mysql this directory will automatically be created before the MySQL server starts, otherwise you are responsible for ensuring the directory exists with appropriate ownership and permissions. :::

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable MySQL server.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.ensureDatabases
documents.content: Ensures that the specified databases exist. This option will never delete existing databases, especially not when the value of this option is changed. This means that databases created once through this option or otherwise have to be removed manually.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.ensureUsers
documents.content: Ensures that the specified users exist and have at least the ensured permissions. The MySQL users will be identified using Unix socket authentication. This authenticates the Unix user with the same name only, and that without the need for a password. This option will never delete existing users or remove permissions, especially not when the value of this option is changed. This means that users created and permissions assigned once through this option or otherwise have to be removed manually.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.ensureUsers.*.ensurePermissions
documents.content:
Permissions to ensure for the user, specified as attribute set. The attribute names specify the database and tables to grant the permissions for, separated by a dot. You may use wildcards here. The attribute values specfiy the permissions to grant. You may specify one or multiple comma-separated SQL privileges here.
For more information on how to specify the target and on which privileges exist, see the GRANT syntax. The attributes are used as GRANT ${attrName} ON ${attrValue}.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.ensureUsers.*.name
documents.content: Name of the user to ensure.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.clusterAddress
documents.content: Full Galera cluster connection string. If nodeAddresses is set, this will be auto-generated, but you can override it with a custom value. Format is typically 'gcomm://node1,node2,node3' with optional parameters.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.clusterPassword
documents.content: Optional password for securing cluster communications. If provided, it will be used in the clusterAddress for authentication between nodes.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable MariaDB Galera Cluster.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.localAddress
documents.content: IP address or hostname of this node that will be used for cluster communication. Must be reachable by all other nodes.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.localName
documents.content: The unique name that identifies this particular node within the cluster. Each node must have a different name.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.name

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.nodeAddresses

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.package

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.galeraCluster.sstMethod
