documents.title: Option: services.mysql.group
documents.content:
Group account under which MySQL runs.
::: {.note} If left as the default value this group will automatically be created on system activation, otherwise you are responsible for ensuring the user exists before the MySQL service starts. :::

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.initialDatabases
documents.content: List of database names and their initial schemas that should be used to create databases on the first startup of MySQL. The schema attribute is optional: If not specified, an empty database is created.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.initialDatabases.*.name
documents.content: The name of the database to create.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.initialDatabases.*.schema
documents.content: The initial schema of the database; if null (the default), an empty database is created.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.initialScript
documents.content: A file containing SQL statements to be executed on the first startup. Can be used for granting certain permissions on the database.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.package
documents.content: Which MySQL derivation to use. MariaDB packages are supported too.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.masterHost
documents.content: Hostname of the MySQL master server.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.masterPassword
documents.content: Password of the MySQL replication user.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.masterPort
documents.content: Port number on which the MySQL master server runs.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.masterUser
documents.content: Username of the MySQL replication user.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.role
documents.content: Role of the MySQL server instance.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.serverId
documents.content: Id of the MySQL server instance. This number must be unique for each instance.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.replication.slaveHost
documents.content: Hostname of the MySQL slave server.

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.settings
documents.content:
MySQL configuration. Refer to https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/server-system-variables.html, https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/server-system-variables.html, and https://mariadb.com/kb/en/server-system-variables/ for details on supported values.
::: {.note} MySQL configuration options such as --quick should be treated as boolean options and provided values such as true, false, 1, or 0. See the provided example below. :::

documents.title: Option: services.mysql.user
documents.content:
User account under which MySQL runs.
::: {.note} If left as the default value this user will automatically be created on system activation, otherwise you are responsible for ensuring the user exists before the MySQL service starts. :::

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.calendar
documents.content: Configured when to run the backup service systemd unit (DayOfWeek Year-Month-Day Hour:Minute:Second).

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.compressionAlg
documents.content: Compression algorithm to use for database dumps.

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.compressionLevel
documents.content:
Compression level to use for gzip, xz or zstd.
For gzip: 1-9
For xz: 0-9
For zstd: 1-19

:::{.note} If compression level is also specified in gzipOptions, the gzipOptions value will be overwritten :::

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.databases
documents.content: List of database names to dump.

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable MySQL backups.

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.gzipOptions
documents.content: Command line options to use when invoking gzip. Only used when compression is set to "gzip". If compression level is specified both here and in compressionLevel, the compressionLevel value will take precedence.

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.location
documents.content: Location to put the compressed MySQL database dumps.

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.singleTransaction
documents.content: Whether to create database dump in a single transaction. Can be either a boolean for all databases or a list of database names.

documents.title: Option: services.mysqlBackup.user
documents.content: User to be used to perform backup.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.customNodes
documents.content: List of custom n8n community node packages to load. Each package is expected to be an npm package with an n8n.nodes entry in its package.json. The packages are made available to n8n via the N8N_CUSTOM_EXTENSIONS environment variable.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable n8n server.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment
documents.content:
Environment variables to pass to the n8n service. See https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/configuration/environment-variables/ for available options.
Environment variables ending with _FILE are automatically handled as secrets: they are loaded via systemd credentials for secure access with DynamicUser=true.
This can be useful to pass secrets via tools like agenix or sops-nix.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.GENERIC_TIMEZONE
documents.content: The n8n instance timezone. Important for schedule nodes (such as Cron).

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_DIAGNOSTICS_ENABLED
documents.content: Whether to share selected, anonymous telemetry with n8n. Note that if you set this to false, you can't enable Ask AI in the Code node.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_PORT
documents.content: The HTTP port n8n runs on.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_RUNNERS_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE
documents.content:
Path to a file containing the shared authentication token used between the n8n server (task broker) and the task runners.
This option is required when {option}services.n8n.taskRunners.enable is true. The file should be readable by the service and not stored in the Nix store. Use tools like agenix or sops-nix to manage this secret.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_RUNNERS_BROKER_LISTEN_ADDRESS
documents.content: Address the task broker listens on.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_RUNNERS_BROKER_PORT
documents.content: Port the task broker listens on for task runner connections.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_USER_FOLDER
documents.content: Provide the path where n8n will create the .n8n folder. This directory stores user-specific data, such as database file and encryption key.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.environment.N8N_VERSION_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED
documents.content: When enabled, n8n sends notifications of new versions and security updates.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.openFirewall
documents.content: Open ports in the firewall for the n8n web interface.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.package
documents.content: The n8n package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable n8n task runners for sandboxed Code node execution.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.environment
documents.content:
Environment variables for the task runner launcher and runners. These are common to all runners and passed via allowed-env in the launcher config. See https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/configuration/environment-variables/task-runners/ for available options.
Environment variables ending with _FILE are automatically handled as secrets: they are loaded via systemd credentials for secure access with DynamicUser=true.
Note: The authentication token should be set via {option}services.n8n.environment.N8N_RUNNERS_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.environment.N8N_RUNNERS_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE
documents.content: Path to the authentication token file for the task runner.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.environment.N8N_RUNNERS_TASK_BROKER_URI
documents.content: URI of the n8n task broker that the runner connects to.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.launcherPackage
documents.content: The n8n-task-runner-launcher package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.runners
documents.content: Configuration for individual task runners.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.runners.<name>.args
documents.content: Additional command-line arguments to pass to the task runner.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.runners.<name>.command
documents.content: Command to execute for this runner.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.runners.<name>.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the ‹name› task runner. Only takes effect when {option}services.n8n.taskRunners.enable is true.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.runners.<name>.environment
documents.content: Environment variables specific to this task runner.

documents.title: Option: services.n8n.taskRunners.runners.<name>.healthCheckPort
documents.content: Port for the runner's health check server.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.cgiConfigFile
documents.content: Derivation for the configuration file of Nagios CGI scripts that can be used in web servers for running the Nagios web interface.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Nagios to monitor your system or network.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.enableWebInterface
documents.content: Whether to enable the Nagios web interface. You should also enable Apache ({option}services.httpd.enable).

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.extraConfig
documents.content: Configuration to add to /etc/nagios.cfg

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.mainConfigFile
documents.content: If non-null, overrides the main configuration file of Nagios.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.objectDefs
documents.content: A list of Nagios object configuration files that must define the hosts, host groups, services and contacts for the network that you want Nagios to monitor.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.plugins
documents.content: Packages to be added to the Nagios {env}PATH. Typically used to add plugins, but can be anything.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.validateConfig
documents.content: if true, the syntax of the nagios configuration file is checked at build time

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost
documents.content: Apache configuration can be done by adapting {option}services.httpd.virtualHosts. See for further information.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.acmeRoot
documents.content: Directory for the acme challenge which is PUBLIC, don't put certs or keys in here. Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.addSSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443).

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.adminAddr
documents.content: E-mail address of the server administrator.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.documentRoot
documents.content: The path of Apache's document root directory. If left undefined, an empty directory in the Nix store will be used as root.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.enableACME
documents.content: Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost. Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}useACMEHost.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.enableUserDir
documents.content: Whether to enable serving {file}~/public_html as /~«username».

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to httpd.conf verbatim. They will go after directories and directory aliases defined by default.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.forceSSL
documents.content: Whether to add a separate nginx server block that permanently redirects (301) all plain HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.globalRedirect
documents.content: If set, all requests for this host are redirected permanently to the given URL.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.hostName
documents.content: Canonical hostname for the server.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTP 2. HTTP/2 is supported in all multi-processing modules that come with httpd. However, if you use the prefork mpm, there will be severe restrictions. Refer to https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/howto/http2.html#mpm-config for details.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.listen
documents.content:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.
::: {.note} This option overrides addSSL, forceSSL and onlySSL.
If you only want to set the addresses manually and not the ports, take a look at listenAddresses. :::

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.listen.*.ip
documents.content: IP to listen on. 0.0.0.0 for IPv4 only, * for all.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.listen.*.port
documents.content: Port to listen on

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.listen.*.ssl
documents.content: Whether to enable SSL (https) support.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.listenAddresses
documents.content: Listen addresses for this virtual host. Compared to listen this only sets the addresses and the ports are chosen automatically.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.locations
documents.content: Declarative location config. See https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/core.html#location for details.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.locations.<name>.alias
documents.content: Alias directory for requests. See https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/mod_alias.html#alias.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.locations.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the location verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.locations.<name>.index
documents.content: Adds DirectoryIndex directive. See https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/mod_dir.html#directoryindex.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.locations.<name>.priority
documents.content: Order of this location block in relation to the others in the vhost. The semantics are the same as with lib.mkOrder. Smaller values have a greater priority.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.locations.<name>.proxyPass
documents.content: Sets up a simple reverse proxy as described by https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/howto/reverse_proxy.html#simple.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.logFormat
documents.content: Log format for Apache's log files. Possible values are: combined, common, referer, agent.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.onlySSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS and reject plain HTTP connections. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on port 443.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.robotsEntries
documents.content: Specification of pages to be ignored by web crawlers. See http://www.robotstxt.org/ for details.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.servedDirs
documents.content: This option provides a simple way to serve static directories.

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.servedFiles
documents.content:
This option provides a simple way to serve individual, static files.
::: {.note} This option has been deprecated and will be removed in a future version of NixOS. You can achieve the same result by making use of the locations.<name>.alias option. :::

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.serverAliases

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.sslServerCert

documents.title: Option: services.nagios.virtualHost.sslServerKey
documents.content: Path to server SSL certificate key.

documents.content: A host of an existing Let's Encrypt certificate to use. This is useful if you have many subdomains and want to avoid hitting the rate limit. Alternately, you can generate a certificate through {option}enableACME. Note that this option does not create any certificates, nor it does add subdomains to existing ones – you will need to create them manually using .

documents.title: Option: services.namecoind.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable namecoind, Namecoin client.

documents.title: Option: services.namecoind.extraNodes
documents.content: List of additional peer IP addresses to connect to.

documents.content: Key file for securing RPC connections.

documents.content: Password for RPC connections.

documents.title: Option: services.namecoind.rpc.user
documents.content: User name for RPC connections.

documents.title: Option: services.namecoind.wallet

Binary cache URL to connect to.
The URL format is compatible with the nix remote url style, such as:
http://, https:// for binary caches via HTTP or HTTPS
s3:// for binary caches stored in Amazon S3
gs:// for binary caches stored in Google Cloud Storage

documents.title: Option: services.nar-serve.domain
documents.content:
When set, enables the feature of serving . on top of /nix/store/-.
Useful to preview static websites where paths are absolute.

The NATS data directory. Only used if JetStream is enabled, for storing stream metadata and messages.
If left as the default value this directory will automatically be created before the NATS server starts, otherwise the sysadmin is responsible for ensuring the directory exists with appropriate ownership and permissions.

documents.title: Option: services.nats.group

documents.title: Option: services.nats.jetstream

documents.title: Option: services.nats.user
documents.content: User account under which NATS runs.

documents.title: Option: services.nats.validateConfig
documents.content: If true, validate nats config at build time. When the config can't be checked during build time, for example when it includes other files, disable this option.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Navidrome music server.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.finalPackage
documents.content: The final navidrome package including all selected plugins.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.group
documents.content: Group under which Navidrome runs.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to open the TCP port in the firewall

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.package
documents.content: The navidrome package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.plugins

documents.content: Configuration for Navidrome, see https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/configuration-options/ for supported values.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.settings.Address
documents.content: Address to run Navidrome on.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.settings.EnableInsightsCollector
documents.content: Enable anonymous usage data collection, see https://www.navidrome.org/docs/getting-started/insights/ for details.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.settings.Plugins.Enabled
documents.content: Enable plugin support in navidrome.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.settings.Plugins.Folder

The folder containing navidrome plugins.

documents.title: Option: services.navidrome.user
documents.content: User under which Navidrome runs.

documents.content: Path to the file containing the KSK public key. The key can be generated using the dnssec-keygen command, provided by the package bind as follows:

documents.title: Option: services.ncdns.dnssec.keys.zonePublic
documents.content: Path to the file containing the ZSK public key. The key can be generated using the dnssec-keygen command, provided by the package bind as follows:

documents.title: Option: services.ncps.analytics.reporting.enable

documents.title: Option: services.ncps.analytics.reporting.samples

documents.content: Network that we proxy. (Legacy option, use services.ndppd.proxies.<interface>.rules.<network> instead)

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies
documents.content: This sets up a listener, that will listen for any Neighbor Solicitation messages, and respond to them according to a set of rules.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.interface
documents.content: Listen for any Neighbor Solicitation messages on this interface, and respond to them according to a set of rules. Defaults to the name of the attrset.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.router
documents.content: Turns on or off the router flag for Neighbor Advertisement Messages.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.rules
documents.content: This is a rule that the target address is to match against. If no netmask is provided, /128 is assumed. You may have several rule sections, and the addresses may or may not overlap.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.rules.<name>.interface
documents.content: Interface to use when method is iface.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.rules.<name>.method
documents.content: static: Immediately answer any Neighbor Solicitation Messages (if they match the IP rule). iface: Forward the Neighbor Solicitation Message through the specified interface and only respond if a matching Neighbor Advertisement Message is received. auto: Same as iface, but instead of manually specifying the outgoing interface, check for a matching route in /proc/net/ipv6_route.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.rules.<name>.network
documents.content: This is the target address is to match against. If no netmask is provided, /128 is assumed. The addresses of several rules may or may not overlap. Defaults to the name of the attrset.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.timeout
documents.content: Controls how long to wait for a Neighbor Advertisement Message before invalidating the entry, in milliseconds.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.proxies.<name>.ttl
documents.content: Controls how long a valid or invalid entry remains in the cache, in milliseconds.

documents.title: Option: services.ndppd.routeTTL

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.bolt.advertisedAddress
documents.content: Neo4j advertised address for BOLT traffic. The advertised address is expressed in the format <ip-address>:<port-number>.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.bolt.enable
documents.content: Enable the BOLT connector for Neo4j. Setting this option to false will stop Neo4j from listening for incoming connections on the BOLT port (7687 by default).

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.bolt.listenAddress
documents.content: Neo4j listen address for BOLT traffic. The listen address is expressed in the format <ip-address>:<port-number>.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.bolt.sslPolicy
documents.content:
Neo4j SSL policy for BOLT traffic.
The legacy policy is a special policy which is not defined in the policy configuration section, but rather derives from {option}directories.certificates and associated files (by default: {file}neo4j.key and {file}neo4j.cert). Its use will be deprecated.
Note: This connector must be configured to support/require SSL/TLS for the legacy policy to actually be utilized. See {option}bolt.tlsLevel.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.bolt.tlsLevel
documents.content: SSL/TSL requirement level for BOLT traffic.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.constrainLoadCsv
documents.content:
Sets the root directory for file URLs used with the Cypher LOAD CSV clause to be that defined by {option}directories.imports. It restricts access to only those files within that directory and its subdirectories.
Setting this option to false introduces possible security problems.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.defaultListenAddress
documents.content:
Default network interface to listen for incoming connections. To listen for connections on all interfaces, use "0.0.0.0".
Specifies the default IP address and address part of connector specific {option}listenAddress options. To bind specific connectors to a specific network interfaces, specify the entire {option}listenAddress option for that connector.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.directories.certificates
documents.content:
Directory for storing certificates to be used by Neo4j for TLS connections.
When setting this directory to something other than its default, ensure the directory's existence, and that read/write permissions are given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.
Note that changing this directory from its default will prevent the directory structure required for each SSL policy from being automatically generated. A policy's directory structure as defined by its {option}baseDirectory,{option}revokedDir and {option}trustedDir must then be setup manually. The existence of these directories is mandatory, as well as the presence of the certificate file and the private key. Ensure the correct permissions are set on these directories and files.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.directories.data
documents.content:
Path of the data directory. You must not configure more than one Neo4j installation to use the same data directory.
When setting this directory to something other than its default, ensure the directory's existence, and that read/write permissions are given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.directories.home
documents.content: Path of the Neo4j home directory. Other default directories are subdirectories of this path. This directory will be created if non-existent, and its ownership will be {command}chown to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.directories.imports
documents.content:
The root directory for file URLs used with the Cypher LOAD CSV clause. Only meaningful when {option}constrainLoadCvs is set to true.
When setting this directory to something other than its default, ensure the directory's existence, and that read permission is given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.directories.plugins
documents.content:
Path of the database plugin directory. Compiled Java JAR files that contain database procedures will be loaded if they are placed in this directory.
When setting this directory to something other than its default, ensure the directory's existence, and that read permission is given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.

documents.content: Enable the HTTP connector for Neo4j. Setting this option to false will stop Neo4j from listening for incoming connections on the HTTPS port (7474 by default).

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.http.listenAddress
documents.content: Neo4j listen address for HTTP traffic. The listen address is expressed in the format <ip-address>:<port-number>.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.https.advertisedAddress

Neo4j SSL policy for HTTPS traffic.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.package
documents.content: The neo4j package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.readOnly
documents.content: Only allow read operations from this Neo4j instance.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.shell.enable
documents.content: Enable a remote shell server which Neo4j Shell clients can log in to. Only applicable to {command}neo4j-shell.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies
documents.content: Defines the SSL policies for use with Neo4j connectors. Each attribute of this set defines a policy, with the attribute name defining the name of the policy and its namespace. Refer to the operations manual section on Neo4j's SSL Framework for further details.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.allowKeyGeneration
documents.content:
Allows the generation of a private key and associated self-signed certificate. Only performed when both objects cannot be found for this policy. It is recommended to turn this off again after keys have been generated.
The public certificate is required to be duplicated to the directory holding trusted certificates as defined by the {option}trustedDir option.
Keys should in general be generated and distributed offline by a trusted certificate authority and not by utilizing this mode.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.baseDirectory
documents.content:
The mandatory base directory for cryptographic objects of this policy. This path is only automatically generated when this option as well as {option}directories.certificates are left at their default. Ensure read/write permissions are given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.
It is also possible to override each individual configuration with absolute paths. See the {option}privateKey and {option}publicCertificate policy options.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.ciphers
documents.content: Restrict the allowed ciphers of this policy to those defined here. The default ciphers are those of the JVM platform.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.clientAuth
documents.content: The client authentication stance for this policy.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.privateKey
documents.content: The name of private PKCS #8 key file for this policy to be found in the {option}baseDirectory, or the absolute path to the key file. It is mandatory that a key can be found or generated.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.publicCertificate
documents.content:
The name of public X.509 certificate (chain) file in PEM format for this policy to be found in the {option}baseDirectory, or the absolute path to the certificate file. It is mandatory that a certificate can be found or generated.
The public certificate is required to be duplicated to the directory holding trusted certificates as defined by the {option}trustedDir option.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.revokedDir
documents.content: Path to directory of CRLs (Certificate Revocation Lists) in PEM format. Must be an absolute path. The existence of this directory is mandatory and will need to be created manually when: setting this option to something other than its default; setting either this policy's {option}baseDirectory or {option}directories.certificates to something other than their default. Ensure read/write permissions are given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.tlsVersions
documents.content: Restrict the TLS protocol versions of this policy to those defined here.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.trustAll
documents.content: Makes this policy trust all remote parties. Enabling this is not recommended and the policy's trusted directory will be ignored. Use of this mode is discouraged. It would offer encryption but no security.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.ssl.policies.<name>.trustedDir
documents.content:
Path to directory of X.509 certificates in PEM format for trusted parties. Must be an absolute path. The existence of this directory is mandatory and will need to be created manually when: setting this option to something other than its default; setting either this policy's {option}baseDirectory or {option}directories.certificates to something other than their default. Ensure read/write permissions are given to the Neo4j daemon user neo4j.
The public certificate as defined by {option}publicCertificate is required to be duplicated to this directory.

documents.title: Option: services.neo4j.workerCount
documents.content: Number of Neo4j worker threads, where the default of 0 indicates a worker count equal to the number of available processors.

documents.title: Option: services.netatalk.enable

documents.title: Option: services.netatalk.extmap
documents.content: File name extension mappings. See {manpage}extmap.conf(5). for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.netatalk.port

documents.title: Option: services.netatalk.settings

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients
documents.content:
Attribute set of NetBird client daemons, by default each one will:
be manageable using dedicated tooling:

netbird-<name> script,
NetBird - netbird-<name> graphical interface when appropriate (see ui.enable),

run as a netbird-<name>.service,
listen for incoming remote connections on the port 51820 (openFirewall by default),
manage the netbird-<name> wireguard interface,
use the {file}/var/lib/netbird-<name>/config.json configuration file,
override {file}/var/lib/netbird-<name>/config.json with values from {file}/etc/netbird-<name>/config.d/*.json,
(hardened) be locally manageable by netbird-<name> system group,

With following caveats:
multiple daemons will interfere with each other's DNS resolution of netbird.cloud, but should remain fully operational otherwise. Setting up custom (non-conflicting) DNS zone is currently possible only when self-hosting.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.autoStart
documents.content:
Start the service with the system.
As of 2024-02-13 it is not possible to start a NetBird client daemon without immediately connecting to the network, but it is planned for a near future.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.bin.suffix
documents.content: A system group name for this client instance.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.config
documents.content:
Additional configuration that exists before the first start and later overrides the existing values in {file}config.json.
It is mostly helpful to manage configuration ignored/not yet implemented outside of netbird up invocation.
WARNING: this is not an upstream feature, it could break in the future (by having lower priority) after upstream implements an equivalent.
It is implemented as a preStart script which overrides {file}config.json with content of {file}/etc/netbird-‹name›/config.d/*.json files. This option manages specifically {file}50-nixos.json file.
Consult the source code or inspect existing file for a complete list of available configurations.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.dir.baseName
documents.content: A systemd service name to use (without .service suffix).

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.dir.runtime
documents.content: A runtime directory used by NetBird client.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.dir.state
documents.content: A state directory used by NetBird client to store {file}config.json, {file}state.json & {file}resolv.conf.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.dns-resolver.address
documents.content:
An explicit address that NetBird will serve *.netbird.cloud. (usually) entries on.
NetBird serves DNS on it's own (dynamic) client address by default.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.dns-resolver.port
documents.content: A port to serve DNS entries on when dns-resolver.address is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.environment
documents.content: Environment for the netbird service, used to pass configuration options.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.hardened
documents.content:
Hardened service:
runs as a dedicated user with minimal set of permissions (see caveats),
restricts daemon configuration socket access to dedicated user group (you can grant access to it with users.users."<user>".extraGroups = [ netbird-‹name› ]),

Even though the local system resources access is restricted:
CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_BPF still give unlimited network manipulation possibilites,
older kernels don't have CAP_BPF and use CAP_SYS_ADMIN instead,

Known security features that are not (yet) integrated into the module:
2024-02-14: rosenpass is an experimental feature configurable solely through --enable-rosenpass flag on the netbird up command, see the docs

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.interface
documents.content: Name of the network interface managed by this client.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.logLevel
documents.content: Log level of the NetBird daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.login.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable automated login for NetBird client.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.login.setupKeyFile
documents.content: A Setup Key file path used for automated login of the machine.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.login.systemdDependencies
documents.content: Additional systemd dependencies required to succeed before the Setup Key file becomes available.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.name
documents.content:
Primary name for use (as a suffix) in:
systemd service name,
hardened user name and group,
systemd *Directory= names,
desktop application identification,

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.openFirewall
documents.content: Opens up firewall port for communication between NetBird peers directly over LAN or public IP, without using (internet-hosted) TURN servers as intermediaries.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.openInternalFirewall
documents.content: Opens up internal firewall ports for the NetBird's network interface.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.port
documents.content: Port the NetBird client listens on.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.service.name
documents.content: A systemd service name to use (without .service suffix).

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.clients.<name>.suffixedName
documents.content: A systemd service name to use (without .service suffix).

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.tunnels.<name>.config
documents.content:
Additional configuration that exists before the first start and later overrides the existing values in {file}config.json.
It is mostly helpful to manage configuration ignored/not yet implemented outside of netbird up invocation.
WARNING: this is not an upstream feature, it could break in the future (by having lower priority) after upstream implements an equivalent.
It is implemented as a preStart script which overrides {file}config.json with content of {file}/etc/netbird-‹name›/config.d/*.json files. This option manages specifically {file}50-nixos.json file.
Consult the source code or inspect existing file for a complete list of available configurations.

documents.title: Option: services.netbird.tunnels.<name>.hardened
documents.content:
Hardened service:
runs as a dedicated user with minimal set of permissions (see caveats),
restricts daemon configuration socket access to dedicated user group (you can grant access to it with users.users."<user>".extraGroups = [ netbird-‹name› ]),

Even though the local system resources access is restricted:
CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_BPF still give unlimited network manipulation possibilites,
older kernels don't have CAP_BPF and use CAP_SYS_ADMIN instead,

Known security features that are not (yet) integrated into the module:
2024-02-14: rosenpass is an experimental feature configurable solely through --enable-rosenpass flag on the netbird up command, see the docs

documents.title: Option: services.netdata.deadlineBeforeStopSec
documents.content:
In order to detect when netdata is misbehaving, we run a concurrent task pinging netdata (wait-for-netdata-up) in the systemd unit.
If after a while, this task does not succeed, we stop the unit and mark it as failed.
You can control this deadline in seconds with this option, it's useful to bump it if you have (1) a lot of data (2) doing upgrades (3) have low IOPS/throughput.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.appstoreEnable
documents.content: Allow the installation and updating of apps from the Nextcloud appstore. Enabled by default unless there are packages in . documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.caching.redis

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.cli.memoryLimit

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.config.dbuser

Whether to enable S3 object storage as primary storage.

The file must contain a random 32-byte key encoded as a base64 string, e.g. generated with the command

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.config.objectstore.s3.usePathStyle

Required for some non-Amazon S3 implementations.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.configureRedis
documents.content:
Whether to configure Nextcloud to use the recommended Redis settings for small instances.
::: {.note} The Nextcloud system check recommends to configure either Redis or Memcache for file lock caching. :::
::: {.note} The notify_push app requires Redis to be configured. If this option is turned off, this must be configured manually. :::

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.database.createLocally
documents.content: Whether to create the database and database user locally.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.datadir
documents.content: Nextcloud's data storage path. Will be by default. This folder will be populated with a config.php file and a data folder which contains the state of the instance (excluding the database).";

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable nextcloud.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.enableImagemagick
documents.content: Whether to enable the ImageMagick module for PHP. This is used by the theming app and for generating previews of certain images (e.g. SVG and HEIF). You may want to disable it for increased security. In that case, previews will still be available for some images (e.g. JPEG and PNG). See https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues/13099 .

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.extraApps
documents.content: Extra apps to install. Should be an attrSet of appid to packages generated by fetchNextcloudApp. The appid must be identical to the "id" value in the apps appinfo/info.xml. Using this will disable the appstore to prevent Nextcloud from updating these apps (see ).

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.extraAppsEnable
documents.content: Automatically enable the apps in every time Nextcloud starts. If set to false, apps need to be enabled in the Nextcloud web user interface or with nextcloud-occ app:enable.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.fastcgiTimeout
documents.content: FastCGI timeout for database connection in seconds.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.finalPackage
documents.content: Package to the finalized Nextcloud package, including all installed apps. This is automatically set by the module.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.home
documents.content: Storage path of nextcloud.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.hostName
documents.content: FQDN for the nextcloud instance.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.https
documents.content:
Use HTTPS for generated links.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.imaginary.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Imaginary.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.maxUploadSize
documents.content: The upload limit for files. This changes the relevant options in php.ini and nginx if enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.nginx.enableFastcgiRequestBuffering
documents.content:
Whether to buffer requests against fastcgi requests. This is a workaround for PUT requests with the Transfer-Encoding: chunked header set and an unspecified Content-Length. Without request buffering for these requests, Nextcloud will create files with zero bytes length as described in nextcloud/server#7995.
::: {.note} Please keep in mind that upstream suggests to not enable this as it might lead to timeouts on large files being uploaded as described in the administrator manual. :::

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.nginx.hstsMaxAge
documents.content:
Value for the max-age directive of the HTTP Strict-Transport-Security header.
See section 6.1.1 of IETF RFC 6797 for detailed information on this directive and header.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.notify_push.bendDomainToLocalhost
documents.content:
Whether to add an entry to /etc/hosts for the configured nextcloud domain to point to localhost and add localhost to nextcloud's trusted_proxies config option.
This is useful when nextcloud's domain is not a static IP address and when the reverse proxy cannot be bypassed because the backend connection is done via unix socket.

documents.content: Additional PHP extensions to use for Nextcloud. By default, only extensions necessary for a vanilla Nextcloud installation are enabled, but you may choose from the list of available extensions and add further ones. This is sometimes necessary to be able to install a certain Nextcloud app that has additional requirements.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.phpOptions
documents.content:
Options for PHP's php.ini file for nextcloud.
Please note that this option is additive on purpose while the attribute values inside the default are option defaults: that means that
will override the php.ini option opcache.interned_strings_buffer without discarding the rest of the defaults.
Overriding all of phpOptions (including upload_max_filesize, post_max_size and memory_limit which all point to by default) can be done like this:

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.phpPackage
documents.content: The php package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.poolConfig
documents.content: Options for Nextcloud's PHP pool. See the documentation on php-fpm.conf for details on configuration directives.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.poolSettings
documents.content:
Options for nextcloud's PHP pool. See the documentation on php-fpm.conf for details on configuration directives. The above are recommended for a server with 4GiB of RAM.
It's advisable to read the section about PHPFPM tuning in the upstream manual and consider customizing the values.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.secretFile
documents.content: Secret options which will be appended to Nextcloud's config.php file (written as JSON, in the same form as the option), for example {"redis":{"password":"secret"}}.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.secrets
documents.content: Secret files to read into entries in config.php. This uses nix_read_secret and LoadCredential to read the contents of the file into the entry in config.php.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings
documents.content: Extra options which should be appended to Nextcloud's config.php file.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings."profile.enabled"
documents.content:
Makes user-profiles globally available under nextcloud.tld/u/user.name. Even though it's enabled by default in Nextcloud, it must be explicitly enabled here because it has the side-effect that personal information is even accessible to unauthenticated users by default. By default, the following properties are set to “Show to everyone” if this flag is enabled:
About
Full name
Headline
Organisation
Profile picture
Role
Twitter
Website Only has an effect in Nextcloud 23 and later.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.default_phone_region
documents.content:
An ISO 3166-1 country code which replaces automatic phone-number detection without a country code.
As an example, with DE set as the default phone region, the +49 prefix can be omitted for phone numbers.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.enabledPreviewProviders
documents.content: The preview providers that should be explicitly enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.log_type
documents.content: Logging backend to use. systemd automatically adds the php-systemd extensions to services.nextcloud.phpExtraExtensions. See the nextcloud documentation for details.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.loglevel
documents.content:
Log level value between 0 (DEBUG) and 4 (FATAL).
0 (debug): Log all activity.
1 (info): Log activity such as user logins and file activities, plus warnings, errors, and fatal errors.
2 (warn): Log successful operations, as well as warnings of potential problems, errors and fatal errors.
3 (error): Log failed operations and fatal errors.
4 (fatal): Log only fatal errors that cause the server to stop.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_domain
documents.content: The return address that you want to appear on emails sent by the Nextcloud server, for example nc-admin@example.com, substituting your own domain, of course.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_from_address
documents.content: FROM address that overrides the built-in sharing-noreply and lostpassword-noreply FROM addresses. Defaults to different FROM addresses depending on the feature.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_send_plaintext_only
documents.content: Email will be sent by default with an HTML and a plain text body. This option allows sending only plain text emails.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_sendmailmode
documents.content: For smtp, the sendmail binary is started with the parameter -bs: Use the SMTP protocol on standard input and output. For pipe, the binary is started with the parameters -t: Read message from STDIN and extract recipients.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpauth
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpmode. Change this to true if your mail server requires authentication.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpdebug
documents.content: Enable SMTP class debugging. loglevel will likely need to be adjusted too. See docs.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtphost
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpmode. Specify the IP address of your mail server host. This may contain multiple hosts separated by a semicolon. If you need to specify the port number, append it to the IP address separated by a colon, like this: 127.0.0.1:24.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpmode
documents.content: Which mode to use for sending mail. If you are using local or remote SMTP, set this to smtp. For the sendmail option, you need an installed and working email system on the server, with your local sendmail installation. For qmail, the binary is /var/qmail/bin/sendmail, and it must be installed on your Unix system. Use the string null to send no mails (disable mail delivery). This can be useful if mails should be sent via APIs and rendering messages is not necessary.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpname
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpauth. Specify the username for authenticating to the SMTP server.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpport
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpmode. Specify the port for sending mail.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpsecure
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpmode. Specify ssl when you are using SSL/TLS. Any other value will be ignored. If the server advertises STARTTLS capabilities, they might be used, but they cannot be enforced by this config option.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtpstreamoptions
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpmode. Array of additional streams options that will be passed to underlying Swift mailer implementation.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_smtptimeout
documents.content: This depends on mail_smtpmode. This sets the SMTP server timeout, in seconds. You may need to increase this if you are running an anti-malware or spam scanner.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.mail_template_class
documents.content: Replaces the default mail template layout. This can be utilized if the options to modify the mail texts with the theming app are not enough. The class must extend \OC\Mail\EMailTemplate

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.overwriteprotocol
documents.content: Force Nextcloud to always use HTTP or HTTPS i.e. for link generation. Nextcloud uses the currently used protocol by default, but when behind a reverse-proxy, it may use http for everything although Nextcloud may be served via HTTPS.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.skeletondirectory
documents.content: The directory where the skeleton files are located. These files will be copied to the data directory of new users. Leave empty to not copy any skeleton files.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.trusted_domains
documents.content: Trusted domains, from which the nextcloud installation will be accessible. You don't need to add services.nextcloud.hostname here.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.settings.trusted_proxies
documents.content: Trusted proxies, to provide if the nextcloud installation is being proxied to secure against e.g. spoofing.

documents.title: Option: services.nextcloud.webfinger

documents.title: Option: services.nextjs-ollama-llm-ui.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable Simple Ollama web UI service; an easy to use web frontend for a Ollama backend service. Run state-of-the-art AI large language models (LLM) similar to ChatGPT locally with privacy on your personal computer. This service is stateless and doesn't store any data on the server; all data is kept locally in your web browser. See https://github.com/jakobhoeg/nextjs-ollama-llm-ui.
Required: You need the Ollama backend service running by having "services.nextjs-ollama-llm-ui.ollamaUrl" point to the correct url. You can host such a backend service with NixOS through "services.ollama". .

documents.title: Option: services.nextjs-ollama-llm-ui.hostname
documents.content:
The hostname under which the Ollama UI interface should be accessible. By default it uses localhost/127.0.0.1 to be accessible only from the local machine. Change to "0.0.0.0" to make it directly accessible from the local network.
Note: You should keep it at 127.0.0.1 and only serve to the local network or internet from a (home) server behind a reverse-proxy and secured encryption. See https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/Nginx for instructions on how to set up a reverse-proxy.

documents.title: Option: services.nextjs-ollama-llm-ui.ollamaUrl
documents.content: The address (including host and port) under which we can access the Ollama backend server. !Note that if the the UI service is running under a domain "https://ui.example.org", the Ollama backend service must allow "CORS" requests from this domain, e.g. by adding "services.ollama.environment.OLLAMA_ORIGINS = [ ... "https://ui.example.org" ];"!

documents.title: Option: services.nextjs-ollama-llm-ui.port
