documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backend-address-family
documents.content:
Specify address family of backend connections. If "auto" is given, both IPv4 and IPv6 are considered. If "IPv4" is given, only IPv4 address is considered. If "IPv6" is given, only IPv6 address is considered.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx--backend-address-family

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends
documents.content: A list of backend specifications.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params
documents.content: Parameters to configure a backend.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.affinity
documents.content:
If "ip" is given, client IP based session affinity is enabled. If "none" is given, session affinity is disabled.
Session affinity is enabled (by nghttpx) per-backend pattern. If at least one backend has a non-"none" affinity, then session affinity is enabled for all backend servers sharing the same pattern.
It is advised to set affinity on all backends explicitly if session affinity is desired. The session affinity may break if one of the backend gets unreachable, or backend settings are reloaded or replaced by API.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.dns
documents.content:
Name resolution of a backends host name is done at start up, or configuration reload. If "dns" is true, name resolution takes place dynamically.
This is useful if a backends address changes frequently. If "dns" is true, name resolution of a backend's host name at start up, or configuration reload is skipped.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.fall
documents.content:
If nghttpx cannot connect to the backend N times in a row, the backend is assumed to be offline and is excluded from load balancing. If N is 0 the backend is never excluded from load balancing.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.proto
documents.content:
This option configures the protocol the backend server expects to use.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.redirect-if-not-tls
documents.content:
If true, a backend match requires the frontend connection be TLS encrypted. If it is not, nghttpx responds to the request with a 308 status code and https URI the client should use instead in the Location header.
The port number in the redirect URI is 443 by default and can be changed using 'services.nghttpx.redirect-https-port' option.
If at least one backend has "redirect-if-not-tls" set to true, this feature is enabled for all backend servers with the same pattern. It is advised to set "redirect-if-no-tls" parameter to all backends explicitly if this feature is desired.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.rise
documents.content:
If the backend is excluded from load balancing, nghttpx will periodically attempt to make a connection to the backend. If the connection is successful N times in a row the backend is re-included in load balancing. If N is 0 a backend is never reconsidered for load balancing once it falls.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.sni
documents.content:
Override the TLS SNI field value. This value (in nghttpx) defaults to the host value of the backend configuration.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.params.tls
documents.content:
This option determines whether nghttpx will negotiate its connection with a backend server using TLS or not. The burden is on the backend server to provide the TLS certificate!
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.patterns
documents.content:
List of nghttpx backend patterns.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-b for more information on the pattern syntax and nghttpxs behavior.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backends.*.server
documents.content: Backend server location specified as either a host:port pair or a unix domain docket.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.backlog
documents.content:
Listen backlog size.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx--backlog

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable nghttpx.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.extraConfig
documents.content: Extra configuration options to be appended to the generated configuration file.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends
documents.content: A list of frontend listener specifications.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.params
documents.content: Parameters to configure a backend.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.params.api
documents.content:
Enable API access for this frontend. This enables you to dynamically modify nghttpx at run-time therefore this feature is disabled by default and should be turned on with care.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-f for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.params.healthmon
documents.content:
Make this frontend a health monitor endpoint. Any request received on this frontend is responded to with a 200 OK.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-f for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.params.proxyproto
documents.content:
Accept PROXY protocol version 1 on frontend connection.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-f for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.params.sni-fwd
documents.content:
When performing a match to select a backend server, SNI host name received from the client is used instead of the request host. See --backend option about the pattern match.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-f for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.params.tls
documents.content:
Enable or disable TLS. If true (enabled) the key and certificate must be configured for nghttpx.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-f for more detail.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.frontends.*.server
documents.content:
Frontend server interface binding specification as either a host:port pair or a unix domain docket.
NB: a host of "*" listens on all interfaces and includes IPv6 addresses.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.rlimit-nofile
documents.content:
Set maximum number of open files (RLIMIT_NOFILE) to <N>. If 0 is given, nghttpx does not set the limit.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx--rlimit-nofile

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.single-process
documents.content:
Run this program in a single process mode for debugging purpose. Without this option, nghttpx creates at least 2 processes: master and worker processes. If this option is used, master and worker are unified into a single process. nghttpx still spawns additional process if neverbleed is used. In the single process mode, the signal handling feature is disabled.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx--single-process

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.single-thread
documents.content:
Run everything in one thread inside the worker process. This feature is provided for better debugging experience, or for the platforms which lack thread support. If threading is disabled, this option is always enabled.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx--single-thread

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.tls
documents.content: TLS certificate and key paths. Note that this does not enable TLS for a frontend listener, to do so, a frontend specification must set params.tls to true.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.tls.crt
documents.content: Path to the TLS certificate file.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.tls.key
documents.content: Path to the TLS key file.

documents.title: Option: services.nghttpx.workers
documents.content:
Set the number of worker threads.
Please see https://nghttp2.org/documentation/nghttpx.1.html#cmdoption-nghttpx-n

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.additionalModules
documents.content: Additional third-party nginx modules to install. Packaged modules are available in pkgs.nginxModules.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.appendConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines appended to the generated Nginx configuration file. Commonly used by different modules providing http snippets. {option}appendConfig can be specified more than once and its value will be concatenated (contrary to {option}config which can be set only once).

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.appendHttpConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines to be appended to the generated http block. This is mutually exclusive with using config and httpConfig for specifying the whole http block verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.clientMaxBodySize
documents.content: Set nginx global client_max_body_size.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.commonHttpConfig
documents.content: With nginx you must provide common http context definitions before they are used, e.g. log_format, resolver, etc. inside of server or location contexts. Use this attribute to set these definitions at the appropriate location.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.config
documents.content:
Verbatim {file}nginx.conf configuration. This is mutually exclusive to any other config option for {file}nginx.conf except for

If additional verbatim config in addition to other options is needed, should be used instead.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultHTTPListenPort
documents.content: If vhosts do not specify listen.port, use these ports for HTTP by default.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListen
documents.content: If vhosts do not specify listen, use these addresses by default. This option takes precedence over {option}defaultListenAddresses and other listen-related defaults options.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListen.*.addr
documents.content: IP address.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListen.*.extraParameters
documents.content: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListen.*.port
documents.content: Port number.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListen.*.proxyProtocol
documents.content: Enable PROXY protocol.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListen.*.ssl
documents.content: Enable SSL.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultListenAddresses
documents.content: If vhosts do not specify listenAddresses, use these addresses by default. This is akin to writing defaultListen = [ { addr = "0.0.0.0" } ].

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultMimeTypes
documents.content: Default MIME types for NGINX, as MIME types definitions from NGINX are very incomplete, we use by default the ones bundled in the mailcap package, used by most of the other Linux distributions.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.defaultSSLListenPort
documents.content: If vhosts do not specify listen.port, use these ports for SSL by default.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Nginx Web Server.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.enableQuicBPF
documents.content: Enables routing of QUIC packets using eBPF. When enabled, this allows to support QUIC connection migration. The directive is only supported on Linux 5.7+. Note that enabling this option will make nginx run with extended capabilities that are usually limited to processes running as root namely CAP_SYS_ADMIN and CAP_NET_ADMIN.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.enableReload
documents.content: Reload nginx when configuration file changes (instead of restart). The configuration file is exposed at {file}/etc/nginx/nginx.conf. See also systemd.services.*.restartIfChanged.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.eventsConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines to be set inside the events block.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.experimentalZstdSettings
documents.content:
Enable alpha quality zstd module with recommended settings. Learn more about compression in Zstd format here.
This adds pkgs.nginxModules.zstd to services.nginx.additionalModules.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.gitweb.enable
documents.content: If true, enable gitweb in nginx.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.gitweb.group
documents.content: Group that the CGI process will belong to. (Set to config.services.gitolite.group if you are using gitolite.)

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.gitweb.location
documents.content: Location to serve gitweb on.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.gitweb.user
documents.content: Existing user that the CGI process will belong to. (Default almost surely will do.)

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.gitweb.virtualHost
documents.content: VirtualHost to serve gitweb on. Default is catch-all.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.group
documents.content: Group account under which nginx runs.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.httpConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines to be set inside the http block. This is mutually exclusive with the structured configuration via virtualHosts and the recommendedXyzSettings configuration options. See appendHttpConfig for appending to the generated http block.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.logError
documents.content: Configures logging. The first parameter defines a file that will store the log. The special value stderr selects the standard error file. Logging to syslog can be configured by specifying the “syslog:” prefix. The second parameter determines the level of logging, and can be one of the following: debug, info, notice, warn, error, crit, alert, or emerg. Log levels above are listed in the order of increasing severity. Setting a certain log level will cause all messages of the specified and more severe log levels to be logged. If this parameter is omitted then error is used.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.mapHashBucketSize
documents.content:
Sets the bucket size for the map variables hash tables. Default value depends on the processor’s cache line size.
Refer to the nginx docs on hashes for more information.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.mapHashMaxSize
documents.content: Sets the maximum size of the map variables hash tables.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.package
documents.content: Nginx package to use. This defaults to the stable version. Note that the nginx team recommends to use the mainline version which available in nixpkgs as nginxMainline. Supported Nginx forks include angie, openresty and tengine.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.preStart
documents.content: Shell commands executed before the service's nginx is started.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.prependConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines prepended to the generated Nginx configuration file. Can for example be used to load modules. {option}prependConfig can be specified more than once and its value will be concatenated (contrary to {option}config which can be set only once).

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath
documents.content: Configure a proxy cache path entry. See https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html#proxy_cache_path for documentation.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable this proxy cache path entry.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.inactive
documents.content: Cached data that has not been accessed for the time specified by the inactive parameter is removed from the cache, regardless of its freshness.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.keysZoneName
documents.content: Set name to shared memory zone.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.keysZoneSize
documents.content: Set size to shared memory zone.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.levels
documents.content: The levels parameter defines structure of subdirectories in cache: from 1 to 3, each level accepts values 1 or 2. Can be used any combination of 1 and 2 in these formats: x, x:x and x:x:x.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.maxSize
documents.content: Set maximum cache size

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyCachePath.<name>.useTempPath
documents.content: Nginx first writes files that are destined for the cache to a temporary storage area, and the use_temp_path=off directive instructs Nginx to write them to the same directories where they will be cached. Recommended that you set this parameter to off to avoid unnecessary copying of data between file systems.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyResolveWhileRunning
documents.content:
Resolves domains of proxyPass targets at runtime and not only at startup. This can be used as a workaround if nginx fails to start because of not-yet-working DNS.
:::{.warn} services.nginx.resolver must be set for this option to work. :::

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.proxyTimeout
documents.content: Change the proxy related timeouts in recommendedProxySettings.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.recommendedBrotliSettings
documents.content:
Enable recommended brotli settings. Learn more about compression in Brotli format here.
This adds pkgs.nginxModules.brotli to services.nginx.additionalModules.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.recommendedGzipSettings
documents.content: Enable recommended gzip settings. Learn more about compression in Gzip format here.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.recommendedOptimisation
documents.content: Enable recommended optimisation settings.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.recommendedProxySettings
documents.content: Whether to enable recommended proxy settings if a vhost does not specify the option manually.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.recommendedTlsSettings
documents.content: Enable recommended TLS settings.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.recommendedUwsgiSettings
documents.content: Whether to enable recommended uwsgi settings if a vhost does not specify the option manually.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.resolver
documents.content: Configures name servers used to resolve names of upstream servers into addresses

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.resolver.addresses
documents.content: List of resolvers to use

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.resolver.ipv4
documents.content: By default, nginx will look up both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses while resolving. If looking up of IPv4 addresses is not desired, the ipv4=off parameter can be specified.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.resolver.ipv6
documents.content: By default, nginx will look up both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses while resolving. If looking up of IPv6 addresses is not desired, the ipv6=off parameter can be specified.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.resolver.valid
documents.content: By default, nginx caches answers using the TTL value of a response. An optional valid parameter allows overriding it

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.serverNamesHashBucketSize
documents.content: Sets the bucket size for the server names hash tables. Default value depends on the processor’s cache line size.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.serverNamesHashMaxSize
documents.content: Sets the maximum size of the server names hash tables.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.serverTokens
documents.content: Show nginx version in headers and error pages.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.sslCiphers
documents.content:
List of available cipher suites to choose from when negotiating TLS sessions.
:::{.warn} This option only handles cipher suites up to TLSv1.2. Use ssl_conf_command CipherSuites to configure TLSv1.3 cipher suites. :::

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.sslDhparam
documents.content: Path to DH parameters file, or true to generate with security.dhparms.params.nginx.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.sslProtocols
documents.content: Allowed TLS protocol versions.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.sso.configuration
documents.content:
nginx-sso configuration (documentation) as a Nix attribute set.
Options containing secret data should be set to an attribute set with the singleton attribute _secret - a string value set to the path to the file containing the secret value which should be used in the configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.sso.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable nginx-sso service.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.sso.package
documents.content: The nginx-sso package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.statusPage
documents.content: Enable status page reachable from localhost on http://127.0.0.1/nginx_status.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.streamConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines to be set inside the stream block.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable tailscale.nginx-auth, to authenticate nginx users via tailscale.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.expectedTailnet
documents.content: If you want to prevent node sharing from allowing users to access services across tailnets, declare your expected tailnets domain here.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.group
documents.content: Alias of {option}services.tailscaleAuth.group.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.package
documents.content: Alias of {option}services.tailscaleAuth.package.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.socketPath
documents.content: Alias of {option}services.tailscaleAuth.socketPath.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.user
documents.content: Alias of {option}services.tailscaleAuth.user.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.tailscaleAuth.virtualHosts
documents.content: A list of nginx virtual hosts to put behind tailscale.nginx-auth

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.typesHashMaxSize
documents.content: Sets the maximum size of the types hash tables (types_hash_max_size). It is recommended that the minimum size possible size is used. If {option}recommendedOptimisation is disabled, nginx would otherwise fail to start since the mailmap mime.types database has more entries than the nginx default value 1024.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.upstreams
documents.content: Defines a group of servers to use as proxy target.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.upstreams.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the upstream verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.upstreams.<name>.servers
documents.content: Defines the address and other parameters of the upstream servers. See the documentation for the available parameters.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.upstreams.<name>.servers.<name>.backup
documents.content: Marks the server as a backup server. It will be passed requests when the primary servers are unavailable.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.user
documents.content: User account under which nginx runs.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.uwsgiResolveWhileRunning
documents.content: Resolves domains of uwsgi targets at runtime and not only at start, you have to set services.nginx.resolver, too.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.uwsgiTimeout
documents.content: Change the uwsgi related timeouts in recommendedUwsgiSettings.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.validateConfigFile
documents.content: Whether to enable validating configuration with pkgs.writeNginxConfig.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts
documents.content: Declarative vhost config

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.acmeFallbackHost
documents.content:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.
With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would specify here.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.acmeRoot
documents.content: Directory for the ACME challenge, which is public. Don't put certs or keys in here. Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.addSSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443).

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.default
documents.content: Makes this vhost the default.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.enableACME
documents.content: Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost. Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}useACMEHost.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.forceSSL
documents.content: Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) all plain HTTP traffic to HTTPS. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens are used for the redirect vhosts.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.globalRedirect
documents.content: If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301, configurable with redirectCode) to the given hostname.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.http2
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol. Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given IP address / port. If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.http3
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.http3_hq
documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. Note that special application protocol support is experimental and not yet recommended for production. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.kTLS
documents.content: Whether to enable kTLS support. Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel. Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listen
documents.content:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host. IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets. Note: this option overrides addSSL and onlySSL.
If you only want to set the addresses manually and not the ports, take a look at listenAddresses.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listen.*.addr
documents.content: Listen address.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listen.*.extraParameters
documents.content: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listen.*.port
documents.content: Port number to listen on. If unset and the listen address is not a socket then nginx defaults to 80.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listen.*.proxyProtocol
documents.content: Enable PROXY protocol.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listen.*.ssl
documents.content: Enable SSL.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.listenAddresses
documents.content:
Listen addresses for this virtual host. Compared to listen this only sets the addresses and the ports are chosen automatically.
Note: This option overrides networking.enableIPv6

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations
documents.content: Declarative location config

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.alias
documents.content: Alias directory for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.basicAuth
documents.content:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.
WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.basicAuthFile
documents.content: Basic Auth password file for a vhost. Can be created by running {command}nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.extraConfig
documents.content: These lines go to the end of the location verbatim.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.fastcgiParams
documents.content: FastCGI parameters to override. Unlike in the Nginx configuration file, overriding only some default parameters won't unset the default values for other parameters.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.index
documents.content: Adds index directive.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.priority
documents.content: Order of this location block in relation to the others in the vhost. The semantics are the same as with lib.mkOrder. Smaller values have a greater priority.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.proxyPass
documents.content: Adds proxy_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedProxySettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.proxyWebsockets
documents.content: Whether to support proxying websocket connections with HTTP/1.1.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.recommendedProxySettings
documents.content: Enable recommended proxy settings.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.recommendedUwsgiSettings
documents.content: Enable recommended uwsgi settings.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.return
documents.content: Adds a return directive, for e.g. redirections.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.root
documents.content: Root directory for requests.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.tryFiles
documents.content: Adds try_files directive.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.locations.<name>.uwsgiPass
documents.content: Adds uwsgi_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if recommendedUwsgiSettings is enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.onlySSL
documents.content: Whether to enable HTTPS and reject plain HTTP connections. This will set defaults for listen to listen on all interfaces on port 443.

documents.title: Option: services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.extraConfig
documents.content: Extra nsd config.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.hideVersion
documents.content: Whether NSD should answer VERSION.BIND and VERSION.SERVER CHAOS class queries.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.identity
documents.content: Identify the server (CH TXT ID.SERVER entry).

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.interfaces
documents.content: What addresses the server should listen to.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ipFreebind
documents.content: Whether to bind to nonlocal addresses and interfaces that are down. Similar to ip-transparent.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ipTransparent
documents.content: Allow binding to non local addresses.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ipv4
documents.content: Whether to listen on IPv4 connections.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ipv4EDNSSize
documents.content: Preferred EDNS buffer size for IPv4.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ipv6
documents.content: Whether to listen on IPv6 connections.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ipv6EDNSSize
documents.content: Preferred EDNS buffer size for IPv6.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.keys
documents.content: Define your TSIG keys here.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.keys.<name>.algorithm
documents.content: Authentication algorithm for this key.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.keys.<name>.keyFile
documents.content: Path to the file which contains the actual base64 encoded key. The key will be copied into "/var/lib/nsd/private" before NSD starts. The copied file is only accessibly by the NSD user.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.logTimeAscii
documents.content: Log time in ascii, if false then in unix epoch seconds.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.nsid
documents.content: NSID identity (hex string, or "ascii_somestring").

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.port
documents.content: Port the service should bind do.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable ratelimit capabilities.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.ipv4PrefixLength
documents.content: IPv4 prefix length. Addresses are grouped by netblock.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.ipv6PrefixLength
documents.content: IPv6 prefix length. Addresses are grouped by netblock.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.ratelimit
documents.content: Max qps allowed from any query source. 0 means unlimited. With an verbosity of 2 blocked and unblocked subnets will be logged.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.size
documents.content: Size of the hashtable. More buckets use more memory but lower the chance of hash hash collisions.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.slip
documents.content: Number of packets that get discarded before replying a SLIP response. 0 disables SLIP responses. 1 will make every response a SLIP response.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.ratelimit.whitelistRatelimit
documents.content: Max qps allowed from whitelisted sources. 0 means unlimited. Set the rrl-whitelist option for specific queries to apply this limit instead of the default to them.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.controlCertFile
documents.content: Path to the client certificate signed with the server certificate. This file is used by nsd-control and generated by nsd-control-setup.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.controlKeyFile
documents.content: Path to the client private key, which is used by nsd-control but not by the server. This file is generated by nsd-control-setup.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable remote control via nsd-control.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.interfaces
documents.content: Which interfaces NSD should bind to for remote control.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.port
documents.content: Port number for remote control operations (uses TLS over TCP).

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.serverCertFile
documents.content: Path to the server self signed certificate, which is used by the server but and by nsd-control. This file is generated by nsd-control-setup.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.remoteControl.serverKeyFile
documents.content: Path to the server private key, which is used by the server but not by nsd-control. This file is generated by nsd-control-setup.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.reuseport
documents.content: Whether to enable SO_REUSEPORT on all used sockets. This lets multiple processes bind to the same port. This speeds up operation especially if the server count is greater than one and makes fast restarts less prone to fail

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.rootServer
documents.content: Whether this server will be a root server (a DNS root server, you usually don't want that).

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.roundRobin
documents.content: Whether to enable round robin rotation of records.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.serverCount
documents.content: Number of NSD servers to fork. Put the number of CPUs to use here.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.statistics
documents.content: Statistics are produced every number of seconds. Prints to log. If null no statistics are logged.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.tcpCount
documents.content: Maximum number of concurrent TCP connections per server.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.tcpQueryCount
documents.content: Maximum number of queries served on a single TCP connection. 0 means no maximum.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.tcpTimeout
documents.content: TCP timeout in seconds.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.verbosity
documents.content: Verbosity level.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.version
documents.content: The version string replied for CH TXT version.server and version.bind queries. Will use the compiled package version on null. See hideVersion for enabling/disabling this responses.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.xfrdReloadTimeout
documents.content: Number of seconds between reloads triggered by xfrd.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zonefilesCheck
documents.content: Whether to check mtime of all zone files on start and sighup.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zonefilesWrite
documents.content: Write changed secondary zones to their zonefile every N seconds. If the zone (pattern) configuration has "" zonefile, it is not written. Zones that have received zone transfer updates are written to their zonefile. 0 disables writing to zone files.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones
documents.content: Define your zones here. Zones can cascade other zones and therefore inherit settings from parent zones. Look at the definition of children to learn about inheritance and child zones. The given example will define 3 zones (example.(com|org|net).). Both example.com. and example.org. inherit their configuration from serverGroup1.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.allowAXFRFallback
documents.content: If NSD as secondary server should be allowed to AXFR if the primary server does not allow IXFR.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.allowNotify
documents.content:
Listed primary servers are allowed to notify this secondary server.
Format: <ip> <key-name | NOKEY | BLOCKED>
<ip> either a plain IPv4/IPv6 address or range. Valid patters for ranges:
10.0.0.0/24: via subnet size
10.0.0.0&255.255.255.0: via subnet mask
10.0.0.1-10.0.0.254: via range

A optional port number could be added with a '@':
2001:1234::1@1234

<key-name | NOKEY | BLOCKED>
<key-name> will use the specified TSIG key
NOKEY no TSIG signature is required
BLOCKEDnotifies from non-listed or blocked IPs will be ignored

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.children
documents.content: Children zones inherit all options of their parents. Attributes defined in a child will overwrite the ones of its parent. Only leaf zones will be actually served. This way it's possible to define maybe zones which share most attributes without duplicating everything. This mechanism replaces nsd's patterns in a save and functional way.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.data
documents.content: The actual zone data. This is the content of your zone file. Use imports or pkgs.lib.readFile if you don't want this data in your config file.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssec
documents.content: Whether to enable DNSSEC.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.algorithm
documents.content: Which algorithm to use for DNSSEC

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.coverage
documents.content: The length of time to ensure that keys will be correct; no action will be taken to create new keys to be activated after this time.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.keyttl
documents.content: TTL for dnssec records

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.ksk
documents.content: Key policy for key signing keys

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.ksk.keySize
documents.content: Key size in bits

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.ksk.postPublish
documents.content: How long after deactivation to keep a key in the zone

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.ksk.prePublish
documents.content: How long in advance to publish new keys

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.ksk.rollPeriod
documents.content: How frequently to change keys

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.zsk
documents.content: Key policy for zone signing keys

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.zsk.keySize
documents.content: Key size in bits

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.zsk.postPublish
documents.content: How long after deactivation to keep a key in the zone

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.zsk.prePublish
documents.content: How long in advance to publish new keys

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.dnssecPolicy.zsk.rollPeriod
documents.content: How frequently to change keys

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.maxRefreshSecs
documents.content: Limit refresh time for secondary zones. This is the timer which checks to see if the zone has to be refetched when it expires. Normally the value from the SOA record is used, but this option restricts that value.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.maxRetrySecs
documents.content: Limit retry time for secondary zones. This is the timeout after a failed fetch attempt for the zone. Normally the value from the SOA record is used, but this option restricts that value.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.minRefreshSecs
documents.content: Limit refresh time for secondary zones.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.minRetrySecs
documents.content: Limit retry time for secondary zones.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.multiMasterCheck
documents.content: If enabled, checks all masters for the last zone version. It uses the higher version from all configured masters. Useful if you have multiple masters that have different version numbers served.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.notify
documents.content:
This primary server will notify all given secondary servers about zone changes.
Format: <ip> <key-name | NOKEY>
<ip> a plain IPv4/IPv6 address with on optional port number (ip@port)
<key-name | NOKEY>
<key-name> sign notifies with the specified key
NOKEY don't sign notifies

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.notifyRetry
documents.content: Specifies the number of retries for failed notifies. Set this along with notify.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.outgoingInterface
documents.content: This address will be used for zone-transfer requests if configured as a secondary server or notifications in case of a primary server. Supply either a plain IPv4 or IPv6 address with an optional port number (ip@port).

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.provideXFR
documents.content: Allow these IPs and TSIG to transfer zones, addr TSIG|NOKEY|BLOCKED address range 192.0.2.0/24, 1.2.3.4&255.255.0.0, 3.0.2.20-3.0.2.40

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.requestXFR
documents.content: Format: [AXFR|UDP] <ip-address> <key-name | NOKEY>

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.rrlWhitelist
documents.content: Whitelists the given rrl-types.

documents.title: Option: services.nsd.zones.<name>.zoneStats
documents.content: When set to something distinct to null NSD is able to collect statistics per zone. All statistics of this zone(s) will be added to the group specified by this given name. Use "%s" to use the zones name as the group. The groups are output from nsd-control stats and stats_noreset.

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable ntfy-sh, a push notification service.

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.environmentFile
documents.content:
Path to a file containing extra ntfy environment variables in the systemd EnvironmentFile format. Refer to the documentation for config options.
This can be used to pass secrets such as creating declarative users or token without putting them in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.group
documents.content: Primary group of ntfy-sh user.

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.package
documents.content: The ntfy-sh package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.settings
documents.content: Configuration for ntfy.sh, supported values are here.

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.settings.base-url
documents.content:
Public facing base URL of the service
This setting is required for any of the following features:
attachments (to return a download URL)
e-mail sending (for the topic URL in the email footer)
iOS push notifications for self-hosted servers (to calculate the Firebase poll_request topic)
Matrix Push Gateway (to validate that the pushkey is correct)

documents.title: Option: services.ntfy-sh.user
documents.content: User the ntfy-sh server runs under.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.configText
documents.content: Overridable configuration file contents to use for ntopng. By default, use the contents automatically generated by NixOS.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.enable
documents.content:
Enable ntopng, a high-speed web-based traffic analysis and flow collection tool.
With the default configuration, ntopng monitors all network interfaces and displays its findings at http://localhost:${toString config.services.ntopng.http-port}. Default username and password is admin/admin.
See the {manpage}ntopng(8) manual page and http://www.ntop.org/products/ntop/ for more info.
Note that enabling ntopng will also enable redis (key-value database server) for persistent data storage.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.extraConfig
documents.content: Configuration lines that will be appended to the generated ntopng configuration file. Note that this mechanism does not work when the manual {option}configText option is used.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.httpPort
documents.content: Sets the HTTP port of the embedded web server.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.interfaces
documents.content: List of interfaces to monitor. Use "any" to monitor all interfaces.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.redis.address
documents.content: Redis address - may be a Unix socket or a network host and port.

documents.title: Option: services.ntopng.redis.createInstance
documents.content: Local Redis instance name. Set to null to disable local Redis instance. Defaults to "" for system.stateVersion older than 22.05.

documents.title: Option: services.ntp.enable
documents.content:
Whether to synchronise your machine's time using ntpd, as a peer in the NTP network.
Disables systemd.timesyncd if enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.ntp.extraConfig
documents.content: Additional text appended to {file}ntp.conf.

documents.title: Option: services.ntp.extraFlags
documents.content: Extra flags passed to the ntpd command.

documents.title: Option: services.ntp.restrictDefault
documents.content:
The restriction flags to be set by default.
The default flags prevent external hosts from using ntpd as a DDoS reflector, setting system time, and querying OS/ntpd version. As recommended in section 6.5.1.1.3, answer "No" of https://support.ntp.org/Support/AccessRestrictions

documents.title: Option: services.ntp.restrictSource
documents.content:
The restriction flags to be set on source.
The default flags allow peers to be added by ntpd from configured pool(s), but not by other means.

documents.title: Option: services.ntp.servers
documents.content: The set of NTP servers from which to synchronise.

documents.title: Option: services.ntpd-rs.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Network Time Service (ntpd-rs).

documents.title: Option: services.ntpd-rs.metrics.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable ntpd-rs Prometheus Metrics Exporter.

documents.title: Option: services.ntpd-rs.package
documents.content: The ntpd-rs package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.ntpd-rs.settings
documents.content:
Settings to write to {file}ntp.toml
See https://docs.ntpd-rs.pendulum-project.org/man/ntp.toml.5 for more information about available options.

documents.title: Option: services.ntpd-rs.useNetworkingTimeServers
documents.content: Use source time servers from {var}networking.timeServers in config.

documents.title: Option: services.nullidentdmod.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the nullidentdmod identd daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.nullidentdmod.userid
documents.content: User ID to return. Set to null to return a random string each time.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.adminaddr
documents.content: If set, all recipients to users at either "localhost" (the literal string) or the canonical host name (from the me control attribute) are remapped to this address. This is provided to allow local daemons to be able to send email to "somebody@localhost" and have it go somewhere sensible instead of being bounced by your relay host. To send to multiple addresses, put them all on one line separated by a comma.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.allmailfrom
documents.content: If set, content will override the envelope sender on all messages.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.defaultdomain
documents.content: The content of this attribute is appended to any host name that does not contain a period (except localhost), including defaulthost and idhost. Defaults to the value of the me attribute, if it exists, otherwise the literal name defauldomain.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.defaulthost
documents.content: The content of this attribute is appended to any address that is missing a host name. Defaults to the value of the me control attribute, if it exists, otherwise the literal name defaulthost.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.doublebounceto
documents.content: If the original sender was empty (the original message was a delivery status or disposition notification), the double bounce is sent to the address in this attribute.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.helohost
documents.content: Sets the environment variable $HELOHOST which is used by the SMTP protocol module to set the parameter given to the HELO command. Defaults to the value of the me configuration attribute.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.idhost
documents.content: The content of this attribute is used when building the message-id string for the message. Defaults to the canonicalized value of defaulthost.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.maxpause
documents.content: The maximum time to pause between successive queue runs, in seconds. Defaults to 24 hours (86400).

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.me
documents.content: The fully-qualifiled host name of the computer running nullmailer. Defaults to the literal name me.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.pausetime
documents.content: The minimum time to pause between successive queue runs when there are messages in the queue, in seconds. Defaults to 1 minute (60). Each time this timeout is reached, the timeout is doubled to a maximum of maxpause. After new messages are injected, the timeout is reset. If this is set to 0, nullmailer-send will exit immediately after going through the queue once (one-shot mode).

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.remotes
documents.content:
A list of remote servers to which to send each message. Each line contains a remote host name or address followed by an optional protocol string, separated by white space.
See man 8 nullmailer-send for syntax and available options.
WARNING: This is stored world-readable in the nix store. If you need to specify any secret credentials here, consider using the remotesFile option instead.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.config.sendtimeout
documents.content: The time to wait for a remote module listed above to complete sending a message before killing it and trying again, in seconds. Defaults to 1 hour (3600). If this is set to 0, nullmailer-send will wait forever for messages to complete sending.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable nullmailer daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.group
documents.content: Group to use to run nullmailer-send.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.remotesFile
documents.content:
Path to the remotes control file. This file contains a list of remote servers to which to send each message.
See man 8 nullmailer-send for syntax and available options.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.setSendmail
documents.content: Whether to set the system sendmail to nullmailer's.

documents.title: Option: services.nullmailer.user
documents.content: User to use to run nullmailer-send.

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable nvme-rs, a monitoring service.

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.package
documents.content: The nvme-rs package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings
documents.content: Configuration for nvme-rs in TOML format. See the config.toml example for all available options.

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.check_interval_secs

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.from

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.smtp_password_file
documents.content: File containing SMTP password

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.smtp_port
documents.content: SMTP server port

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.smtp_server
documents.content: SMTP server address

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.smtp_username
documents.content: SMTP username

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.to
documents.content: Recipient email address

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.email.use_tls
documents.content: Use TLS for SMTP connection

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds
documents.content: Threshold configuration for NVMe monitoring

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds.error_threshold
documents.content: Error count warning threshold

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds.spare_warning
documents.content: Available spare warning threshold (%)

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds.temp_critical
documents.content: Temperature critical threshold (°C)

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds.temp_warning
documents.content: Temperature warning threshold (°C)

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds.wear_critical
documents.content: Wear critical threshold (%)

documents.title: Option: services.nvme-rs.settings.thresholds.wear_warning
documents.content: Wear warning threshold (%)

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.acceptInterface

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.bindInterface

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.deniedIPRanges
documents.content: Denied client IP ranges, these gets evaluated after the allowed IP ranges, defaults to all IPv4 addresses: [ "0.0.0.0/0" ] To block all other access than the allowed.

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.enable
documents.content: Enables nylon as a running service upon activation.

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.logging
documents.content: Enable logging, default is no logging.

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.name
documents.content: The name of this nylon instance.

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.nrConnections
documents.content: The number of allowed simultaneous connections to the daemon, default 10.

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.port
documents.content: What port to listen for client requests, default is 1080.

documents.title: Option: services.nylon.<name>.verbosity
documents.content: Enable verbose output, default is to not be verbose.

documents.title: Option: services.nzbget.enable

documents.title: Option: services.nzbget.group

documents.title: Option: services.nzbget.package
documents.content: The nzbget package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.nzbget.settings
documents.content: NZBGet configuration, passed via command line using switch -o. Refer to https://github.com/nzbgetcom/nzbget/blob/develop/nzbget.conf for details on supported values.

documents.content: User account under which NZBGet runs

documents.title: Option: services.nzbhydra2.dataDir
documents.content: The directory where NZBHydra2 stores its data files.

documents.title: Option: services.nzbhydra2.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable NZBHydra2, Usenet meta search.

documents.title: Option: services.nzbhydra2.openFirewall
documents.content: Open ports in the firewall for the NZBHydra2 web interface.

documents.title: Option: services.nzbhydra2.package
documents.content: The nzbhydra2 package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.approvalPrompt
documents.content: OAuth approval_prompt.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.azure.resource
documents.content: The resource that is protected.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.azure.tenant
documents.content: Go to a tenant-specific or common (tenant-independent) endpoint.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.basicAuthPassword
documents.content: The password to set when passing the HTTP Basic Auth header.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.clientID
documents.content: The OAuth Client ID.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.clientSecretFile
documents.content: The path to a file containing the OAuth Client Secret.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.domain
documents.content: Optional cookie domains to force cookies to (ie: .yourcompany.com). The longest domain matching the request's host will be used (or the shortest cookie domain if there is no match).

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.expire
documents.content: Expire timeframe for cookie.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.httpOnly
documents.content: Set HttpOnly cookie flag.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.name
documents.content: The name of the cookie that the oauth_proxy creates.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.refresh
documents.content: Refresh the cookie after this duration; 0 to disable.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.secretFile
documents.content: The path to a file containing the seed string for secure cookies.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.cookie.secure
documents.content: Set secure (HTTPS) cookie flag.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.customTemplatesDir
documents.content: Path to custom HTML templates.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.email.addresses
documents.content: Line-separated email addresses that are allowed to authenticate.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.email.domains
documents.content: Authenticate emails with the specified domains. Use * to authenticate any email.

documents.title: Option: services.oauth2-proxy.enable

otherwise defaults to ollama-cpu

ollama-rocm: supported by most modern AMD GPUs

documents.title: Option: services.onlyoffice.x2t
