documents.title: Option: services.open-web-calendar.calendarSettings
documents.content:
Configure the default calendar.
See the documentation options in https://open-web-calendar.quelltext.eu/host/configure/#configuring-the-default-calendar and https://github.com/niccokunzmann/open-web-calendar/blob/master/open_web_calendar/default_specification.yml.
Individual calendar instances can be further configured outside this module, by specifying the specification_url parameter.

documents.title: Option: services.open-web-calendar.domain
documents.content: The domain under which open-web-calendar is made available

documents.title: Option: services.open-web-calendar.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenWebCalendar service.

documents.title: Option: services.open-web-calendar.package
documents.content: The open-web-calendar package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.open-web-calendar.settings
documents.content:
Configuration for the server. These are set as environment variables to the gunicorn/flask service.
See the documentation options in https://open-web-calendar.quelltext.eu/host/configure/#configuring-the-server.

documents.title: Option: services.open-web-calendar.settings.ALLOWED_HOSTS
documents.content:
The hosts that the Open Web Calendar permits. This is required to mitigate the Host Header Injection vulnerability.
We always set this to the empty list, as Nginx already checks the Host header.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Open-WebUI server.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.environment
documents.content: Extra environment variables for Open-WebUI. For more details see https://docs.openwebui.com/reference/env-configuration

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.environmentFile
documents.content: Environment file to be passed to the systemd service. Useful for passing secrets to the service to prevent them from being world-readable in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.host
documents.content: The host address which the Open-WebUI server HTTP interface listens to.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to open the firewall for Open-WebUI. This adds services.open-webui.port to networking.firewall.allowedTCPPorts.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.package
documents.content: The open-webui package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.port
documents.content: Which port the Open-WebUI server listens to.

documents.title: Option: services.open-webui.stateDir
documents.content: State directory of Open-WebUI.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.afsdb
documents.content: Resolve cells via AFSDB DNS records.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cache.blocks
documents.content: Cache size in 1KB blocks.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cache.chunksize
documents.content: Size of each cache chunk given in powers of 2. 0 resets the chunk size to its default values (13 (8 KB) for memcache, 18-20 (256 KB to 1 MB) for diskcache). Maximum value is 30. Important performance parameter. Set to higher values when dealing with large files.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cache.directory
documents.content: Cache directory.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cache.diskless
documents.content: Use in-memory cache for diskless machines. Has no real performance benefit anymore.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cellName
documents.content: Cell name.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cellServDB
documents.content: This cell's database server records, added to the global CellServDB. See {manpage}CellServDB(5) man page for syntax. Ignored when afsdb is set to true.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cellServDB.<name>.*.dnsname
documents.content: DNS full-qualified domain name of a database server

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.cellServDB.<name>.*.ip
documents.content: IP Address of a database server

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.crypt
documents.content: Whether to enable (weak) protocol encryption.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.daemons
documents.content: Number of daemons to serve user requests. Numbers higher than 6 usually do no increase performance. Default is sufficient for up to five concurrent users.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the OpenAFS client.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.fakestat
documents.content: Return fake data on stat() calls. If true, always do so. If false, only do so for cross-cell mounts (as these are potentially expensive).

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.globalCellServDBFile
documents.content: Global CellServDB file to be deployed. Set to null to only deploy the cells in cellServDB. Any cells defined in cellServDB will override cells in the global file.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.inumcalc
documents.content: Inode calculation method. compat is computationally less expensive, but md5 greatly reduces the likelihood of inode collisions in larger scenarios involving multiple cells mounted into one AFS space.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.mountPoint
documents.content: Mountpoint of the AFS file tree, conventionally /afs. When set to a different value, only cross-cells that use the same value can be accessed.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.packages.module
documents.content: OpenAFS kernel module package. MUST match the userland package!

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.packages.programs
documents.content: OpenAFS programs package. MUST match the kernel module package!

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.sparse
documents.content: Minimal cell list in /afs.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsClient.startDisconnected
documents.content: Start up in disconnected mode. You need to execute fs disco online (as root) to switch to connected mode. Useful for roaming devices.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.advertisedAddresses
documents.content: List of IP addresses this server is advertised under. See {manpage}NetInfo(5)

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.cellName
documents.content: Cell name, this server will serve.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.cellServDB
documents.content: Definition of all cell-local database server machines. If a single list is provided, it will be used as the servers for cellName.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.cellServDB.<name>.*.dnsname
documents.content: DNS full-qualified domain name of a database server

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.cellServDB.<name>.*.ip
documents.content: IP Address of a database server

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.dottedPrincipals
documents.content: If enabled, allow principal names containing (.) dots. Enabling this has security implications!

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the OpenAFS server. An OpenAFS server needs a complex setup. So, be aware that enabling this service and setting some options does not give you a turn-key-ready solution. You need at least a running Kerberos 5 setup, as OpenAFS relies on it for authentication. See the Guide "QuickStartUnix" coming with pkgs.openafs.doc for complete setup instructions.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.package
documents.content: The openafs package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.buserverArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the buserver process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.cellServDB
documents.content: Definition of all cell-local backup database server machines. Use this when your cell uses less backup database servers than other database server machines.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.cellServDB.<name>.*.dnsname
documents.content: DNS full-qualified domain name of a database server

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.cellServDB.<name>.*.ip
documents.content: IP Address of a database server

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable the backup server role. When using OpenAFS built-in buserver, use in conjunction with the database role to maintain the Backup Database. Normally only used in conjunction with tape storage or IBM's Tivoli Storage Manager.
For a modern backup server, enable this role and see {option}enableFabs .

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.enableFabs
documents.content: Whether to enable FABS, the flexible AFS backup system. It stores volumes as dump files, relying on other pre-existing backup solutions for handling them .

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.fabsArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the fabsys process. See {manpage}fabsys_server(1) and {manpage}fabsys_config(1).

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.backup.fabsExtraConfig
documents.content: Additional configuration parameters for the FABS backup server.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.database.enable
documents.content:
Database server role, maintains the Volume Location Database, Protection Database (and Backup Database, see backup role). There can be multiple servers in the database role for replication, which then need reliable network connection to each other.
Servers in this role appear in AFSDB DNS records or the CellServDB.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.database.ptserverArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the ptserver process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.database.vlserverArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the vlserver process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.fileserver.enable
documents.content: Fileserver role, serves files and volumes from its local storage.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.fileserver.fileserverArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the dafileserver process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.fileserver.salvagerArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the dasalvager process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.fileserver.salvageserverArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the salvageserver process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.roles.fileserver.volserverArgs
documents.content: Arguments to the davolserver process. See its man page.

documents.title: Option: services.openafsServer.udpPacketSize
documents.content: UDP packet size to use in Bytes. Higher values can speed up communications. The default of 1 MB is a sufficient in most cases. Make sure to increase the kernel's UDP buffer size accordingly via net.core(w|r|opt)mem_max sysctl.

documents.title: Option: services.openarena.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenArena game server.

documents.title: Option: services.openarena.extraFlags
documents.content: Extra flags to pass to {command}oa_ded

documents.title: Option: services.openarena.openPorts
documents.content: Whether to open firewall ports for OpenArena

documents.title: Option: services.openarena.package
documents.content: The openarena package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenBao daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.extraArgs
documents.content: Additional arguments given to OpenBao.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.package
documents.content: The openbao package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.settings
documents.content:
Settings of OpenBao.
See documentation for more details.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.settings.listener
documents.content: Configure a listener for responding to requests.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.settings.listener.<name>.address
documents.content: The TCP address or UNIX socket path to listen on.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.settings.listener.<name>.type
documents.content: The listener type to enable.

documents.title: Option: services.openbao.settings.ui
documents.content: Whether to enable the OpenBao web UI.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.address
documents.content: Web server bind address.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenCloud.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.environment
documents.content:
Extra environment variables to set for the service.
Use this to set configuration that may affect multiple microservices.
Set OC_INSECURE = "false" if you want OpenCloud to terminate TLS.
Configuration provided here will override settings.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.environmentFile
documents.content:
An environment file as defined in {manpage}systemd.exec(5).
Use this to inject secrets, e.g. database or auth credentials out of band.
Configuration provided here will override settings and environment.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.group
documents.content: The group to run OpenCloud under. By default, a group named opencloud will be created.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.idpWebPackage
documents.content: The idp-web package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.package
documents.content: The opencloud package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.port
documents.content: Web server port.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.settings
documents.content:
Additional YAML configuration for OpenCloud services.
Every item in this attrset will be mapped to a .yaml file in /etc/opencloud.
The possible config options are currently not well documented, see source code: https://github.com/opencloud-eu/opencloud/blob/main/pkg/config/config.go

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.stateDir
documents.content: OpenCloud data directory.

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.url
documents.content: Web interface root public URL, including scheme and port (if non-default).

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.user
documents.content: The user to run OpenCloud as. By default, a user named opencloud will be created whose home directory is .

documents.title: Option: services.opencloud.webPackage
documents.content: The web package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.configFile
documents.content: Additional opendkim configuration as a file.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.domains
documents.content: Local domains set (see {manpage}opendkim(8) for more information on datasets). Messages from them are signed, not verified.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenDKIM sender authentication system.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.group
documents.content: Group for the daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.keyPath
documents.content: The path that opendkim should put its generated private keys into. The DNS settings will be found in this directory with the name selector.txt.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.selector
documents.content: Selector to use when signing.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.settings
documents.content: Additional opendkim configuration

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.socket
documents.content: Socket which is used for communication with OpenDKIM.

documents.title: Option: services.opendkim.user
documents.content: User for the daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.discoverPortal
documents.content: Portal to discover targets on

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the openiscsi iscsi daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.enableAutoLoginOut
documents.content: Whether to enable automatic login and logout of all automatic targets. You probably do not want this .

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.extraConfig
documents.content: Lines to append to default iscsid.conf

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.extraConfigFile
documents.content: Append an additional file's contents to /etc/iscsid.conf. Use a non-store path and store passwords in this file.

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.name
documents.content: Name of this iscsi initiator

documents.title: Option: services.openiscsi.package
documents.content: The openiscsi package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.configDir
documents.content: Use this config directory instead of generating one from the settings option. Overrides all NixOS settings.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.declarativeContents
documents.content:
Declarative contents for the LDAP database, in LDIF format by suffix.
All data will be erased when starting the LDAP server. Modifications to the database are not prevented, they are just dropped on the next reboot of the server. Performance-wise the database and indexes are rebuilt on each server startup, so this will slow down server startup, especially with large databases.
Note that the root of the DB must be defined in services.openldap.settings and the olcDbDirectory must begin with "/var/lib/openldap".

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the ldap server.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.group
documents.content: Group account under which slapd runs.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.mutableConfig
documents.content: Whether to allow writable on-line configuration. If true, the NixOS settings will only be used to initialize the OpenLDAP configuration if it does not exist, and are subsequently ignored.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.package
documents.content: The openldap package to use. This can be used to, for example, set an OpenLDAP package with custom overrides to enable modules or other functionality.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.settings
documents.content: Configuration for OpenLDAP, in OLC format

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.settings.attrs
documents.content: Attributes of the parent entry.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.settings.children
documents.content: Child entries of the current entry, with recursively the same structure.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.settings.includes
documents.content: LDIF files to include after the parent's attributes but before its children.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.urlList
documents.content: URL list slapd should listen on.

documents.title: Option: services.openldap.user
documents.content: User account under which slapd runs.

documents.title: Option: services.openntpd.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenNTP time synchronization server.

documents.title: Option: services.openntpd.extraConfig
documents.content: Additional text appended to {file}openntpd.conf.

documents.title: Option: services.openntpd.extraOptions
documents.content: Extra options used when launching openntpd.

documents.title: Option: services.openntpd.servers
documents.content: The set of NTP servers from which to synchronise.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.dataDir
documents.content: Data directory for OpenSearch. If you change this, you need to manually create the directory. You also need to create the opensearch user and group, or change and to existing ones with access to the directory.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable OpenSearch.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.extraCmdLineOptions
documents.content: Extra command line options for the OpenSearch launcher.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.extraJavaOptions
documents.content: Extra command line options for Java.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.group
documents.content: The group OpenSearch runs as. Should be left at default unless you have very specific needs.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.logging
documents.content: opensearch logging configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.package
documents.content: The OpenSearch package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.restartIfChanged
documents.content: Automatically restart the service on config change. This can be set to false to defer restarts on a server or cluster. Please consider the security implications of inadvertently running an older version, and the possibility of unexpected behavior caused by inconsistent versions across a cluster when disabling this option.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings
documents.content: OpenSearch configuration.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings."cluster.name"
documents.content: The name of the cluster.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings."discovery.type"
documents.content: The type of discovery to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings."http.port"
documents.content: The port to listen on for HTTP traffic.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings."network.host"
documents.content: Which port this service should listen on.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings."plugins.security.disabled"
documents.content: Whether to enable the security plugin, plugins.security.ssl.transport.keystore_filepath or plugins.security.ssl.transport.server.pemcert_filepath and plugins.security.ssl.transport.client.pemcert_filepath must be set for this plugin to be enabled.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.settings."transport.port"
documents.content: The port to listen on for transport traffic.

documents.title: Option: services.opensearch.user
documents.content: The user OpenSearch runs as. Should be left at default unless you have very specific needs.

documents.title: Option: services.opensmtpd.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the OpenSMTPD server.

documents.title: Option: services.opensmtpd.extraServerArgs
documents.content: Extra command line arguments provided when the smtpd process is started.

documents.title: Option: services.opensmtpd.package
documents.content: The opensmtpd package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opensmtpd.procPackages
documents.content:
Packages to search for filters, tables, queues, and schedulers.
Add packages here if you want to use them as as such, for example from the opensmtpd-table-* packages.

documents.title: Option: services.opensmtpd.serverConfiguration
documents.content: The contents of the smtpd.conf configuration file. See the OpenSMTPD documentation for syntax information.

documents.title: Option: services.opensmtpd.setSendmail
documents.content: Whether to set the system sendmail to OpenSMTPD's.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.configFile
documents.content: Path to JSON config file. See: https://github.com/evilsocket/opensnitch/blob/master/daemon/data/default-config.json If this option is set, it will override any configuration done in options.services.opensnitch.settings.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Opensnitch application firewall.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.package
documents.content: The opensnitch package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.rules
documents.content: Declarative configuration of firewall rules. All rules will be stored in /var/lib/opensnitch/rules by default. Rules path can be configured with settings.Rules.Path. See upstream documentation for available options.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.settings
documents.content: opensnitchd configuration. Refer to upstream documentation for details on supported values.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.settings.Audit.AudispSocketPath
documents.content: Configure audit socket path. Used when settings.ProcMonitorMethod is set to audit.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.settings.Ebpf.ModulesPath
documents.content: Configure eBPF modules path. Used when settings.ProcMonitorMethod is set to ebpf.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.settings.Firewall
documents.content: Which firewall backend to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.settings.ProcMonitorMethod
documents.content: Which process monitoring method to use.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.settings.Rules.Path
documents.content: Path to the directory where firewall rules can be found and will get stored by the NixOS module.

documents.title: Option: services.opensnitch.upstreamDefaults
documents.content:
Whether to base the config declared in {option}services.opensnitch.settings on the upstream example config (https://github.com/evilsocket/opensnitch/blob/master/daemon/data/default-config.json)
Disable this if you want to declare your opensnitch config from scratch.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.allowSFTP
documents.content: Whether to enable the SFTP subsystem in the SSH daemon. This enables the use of commands such as {command}sftp and {command}sshfs.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommand
documents.content: Specifies a program to be used to look up the user's public keys. The program must be owned by root, not writable by group or others and specified by an absolute path.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.authorizedKeysCommandUser
documents.content: Specifies the user under whose account the AuthorizedKeysCommand is run. It is recommended to use a dedicated user that has no other role on the host than running authorized keys commands.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.authorizedKeysFiles
documents.content:
Specify the rules for which files to read on the host.
This is an advanced option. If you're looking to configure user keys, you can generally use or .
These are paths relative to the host root file system or home directories and they are subject to certain token expansion rules. See AuthorizedKeysFile in man sshd_config for details.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.authorizedKeysInHomedir
documents.content:
Enables the use of the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file.
Otherwise, the only files trusted by default are those in /etc/ssh/authorized_keys.d, i.e. SSH keys from .

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the OpenSSH secure shell daemon, which allows secure remote logins.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.enableRecommendedAlgorithms
documents.content:
Use algorithms curated and recommended by NixOS.
Set to false to use upstream's default algorithms.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.extraConfig
documents.content: Verbatim contents of {file}sshd_config.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.generateHostKeys
documents.content:
Whether to generate SSH host keys.
This can be enabled explicitly if you want to generate host keys but don't want to enable the SSH daemon.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.hostKeys
documents.content: NixOS can automatically generate SSH host keys. This option specifies the path, type and size of each key. See {manpage}ssh-keygen(1) for supported types and sizes.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.knownHosts
documents.content: Alias of {option}programs.ssh.knownHosts.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.knownHosts.<name>.certAuthority
documents.content: This public key is an SSH certificate authority, rather than an individual host's key.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.knownHosts.<name>.extraHostNames
documents.content: A list of additional host names and/or IP numbers used for accessing the host's ssh service. This list is ignored if hostNames is set explicitly.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.knownHosts.<name>.hostNames
documents.content: A list of host names and/or IP numbers used for accessing the host's ssh service. This list includes the name of the containing knownHosts attribute by default for convenience. If you wish to configure multiple host keys for the same host use multiple knownHosts entries with different attribute names and the same hostNames list.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.knownHosts.<name>.publicKey
documents.content: The public key data for the host. You can fetch a public key from a running SSH server with the {command}ssh-keyscan command. The public key should not include any host names, only the key type and the key itself.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.knownHosts.<name>.publicKeyFile
documents.content: The path to the public key file for the host. The public key file is read at build time and saved in the Nix store. You can fetch a public key file from a running SSH server with the {command}ssh-keyscan command. The content of the file should follow the same format as described for the publicKey option. Only a single key is supported. If a host has multiple keys, use {option}programs.ssh.knownHostsFiles instead.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.listenAddresses
documents.content:
List of addresses and ports to listen on (ListenAddress directive in config). If port is not specified for address sshd will listen on all ports specified by ports option. NOTE: this will override default listening on all local addresses and port 22. NOTE: setting this option won't automatically enable given ports in firewall configuration. NOTE: If the IP address is not available at boot time, the following has to be added to make sure sshd will wait for dhcp configuration:
See the following issue for details: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/105570

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.listenAddresses.*.addr
documents.content: Host, IPv4 or IPv6 address to listen to.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.listenAddresses.*.port
documents.content: Port to listen to.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.moduliFile
documents.content: Path to moduli file to install in /etc/ssh/moduli. If this option is unset, then the moduli file shipped with OpenSSH will be used.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to automatically open the specified ports in the firewall.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.package
documents.content: OpenSSH package to use for sshd.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.ports
documents.content: Specifies on which ports the SSH daemon listens.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.settings
documents.content: Configuration for sshd_config(5).

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.settings.AcceptEnv
documents.content: Specifies what environment variables sent by the client will be copied into the session's environment. The TERM environment variable is always accepted whenever the client requests a pseudo-terminal as it is required by the protocol.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.settings.AllowGroups
documents.content: If specified, login is allowed only for users part of the listed groups. See {manpage}sshd_config(5) for details.

documents.title: Option: services.openssh.settings.AllowUsers

documents.title: Option: services.paperless.openMPThreadingWorkaround
documents.content:
Whether to enable a workaround for document classifier timeouts.
Paperless uses OpenBLAS via scikit-learn for document classification.
The default is to use threading for OpenMP but this would cause the document classifier to spin on one core seemingly indefinitely if there are large amounts of classes per classification; causing it to effectively never complete due to running into timeouts.
This sets OMP_NUM_THREADS to 1 in order to mitigate the issue. See https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/240591 for more information .

documents.title: Option: services.paperless.passwordFile
documents.content:
A file containing the superuser password.
A superuser is required to access the web interface. If unset, you can create a superuser manually by running paperless-manage createsuperuser.
The default superuser name is admin. To change it, set option {option}settings.PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER. WARNING: When changing the superuser name after the initial setup, the old superuser will continue to exist.
To disable login for the web interface, set the following: settings.PAPERLESS_AUTO_LOGIN_USERNAME = "admin";. WARNING: Only use this on a trusted system without internet access to Paperless.

PDFs are imported periodically via cronjob and successfully imported files are automatically deleted from the consume directory.

documents.title: Option: services.pgbouncer.settings.pgbouncer.ignore_startup_parameters
documents.content:
By default, PgBouncer allows only parameters it can keep track of in startup packets: client_encoding, datestyle, timezone and standard_conforming_strings.
All others parameters will raise an error. To allow others parameters, they can be specified here, so that PgBouncer knows that they are handled by the admin and it can ignore them.
If you need to specify multiple values, use a comma-separated list.
IMPORTANT: When using prometheus-pgbouncer-exporter, you need: extra_float_digits https://github.com/prometheus-community/pgbouncer_exporter#pgbouncer-configuration

documents.title: Option: services.pgbouncer.settings.pgbouncer.listen_addr
documents.content:
Specifies a list (comma-separated) of addresses where to listen for TCP connections. You may also use * meaning “listen on all addresses”. When not set, only Unix socket connections are accepted.
Addresses can be specified numerically (IPv4/IPv6) or by name.

documents.content: Which port to listen on. Applies to both TCP and Unix sockets.

documents.title: Option: services.pgbouncer.settings.pgbouncer.max_client_conn
documents.content:
Maximum number of client connections allowed.
When this setting is increased, then the file descriptor limits in the operating system might also have to be increased. Note that the number of file descriptors potentially used is more than maxClientConn. If each user connects under its own user name to the server, the theoretical maximum used is: maxClientConn + (max pool_size * total databases * total users)
If a database user is specified in the connection string (all users connect under the same user name), the theoretical maximum is: maxClientConn + (max pool_size * total databases)
The theoretical maximum should never be reached, unless somebody deliberately crafts a special load for it. Still, it means you should set the number of file descriptors to a safely high number.

documents.title: Option: services.pgbouncer.settings.pgbouncer.max_db_connections
documents.content:
Do not allow more than this many server connections per database (regardless of user). This considers the PgBouncer database that the client has connected to, not the PostgreSQL database of the outgoing connection.
This can also be set per database in the [databases] section.
Note that when you hit the limit, closing a client connection to one pool will not immediately allow a server connection to be established for another pool, because the server connection for the first pool is still open. Once the server connection closes (due to idle timeout), a new server connection will immediately be opened for the waiting pool.
0 = unlimited

documents.title: Option: services.pgbouncer.settings.pgbouncer.max_user_connections
documents.content:
Do not allow more than this many server connections per user (regardless of database). This considers the PgBouncer user that is associated with a pool, which is either the user specified for the server connection or in absence of that the user the client has connected as.
This can also be set per user in the [users] section.
Note that when you hit the limit, closing a client connection to one pool will not immediately allow a server connection to be established for another pool, because the server connection for the first pool is still open. Once the server connection closes (due to idle timeout), a new server connection will immediately be opened for the waiting pool.
0 = unlimited

documents.title: Option: services.pgbouncer.settings.pgbouncer.pool_mode
documents.content:
Specifies when a server connection can be reused by other clients.
session Server is released back to pool after client disconnects. Default. transaction Server is released back to pool after transaction finishes. statement Server is released back to pool after query finishes. Transactions spanning multiple statements are disallowed in this mode.

Note that WirePlumber (and PipeWire) use dotted attribute names like device.product.id. These are not nested, but flat objects for WirePlumber/PipeWire, so to write these in nix expressions, remember to quote them like "device.product.id". Have a look at the example for this.

documents.title: Option: services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraScripts
documents.content:
Additional scripts for WirePlumber to be used by configuration files.
Every item in this attrset becomes a separate lua file with the path relative to the scripts directory specified in the name of the item. The scripts get passed to the WirePlumber service via the XDG_DATA_DIRS variable. Scripts specified here are preferred over those shipped with WirePlumber if they occupy the same relative path.
For a script to be loaded, it needs to be specified as part of a component, and that component needs to be required by an active profile (e.g. main). Components can be defined in config files either via extraConfig or configPackages.
For the hello-world example, you'd have to add the following extraConfig:
See also:
Location of scripts
Components & Profiles
Migration - Loading custom scripts

If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is enabled for all server blocks on this IP. See https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061.

documents.content: Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol. This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;. documents.content:
Path to an environment file to be loaded. This can be used to securely store tokens and secrets outside of the world-readable Nix store.
See PocketID environment variables.
Example contents of the file: MAXMIND_LICENSE_KEY=your-license-key
Alternatively you can use services.pocket-id.credentials to define each variable in separate files.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.group
documents.content: Group account under which Pocket ID runs.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.package
documents.content: The pocket-id package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.settings
documents.content:
Environment variables to be passed.
See PocketID environment variables.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.settings.ANALYTICS_DISABLED
documents.content:
Whether to disable analytics.
See the analytics documentation.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.settings.APP_URL
documents.content: The URL where you will access the app.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.settings.TRUST_PROXY
documents.content: Whether the app is behind a reverse proxy.

documents.title: Option: services.pocket-id.user
documents.content: User account under which Pocket ID runs.

documents.title: Option: services.podgrab.dataDirectory
documents.content: Directory to store downloads.

documents.title: Option: services.podgrab.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Podgrab, a self-hosted podcast manager.

documents.title: Option: services.podgrab.group
documents.content: Group under which Podgrab runs, and which owns the download directory.

documents.title: Option: services.podgrab.passwordFile
documents.content: The path to a file containing the PASSWORD environment variable definition for Podgrab's authentication.

documents.title: Option: services.podgrab.port
documents.content: The port on which Podgrab will listen for incoming HTTP traffic.

documents.title: Option: services.podgrab.user
documents.content: User under which Podgrab runs, and which owns the download directory.

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Polaris Music Server.

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.extraGroups
documents.content: Polaris' auxiliary groups.

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.group
documents.content: Group under which Polaris is run.

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.openFirewall
documents.content: Open the configured port in the firewall.

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.package
documents.content: The polaris package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.port
documents.content: The port which the Polaris REST api and web UI should listen to. Note: polaris is hardcoded to listen to the hostname "0.0.0.0".

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.settings
documents.content: Contents for the TOML Polaris config, applied each start. Although poorly documented, an example may be found here: test-config.toml

documents.title: Option: services.polaris.user
documents.content: User account under which Polaris runs.

documents.title: Option: services.pomerium.configFile
documents.content: Path to Pomerium config YAML. If set, overrides services.pomerium.settings.

documents.title: Option: services.pomerium.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable the Pomerium authenticating reverse proxy.

documents.title: Option: services.pomerium.secretsFile
documents.content: Path to file containing secrets for Pomerium, in systemd EnvironmentFile format. See the {manpage}systemd.exec(5) man page.

documents.title: Option: services.pomerium.settings
documents.content:
The contents of Pomerium's config.yaml, in Nix expressions.
Specifying configFile will override this in its entirety.
See the Pomerium configuration reference for more information about what to put here.

documents.title: Option: services.pomerium.useACMEHost
documents.content:
If set, use a NixOS-generated ACME certificate with the specified name.
Note that this will require you to use a non-HTTP-based challenge, or disable Pomerium's in-built HTTP redirect server by setting http_redirect_addr to null and use a different HTTP server for serving the challenge response.
If you're using an HTTP-based challenge, you should use the Pomerium-native autocert option instead.

documents.title: Option: services.porn-vault.autoStart
documents.content: Whether to start porn-vault automatically.

documents.title: Option: services.porn-vault.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Porn-Vault.

documents.title: Option: services.porn-vault.openFirewall
documents.content: Whether to open the Porn-Vault port in the firewall.

documents.title: Option: services.porn-vault.package
documents.content: The porn-vault package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.porn-vault.port
documents.content: Which port Porn-Vault will use.

documents.title: Option: services.porn-vault.settings
documents.content:
Configuration for Porn-Vault. The attributes are serialized to JSON in config.json.
See https://gitlab.com/porn-vault/porn-vault/-/blob/dev/config.example.json

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.dex.enable
documents.content:
Whether to enable Dex ldap connector.
To activate dex, first a search user must be created in the Portunus web ui and then the password must to be set as the DEX_SEARCH_USER_PASSWORD environment variable in the setting .

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.dex.oidcClients
documents.content:
List of OIDC clients.
The OIDC secret must be set as the DEX_CLIENT_${id} environment variable in the setting.
::: {.note} Make sure the id only contains characters that are allowed in an environment variable name, e.g. no -. :::

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.dex.oidcClients.*.callbackURL
documents.content: URL where the OIDC client should redirect

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.dex.oidcClients.*.id
documents.content: ID of the OIDC client

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.dex.port
documents.content: Port where dex should listen on.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.domain
documents.content: Subdomain which gets reverse proxied to Portunus webserver.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Portunus, a self-contained user/group management and authentication service for LDAP.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.group
documents.content: Group account under which Portunus runs its webserver.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.ldap.group
documents.content: Group account under which Portunus runs its LDAP server.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.ldap.package
documents.content: The openldap package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.ldap.searchUserName
documents.content: The login name of the search user. This user account must be configured in Portunus either manually or via seeding.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.ldap.suffix
documents.content: The DN of the topmost entry in your LDAP directory. Please refer to the Portunus documentation for more information on how this impacts the structure of the LDAP directory.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.ldap.tls
documents.content:
Whether to enable LDAPS protocol. This also adds two entries to the /etc/hosts file to point to localhost, so that CLIs and programs can use ldaps protocol and verify the certificate without opening the firewall port for the protocol.
This requires a TLS certificate for to be configured via .

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.ldap.user
documents.content: User account under which Portunus runs its LDAP server.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.package
documents.content: The portunus package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.port
documents.content:
Port where the Portunus webserver should listen on.
This must be put behind a TLS-capable reverse proxy because Portunus only listens on localhost.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.seedPath
documents.content: Path to a portunus seed file in json format. See https://github.com/majewsky/portunus#seeding-users-and-groups-from-static-configuration for available options.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.seedSettings
documents.content: Seed settings for users and groups. See upstream for format https://github.com/majewsky/portunus#seeding-users-and-groups-from-static-configuration

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.stateDir
documents.content: Path where Portunus stores its state.

documents.title: Option: services.portunus.user
documents.content: User account under which Portunus runs its webserver.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable Porxie, an ATProto blob proxy for secure content delivery.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.environmentFiles
documents.content: Files to load environment variables from. Use for secrets such as {env}PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD and {env}PORXIE_POLICY_REQUEST_HEADERS.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.package
documents.content: The porxie package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings
documents.content:
Configuration for Porxie as environment variables. See the README for detailed information about application configuration.
Secrets such as {option}settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD should be set via {option}environmentFiles rather than here, as values set here will be readable in the Nix store.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_ALLOWED_MIMETYPES
documents.content:
Blob mimetypes that can be served. Wildcards are supported "/", "image/*", etc.
Validation is done loosely via content sniffing. Further validation can be done by a layer above this proxy, such as an image transformation service. When inference fails, the blob's type falls back to application/octet-stream. When that type is allowed, blobs failing inference can still be served.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_CACHE_HEADER
documents.content:
The Cache-Control header value to send alongside blob responses.
This does not affect internal cache lifetimes, only how downstream clients such as CDNs and browsers are instructed to cache responses.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_HTTP_TIMEOUT
documents.content: Maximum duration before blob fetch requests are timed out.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_MAX_SIZE
documents.content:
Maximum blob size that can be served.
This value cannot be set higher than the system's total memory.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_PROCESSING_TIMEOUT
documents.content: Maximum duration a blob can be processed by this server before aborting.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_ALLOCATION
documents.content:
Total memory allocation for the internal cache.
Blobs are cached using an LFU policy. The most frequently requested blobs are kept longest when the cache reaches maximum size.
For production deployments, a CDN or caching layer in front of this server is recommended for lower latency and better global availability.
The minimum value is 8mb and the maximum is the system's total memory.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_BLOB_TTI
documents.content: How long blobs can be idle in the cache before expiring.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_IDENTITY_TTL
documents.content: How long identity lookups (DID resolution, etc.) can be cached before expiring.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_OWNERSHIP_TTL
documents.content: How long blob ownership can be cached before expiring.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_POLICY_TTL
documents.content: How long policy decisions can be cached before expiring.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_IDENTITY_PLC_URL
documents.content: URL of the PLC instance used for did:plc lookups.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_FAIL_OPEN
documents.content:
Allow requests to proceed even if the policy service is unavailable.
Warning: enabling this means restricted blobs may be served when the policy service is unavailable.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_REQUEST_HEADERS
documents.content:
Headers sent alongside requests to the policy service.
Each header must be in the format Name: value.
As pipes are used as a delimiter, they cannot be contained in headers.
Should be set via {option}environmentFiles for sensitive values such as API keys.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_URL
documents.content:
Policy service URL that DID+CID pairs will be checked against.
Requests are sent via XRPC to <url>/xrpc/dev.blooym.porxie.getBlobPolicy.

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADDRESS
documents.content:
Address to bind the server to.
Use the ip: prefix for an IP address (e.g. ip:127.0.0.1:6314), or on UNIX systems, the unix: prefix for a UNIX socket path (e.g. unix:/run/porxie/porxie.sock).

documents.title: Option: services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD
documents.content:
Admin password for authenticating privileged requests.
Authenticated requests always expect the username admin as per specification.
When not set, authenticated endpoints will be unavailable.
Should be set via {option}environmentFiles rather than directly.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.configurePostfix
documents.content: Whether to configure the required settings to use postfix-tlspol in the local Postfix instance.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable postfix-tlspol.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.package
documents.content: The postfix-tlspol package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings
documents.content:
The postfix-tlspol configuration file as a Nix attribute set.
See the reference documentation for possible options. https://github.com/Zuplu/postfix-tlspol/blob/main/configs/config.default.yaml

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings.dns.address
documents.content:
IP and port to your DNS resolver.
Uses resolvers from /etc/resolv.conf if unset.
::: {.note} The configured DNS resolver must validate DNSSEC signatures. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.address
documents.content: Path or address/port where postfix-tlspol binds its socket to.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.cache-file
documents.content: Path to the cache file.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.log-level
documents.content: Log level

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.prefetch
documents.content: Whether to prefetch DNS records when the TTL of a cached record is about to expire.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.socket-permissions
documents.content:
Permissions to the UNIX socket, if configured.
::: {.note} Due to hardening on the systemd unit the socket can never be created world readable/writable. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.aliasFiles
documents.content: Aliases' tables to be compiled and placed into /var/lib/postfix/conf.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.aliasMapType
documents.content: The format the alias map should have. Use regexp if you want to use regular expressions.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.canonical
documents.content: Entries for the {manpage}canonical(5) table.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.dnsBlacklistOverrides
documents.content: contents of check_client_access for overriding dnsBlacklists

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.dnsBlacklists
documents.content: dns blacklist servers to use with smtpd_client_restrictions

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.enable
documents.content: Whether to run the Postfix mail server.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.enableHeaderChecks
documents.content: Whether to enable postfix header checks

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.enableSmtp
documents.content:
Whether to enable the smtp service configured in the master.cf.
This service listens for plain text SMTP connections on port 25 and supports explicit TLS via StartTLS.
It is the primary port used by SMTP servers to exchange mail.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.enableSubmissions
documents.content:
Whether to enable the submissions service configured in master.cf.
This service listen for implicit TLS connections on port 465.
::: {.info} Per RFC 8314 implicit TLS is recommended for mail submission. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.extraAliases
documents.content: Additional entries to put verbatim into aliases file, cf. man-page {manpage}aliases(8).

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.extraHeaderChecks
documents.content: Extra lines to /etc/postfix/header_checks file.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.extraMasterConf
documents.content: Extra lines to append to the generated master.cf file.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.group
documents.content: What to call the Postfix group (must be used only for postfix).

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.headerChecks
documents.content: Postfix header checks.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.headerChecks.*.action
documents.content: The action to be executed when the pattern is matched

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.headerChecks.*.pattern
documents.content: A regexp pattern matching the header

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.localRecipients
documents.content: List of accepted local users. Specify a bare username, an "@domain.tld" wild-card, or a complete "user@domain.tld" address. If set, these names end up in the local recipient map -- see the {manpage}local(8) man-page -- and effectively replace the system user database lookup that's otherwise used by default.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.mapFiles
documents.content: Maps to be compiled and placed into /var/lib/postfix/conf.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.package
documents.content: The postfix package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.postmasterAlias
documents.content: Who should receive postmaster e-mail. Multiple values can be added by separating values with comma.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.rootAlias
documents.content: Who should receive root e-mail. Blank for no redirection. Multiple values can be added by separating values with comma.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.setSendmail
documents.content: Whether to set the system sendmail to postfix's.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.setgidGroup
documents.content: How to call postfix setgid group (for postdrop). Should be uniquely used group.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main
documents.content:
The main.cf configuration file as key value set.
Null values will not be rendered.
::: {.tip} Check postconf -d for the default values of all settings. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.message_size_limit
documents.content:
Maximum size of an email message in bytes.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#message_size_limit

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.mydestination
documents.content:
List of domain names intended for local delivery using /etc/passwd and /etc/aliases.
::: {.warning} Do not include virtual domains in this list. :::
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mydestination

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.myhostname
documents.content:
The internet hostname of this mail system.
Leave unset to default to the system hostname with the {option}mydomain suffix.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#myhostname

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.mynetworks
documents.content:
List of trusted remote SMTP clients, that are allowed to relay mail.
Leave unset to let Postfix populate this list based on the {option}mynetworks_style setting.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mynetworks

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.mynetworks_style
documents.content:
The method used for generating the default value for {option}mynetworks, if that option is unset.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mynetworks_style

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.recipient_delimiter
documents.content:
Set of characters used as the delimiters for address extensions.
This allows creating different forwarding rules per extension.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#recipient_delimiter

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.relay_domains
documents.content:
List of domains delivered via the relay transport.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#relay_domains

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.relayhost
documents.content:
List of hosts to use for relaying outbound mail.
::: {.note} Putting the hostname in angled brackets, e.g. [relay.example.com], turns off MX and SRV lookups for the hostname. :::
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#relayhost

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.smtp_tls_CAfile
documents.content:
File containing CA certificates of root CAs trusted to sign either remote SMTP server certificates or intermediate CA certificates.
Defaults to the system CA bundle that is managed through the security.pki options.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtp_tls_CAfile

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.smtp_tls_security_level
documents.content:
The client TLS security level.
::: {.tip} Use dane with a local DNSSEC validating DNS resolver enabled. :::
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtp_tls_security_level

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_chain_files
documents.content:
List of paths to the server private keys and certificates.
::: {.caution} The order of items matters and a private key must always be followed by the corresponding certificate. :::
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtpd_tls_chain_files

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_security_level
documents.content:
The server TLS security level. Enable TLS by configuring at least may.
https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtpd_tls_security_level

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master
documents.content:
The {file}master.cf configuration file as an attribute set of service defitions
::: {.tip} Check https://www.postfix.org/master.5.html for possible settings. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.args
documents.content: Arguments to pass to the {option}command. There is no shell processing involved and shell syntax is passed verbatim to the process.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.chroot
documents.content: Whether the service is chrooted to have only access to the {option}services.postfix.queueDir and the closure of store paths specified by the {option}program option.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.command
documents.content: A program name specifying a Postfix service/daemon process. By default it's the attribute {option}name.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.maxproc
documents.content: The maximum number of processes to spawn for this service. If the value is 0 it doesn't have any limit. If null is given it uses the postfix default of 100.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.name
documents.content: The name of the service to run. Defaults to the attribute set key.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.private
documents.content: Whether the service's sockets and storage directory is restricted to be only available via the mail system. If null is given it uses the postfix default true.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.type
documents.content: The type of the service

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.wakeup
documents.content: Automatically wake up the service after the specified number of seconds. If 0 is given, never wake the service up.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.wakeupUnusedComponent
documents.content: If set to false the component will only be woken up if it is used. This is equivalent to postfix' notion of adding a question mark behind the wakeup time in {file}master.cf

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.submissionOptions
documents.content: Options for the submission config in master.cf

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.submissionsOptions
documents.content:
Options for the submission config via smtps in master.cf.
smtpd_tls_security_level will be set to encrypt, if it is missing or has one of the values "may" or "none".
smtpd_tls_wrappermode with value "yes" will be added automatically.

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.transport
documents.content: Entries for the transport map, cf. man-page {manpage}transport(5).

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.user
documents.content: What to call the Postfix user (must be used only for postfix).

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.virtual
documents.content: Entries for the virtual alias map, cf. man-page {manpage}virtual(5).

documents.title: Option: services.postfix.virtualMapType
documents.content: What type of virtual alias map file to use. Use "regexp" for regular expressions.

documents.title: Option: services.postgres-websockets.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable postgres-websockets.

documents.title: Option: services.postgres-websockets.environment
documents.content:
postgres-websockets configuration as defined in: https://github.com/diogob/postgres-websockets/blob/master/src/PostgresWebsockets/Config.hs#L71-L87
PGWS_DB_URI is represented as an attribute set, see environment.PGWS_DB_URI
::: {.note} The environment.PGWS_JWT_SECRET option is blocked. Use jwtSecretFile instead. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postgres-websockets.environment.PGWS_DB_URI
documents.content:
libpq connection parameters as documented in:
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-connect.html#LIBPQ-PARAMKEYWORDS
::: {.note} The environment.PGWS_DB_URI.password and environment.PGWS_DB_URI.passfile options are blocked. Use pgpassFile instead. :::

documents.title: Option: services.postgres-websockets.environment.PGWS_HOST
documents.content: Address the server will listen for websocket connections.

documents.title: Option: services.postgres-websockets.jwtSecretFile
documents.content: Secret used to sign JWT tokens used to open communications channels.

documents.title: Option: services.postgres-websockets.pgpassFile
documents.content:
The password to authenticate to PostgreSQL with. Not needed for peer or trust based authentication.
The file must be a valid .pgpass file as described in: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-pgpass.html
In most cases, the following will be enough:

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.authentication
documents.content: Defines how users authenticate themselves to the server. See the PostgreSQL documentation for pg_hba.conf for details on the expected format of this option. By default, peer based authentication will be used for users connecting via the Unix socket, and md5 password authentication will be used for users connecting via TCP. Any added rules will be inserted above the default rules. If you'd like to replace the default rules entirely, you can use lib.mkForce in your module.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.checkConfig
documents.content: Check the syntax of the configuration file at compile time

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.dataDir
documents.content: The data directory for PostgreSQL. If left as the default value this directory will automatically be created before the PostgreSQL server starts, otherwise the sysadmin is responsible for ensuring the directory exists with appropriate ownership and permissions.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable PostgreSQL Server.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.enableJIT
documents.content: Whether to enable JIT support.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.enableTCPIP
documents.content: Whether PostgreSQL should listen on all network interfaces. If disabled, the database can only be accessed via its Unix domain socket or via TCP connections to localhost.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.ensureDatabases
documents.content: Ensures that the specified databases exist. This option will never delete existing databases, especially not when the value of this option is changed. This means that databases created once through this option or otherwise have to be removed manually.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.ensureUsers
documents.content: Ensures that the specified users exist. The PostgreSQL users will be identified using peer authentication. This authenticates the Unix user with the same name only, and that without the need for a password. This option will never delete existing users or remove DB ownership of databases once granted with ensureDBOwnership = true;. This means that this must be cleaned up manually when changing after changing the config in here.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.systemCallFilter
documents.content:
Configures the syscall filter for postgresql.service. The keys are declarations for SystemCallFilter as described in {manpage}systemd.exec(5).
The value is a boolean: true adds the attribute name to the syscall filter-set, false doesn't. This is done to allow downstream configurations to turn off restrictions made here. E.g. with
it's possible to remove the restriction on @resources (keep in mind that @system-service implies @resources).
As described in the section for , the ordering matters. Hence, it's also possible to specify customizations with
is the flag whether or not it will be added to the SystemCallFilter of postgresql.service.
Settings with a higher priority are added after filter settings with a lower priority. Hence, syscall groups with a higher priority can discard declarations with a lower priority.
By default, syscall groups (i.e. attribute names starting with @) are added before negated groups (i.e. ~@ as prefix) before syscall names and negations.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.systemCallFilter.<name>.enable
documents.content: Whether to enable ‹name› in postgresql's syscall filter.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresql.systemCallFilter.<name>.priority
documents.content:
Set the priority of the system call filter setting. Later declarations override earlier ones, e.g.
results in a service where only read is not allowed.
The ordering in the unit file is controlled by this option: the higher the number, the later it will be added to the filterset.
By default, depending on the prefix a priority is assigned: usually, call-groups (starting with @) are used to allow/deny a larger set of syscalls and later on single syscalls are configured for exceptions. Hence, syscall groups and negative groups are placed before individual syscalls by default.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.connection
documents.content:
Specifies parameters used to connect to the server, as a connection string. See Section 34.1.1 of the PostgreSQL manual for more information.
Because {command}pg_receivewal doesn't connect to any particular database in the cluster, database name in the connection string will be ignored.

documents.content: Directory to write the output to.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.environment
documents.content: Environment variables passed to the service. Usable parameters are listed in Section 34.14 of the PostgreSQL manual.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.extraArgs
documents.content: A list of extra arguments to pass to the {command}pg_receivewal command.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.postgresqlPackage
documents.content: The postgresql package to use.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.slot
documents.content:
Require {command}pg_receivewal to use an existing replication slot (see Section 26.2.6 of the PostgreSQL manual). When this option is used, {command}pg_receivewal will report a flush position to the server, indicating when each segment has been synchronized to disk so that the server can remove that segment if it is not otherwise needed.
When the replication client of {command}pg_receivewal is configured on the server as a synchronous standby, then using a replication slot will report the flush position to the server, but only when a WAL file is closed. Therefore, that configuration will cause transactions on the primary to wait for a long time and effectively not work satisfactorily. The option {option}synchronous must be specified in addition to make this work correctly.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.statusInterval
documents.content: Specifies the number of seconds between status packets sent back to the server. This allows for easier monitoring of the progress from server. A value of zero disables the periodic status updates completely, although an update will still be sent when requested by the server, to avoid timeout disconnect.

documents.title: Option: services.postgresqlWalReceiver.receivers.<name>.synchronous
documents.content:
Flush the WAL data to disk immediately after it has been received. Also send a status packet back to the server immediately after flushing, regardless of {option}statusInterval.
This option should be specified if the replication client of {command}pg_receivewal is configured on the server as a synchronous standby, to ensure that timely feedback is sent to the server.

documents.title: Option: services.privoxy.certsLifetime
documents.content:
If inspectHttps is enabled, the time generated HTTPS certificates will be stored in a temporary directory for reuse. Once the lifetime has expired the directory will cleared and the certificate will have to be generated again, on-demand.
Depending on the traffic, you may want to reduce the lifetime to limit the disk usage, since Privoxy itself never deletes the certificates.
::: {.note} The format is that of the {manpage}tmpfiles.d(5) Age parameter. :::

documents.content: Whether to configure Privoxy to use Tor's faster SOCKS port, suitable for HTTP.

documents.title: Option: services.privoxy.inspectHttps
documents.content:
Whether to configure Privoxy to inspect HTTPS requests, meaning all encrypted traffic will be filtered as well. This works by decrypting and re-encrypting the requests using a per-domain generated certificate.
To issue per-domain certificates, Privoxy must be provided with a CA certificate, using the ca-cert-file, ca-key-file settings.
::: {.warning} The CA certificate must also be added to the system trust roots, otherwise browsers will reject all Privoxy certificates as invalid. You can do so by using the option {option}security.pki.certificateFiles. :::

documents.title: Option: services.prometheus.scrapeConfigs.*.honor_labels
documents.content:
Controls how Prometheus handles conflicts between labels that are already present in scraped data and labels that Prometheus would attach server-side ("job" and "instance" labels, manually configured target labels, and labels generated by service discovery implementations).
If honor_labels is set to "true", label conflicts are resolved by keeping label values from the scraped data and ignoring the conflicting server-side labels.
If honor_labels is set to "false", label conflicts are resolved by renaming conflicting labels in the scraped data to "exported_<original-label>" (for example "exported_instance", "exported_job") and then attaching server-side labels. This is useful for use cases such as federation, where all labels specified in the target should be preserved.
Defaults to false in prometheus when set to null.

documents.title: Option: services.prometheus.scrapeConfigs.*.honor_timestamps
documents.content:
honor_timestamps controls whether Prometheus respects the timestamps present in scraped data.
If honor_timestamps is set to true, the timestamps of the metrics exposed by the target will be used.
If honor_timestamps is set to false, the timestamps of the metrics exposed by the target will be ignored.
Defaults to true in prometheus when set to null.

documents.title: Option: services.prometheus.scrapeConfigs.*.kubernetes_sd_configs.*.selectors
documents.content:
Optional label and field selectors to limit the discovery process to a subset of available resources. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/ and https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/ to learn more about the possible filters that can be used. Endpoints role supports pod, service and endpoints selectors, other roles only support selectors matching the role itself (e.g. node role can only contain node selectors).
Note: When making decision about using field/label selector make sure that this is the best approach - it will prevent Prometheus from reusing single list/watch for all scrape configs. This might result in a bigger load on the Kubernetes API, because per each selector combination there will be additional LIST/WATCH. On the other hand, if you just want to monitor small subset of pods in large cluster it's recommended to use selectors. Decision, if selectors should be used or not depends on the particular situation.

documents.content:
Whether to enable PufferPanel game management server.
Note that PufferPanel templates and binaries downloaded by PufferPanel expect FHS environment. It is possible to set {option}package option to use PufferPanel wrapper with FHS environment. For example, to use Download Game from Steam and Download Java template operations:

documents.title: Option: services.pufferpanel.environment
documents.content:
Environment variables to set for the service. Secrets should be specified using {option}environmentFile.
Refer to the PufferPanel source code for the list of available configuration options. Variable name is an upper-cased configuration entry name with underscores instead of dots, prefixed with PUFFER_. For example, panel.settings.companyName entry can be set using {env}PUFFER_PANEL_SETTINGS_COMPANYNAME.
When running with panel enabled (configured with PUFFER_PANEL_ENABLE environment variable), it is recommended disable registration using PUFFER_PANEL_REGISTRATIONENABLED environment variable (registration is enabled by default). To create the initial administrator user, run {command}pufferpanel --workDir /var/lib/pufferpanel user add --admin.
Some options override corresponding settings set via web interface (e.g. PUFFER_PANEL_REGISTRATIONENABLED). Those options can be temporarily toggled or set in settings but do not persist between restarts.

documents.title: Option: services.rabbitmq.config
documents.content:
Verbatim advanced configuration file contents using the Erlang syntax. This is also known as the {file}advanced.config file or the old config format.
configItems is preferred whenever possible. However, nested data structures can only be expressed properly using the config option.
The contents of this option will be merged into the configItems by RabbitMQ at runtime to form the final configuration.
See the second table on https://www.rabbitmq.com/configure.html#config-items For the distinct formats, see https://www.rabbitmq.com/configure.html#config-file-formats

documents.title: Option: services.rabbitmq.configItems
documents.content:
Configuration options in RabbitMQ's new config file format, which is a simple key-value format that can not express nested data structures. This is known as the {file}rabbitmq.conf file, although outside NixOS that filename may have Erlang syntax, particularly prior to RabbitMQ 3.7.0.
If you do need to express nested data structures, you can use config option. Configuration from config will be merged into these options by RabbitMQ at runtime to form the final configuration.
See https://www.rabbitmq.com/configure.html#config-items For the distinct formats, see https://www.rabbitmq.com/configure.html#config-file-formats

documents.content:

Together with 'port' setting it's mostly an alias for configItems."listeners.tcp.1" and it's left for backwards compatibility with previous version of this module.

documents.title: Option: services.radicle.httpd.nginx
documents.content: With this option, you can customize an nginx virtual host which already has sensible defaults for radicle-httpd. Set to {} if you do not need any customization to the virtual host. If enabled, then by default, the {option}serverName is radicle-${config.networking.hostName}.${config.networking.domain}, TLS is active, and certificates are acquired via ACME. Read more at https://quic.nginx.org/ HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.
